1.2.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ sanatkumārastu nāradāya mahātmane /
proktavānsakalāndharmānkathaṃ tau militāvubhau //
1.2.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
कथं सनत्कुमारस्तु नारदाय महात्मने ।
प्रोक्तवान्सकलान्धर्मान्कथं तौ मिलितावुभौ ॥
1.2.m: The sages said: / How did Sanatkumāra declare all the dharmas to the noble Nārada? / How did the two of them meet?

1.2.s:
kasminsthāne sthitau sūta tāvubhau brahmavādinau /
harigītasamudgāne cakratustadvadasva naḥ //
1.2.d:
कस्मिन्स्थाने स्थितौ सूत तावुभौ ब्रह्मवादिनौ ।
हरिगीतसमुद्गाने चक्रतुस्तद्वदस्व नः ॥
1.2.m: In what place were both those expounders of Brahman stationed, O Sūta, / when they engaged in singing together the songs of Hari? Tell us that!

1.2.s:
sūta uvāca
sanakādyā mahātmāno brahmaṇo mānasāḥ sutāḥ /
nirmamā nirahaṃkārāḥ sarve te hyūdhvaretasaḥ //
1.2.d:
सूत उवाच
सनकाद्या महात्मानो ब्रह्मणो मानसाः सुताः ।
निर्ममा निरहंकाराः सर्वे ते ह्यूध्वरेतसः ॥
1.2.m: Sūta said: / Sanaka and the others are noble mind-born sons of Brahmā, / free from possessiveness, free from egoism, and all of them chaste.

1.2.s:
teṣāṃ nāmāni vakṣyāmi samakaśca sanandanaḥ /
sanasphumāraśca vibhuḥ sanātama iti smṛtaḥ //
viṣṇubhaktā mahātmāno brahmadhyānaparāyaṇāḥ /
sahasrasūryasaṃkāśāḥ satyasandhā mumukṣavaḥ //
1.2.d:
तेषां नामानि वक्ष्यामि समकश्च सनन्दनः ।
सनस्फुमारश्च विभुः सनातम इति स्मृतः ॥
विष्णुभक्ता महात्मानो ब्रह्मध्यानपरायणाः ।
सहस्रसूर्यसंकाशाः सत्यसन्धा मुमुक्षवः ॥
1.2.m:
I shall state their names: Sanaka and Sanandana, / the pervasive Sanatkumāra, and he who is known as Sanātana.

Devotees of Viṣṇu, noble, devoted to meditation on Brahman, / resplendent like a thousand suns, true to their promises, seekers of liberation,

1.2.s:
ekadā meruśṛṅgaṃ te prasthitā brahmaṇaḥ sabhām /
iṣṭaṃ mārge 'tha dadṛśuḥ gaṅgāṃ viṣṇipadīṃ dvijāḥ //
1.2.d:
एकदा मेरुशृङ्गं ते प्रस्थिता ब्रह्मणः सभाम् ।
इष्टं मार्गे ऽथ ददृशुः गङ्गां विष्णिपदीं द्विजाः ॥
1.2.m: once departed for the peak of Meru, to the assembly of Brahmā; / then on the way the twice-born saw the beloved Gaṅgā, who flows from the feet of Viṣṇu.

1.2.s:
tāṃ nirīkṣya samudyuktāḥ strātuṃ sītājale 'bhavan /
etasminnantare tatra devarṣirnārado muniḥ //
1.2.d:
तां निरीक्ष्य समुद्युक्ताः स्त्रातुं सीताजले ऽभवन् ।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र देवर्षिर्नारदो मुनिः ॥
1.2.m: Beholding her, they prepared to bathe in the cool water. / In the meantime, the divine seer, the sage Nārada, arrived there,

1.2.s:
ājagāma dvijaśreṣṭhā dṛṣṭvā bhrāntṝnsvakāgrajān /
tāndṛṣṭvā strātumudyuktānnamaskṛtya kṛtāñjitiḥ //
1.2.d:
आजगाम द्विजश्रेष्ठा दृष्ट्वा भ्रान्तॄन्स्वकाग्रजान् ।
तान्दृष्ट्वा स्त्रातुमुद्युक्तान्नमस्कृत्य कृताञ्जितिः ॥
1.2.m: O best of the twice-born, having seen his wandering elder brothers. / Seeing them prepared to bathe, he bowed with folded hands,

1.2.s:
guṇannāmāni sapremabhaktiyukto madhudviṣaḥ /
nārāyaṇācyutānanta vāsudeva janārdana //
1.2.d:
गुणन्नामानि सप्रेमभक्तियुक्तो मधुद्विषः ।
नारायणाच्युतानन्त वासुदेव जनार्दन ॥
1.2.m: uttering the names of the enemy of Madhu with loving devotion: / 'O Nārāyaṇa, O Acyuta, O Ananta, O Vāsudeva, O Janārdana,

1.2.s:
yajñeśa yajñapuruṣa kṛṣṇa viṣṇo namo 'stu te /
padmākṣa kamalākānta gaṅgājanaka keśava /
kṣirodaśāyindeveśa dāmodara namo 'stu te //
1.2.d:
यज्ञेश यज्ञपुरुष कृष्ण विष्णो नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
पद्माक्ष कमलाकान्त गङ्गाजनक केशव ।
क्षिरोदशायिन्देवेश दामोदर नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.2.m: O Lord of sacrifice, O Person of sacrifice, O Kṛṣṇa, O Viṣṇu, homage be to you! / O lotus-eyed one, O beloved of Kamalā, O father of Gaṅgā, O Keśava, / O you who recline on the milk-ocean, O lord of gods, O Dāmodara, homage be to you!

1.2.s:
śrīrāma viṣṇo narasiṃha vāmana pradyumnasaṃkarpaṇa vātpadeva /
ajāniruddhāmalaruṅmurāraṃ tvaṃ pāhi naḥ sarvabhayādajastram //
1.2.d:
श्रीराम विष्णो नरसिंह वामन प्रद्युम्नसंकर्पण वात्पदेव ।
अजानिरुद्धामलरुङ्मुरारं त्वं पाहि नः सर्वभयादजस्त्रम् ॥
1.2.m: O Śrīrāma, O Viṣṇu, O Narasiṃha, O Vāmana, O Pradyumna, O Saṃkarṣaṇa, O Vāsudeva, / O unborn one, O Aniruddha, O flawless splendour, O enemy of Mura, protect us perpetually from all danger!'

1.2.s:
ityucca ranharernāma natvā tānsvāgrajānmunīn /
upāsīnaśca taiḥ sārddhaṃ sasnau prītisamanvitaḥ //
1.2.d:
इत्युच्च रन्हरेर्नाम नत्वा तान्स्वाग्रजान्मुनीन् ।
उपासीनश्च तैः सार्द्धं सस्नौ प्रीतिसमन्वितः ॥
1.2.m: Thus uttering the names of Hari, bowing to those sages, his elder brothers, / and sitting near them, he bathed together with them, filled with joy.

1.2.s:
te ṣāṃ cāpi tu sītāyā jale lokamalāpa he /
strātvā saṃtartya devarṣipitanvigatakalmaṣāḥ //
1.2.d:
ते षां चापि तु सीताया जले लोकमलाप हे ।
स्त्रात्वा संतर्त्य देवर्षिपितन्विगतकल्मषाः ॥
1.2.m: And having bathed in the cool water that removes the impurity of the worlds, / and satisfied the gods, seers, and ancestors, free from all sin,

1.2.s:
uttīryya saṃdhyopāstyādi kṛtvācāraṃ svakaṃ dvijāḥ /
kathāṃ pracakrurvividhāḥ nārāyaṇa guṇāśritāḥ //
1.2.d:
उत्तीर्य्य संध्योपास्त्यादि कृत्वाचारं स्वकं द्विजाः ।
कथां प्रचक्रुर्विविधाः नारायण गुणाश्रिताः ॥
1.2.m: coming out of the water and performing their customary practices, such as the morning and evening worship, O twice-born, / they held diverse discussions centred on the qualities of Nārāyaṇa.

1.2.s:
kṛtatriyeṣu muniṣu gaṅgātīre manorame /
cakāranāradaḥ praśnaṃ nānākhyānakayāntare //
1.2.d:
कृतत्रियेषु मुनिषु गङ्गातीरे मनोरमे ।
चकारनारदः प्रश्नं नानाख्यानकयान्तरे ॥
1.2.m: When the sages had completed their rites on the delightful bank of the Gaṅgā, / Nārada asked a question amidst various narratives.

1.2.s:
nārada uvāca
sarvajñāḥ stha muniśreṣṭhāḥ bhagavadbhaktitatparāḥ /
yūyaṃ sarve jagannāthā bhagavantaḥ sanātanāḥ //
1.2.d:
नारद उवाच
सर्वज्ञाः स्थ मुनिश्रेष्ठाः भगवद्भक्तितत्पराः ।
यूयं सर्वे जगन्नाथा भगवन्तः सनातनाः ॥
1.2.m: Nārada said: / You are omniscient, O best among sages, intent on devotion to the Blessed One; / you are all eternal lords, venerable masters of the universe.

1.2.s:
lokoddhāraparānyuṣmāndīneṣu kṛtasauhṛdān /
pṛcche tato vadata me bhagavallakṣaṇaṃ budhāḥ //
1.2.d:
लोकोद्धारपरान्युष्मान्दीनेषु कृतसौहृदान् ।
पृच्छे ततो वदत मे भगवल्लक्षणं बुधाः ॥
1.2.m: To you who are devoted to delivering the world and show benevolence to the destitute, / I put a question; therefore, O wise ones, tell me the characteristic of the Blessed One,

1.2.s:
yenedamakhilaṃ jātaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
gaṅgāpādodakaṃ yasya sa kathaṃ jñāyate hariḥ //
kathaṃ ca trividhaṃ karma saphalaṃ jāyate nṛṇām //
1.2.d:
येनेदमखिलं जातं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
गङ्गापादोदकं यस्य स कथं ज्ञायते हरिः ॥
कथं च त्रिविधं कर्म सफलं जायते नृणाम् ॥
1.2.m:
by whom this entire universe of the unmoving and the moving was brought forth, / whose foot-water is the Gaṅgā—how is that Hari to be known?

And how does the threefold action of men become fruitful?

1.2.s:
jñānasya lakṣaṇa brūta tapasaścāpi mānadāḥ //
atitheḥ pūjanaṃ vāpi yena viṣṇuḥ prasīdati /
evamādīni guhyāni harituṣṭikarāṇi ca /
anugṛhya ca māṃ nāthāstattvato vaktumarhatha //
1.2.d:
ज्ञानस्य लक्षण ब्रूत तपसश्चापि मानदाः ॥
अतिथेः पूजनं वापि येन विष्णुः प्रसीदति ।
एवमादीनि गुह्यानि हरितुष्टिकराणि च ।
अनुगृह्य च मां नाथास्तत्त्वतो वक्तुमर्हथ ॥
1.2.m:
Tell me also the characteristic of knowledge and of asceticism, O bestow-ers of honor!

Or the worship of a guest, through which Viṣṇu is pleased— / these and other secrets that bring satisfaction to Hari, / deign to tell me truly, O lords, showing favour to me.

1.2.s:
śaunaka uvāca
namaḥ parāya devāya parasmātparamātra ca /
parāvara nivāsāya saguṇāyāguṇāya ca //
1.2.d:
शौनक उवाच
नमः पराय देवाय परस्मात्परमात्र च ।
परावर निवासाय सगुणायागुणाय च ॥
1.2.m: Śaunaka said: / Homage to the supreme god, who is higher than the highest, / residing in the higher and the lower, both with attributes and without attributes,

1.2.s:
amāyāyātmasaṃjñāya mācine viśvarupiṇe /
yogīśvarāya yogāya yogagamyāya viṣṇave //
1.2.d:
अमायायात्मसंज्ञाय माचिने विश्वरुपिणे ।
योगीश्वराय योगाय योगगम्याय विष्णवे ॥
1.2.m: free from māyā, known as the Self, the creator of māyā, whose form is the universe, / to the Lord of yoga, to yoga, to Viṣṇu who is accessible through yoga;

1.2.s:
jñānāya jñānagamyāya sarvajñānaikahetave /
jñāceśvarāya jñeyāya jñātre vijñānasaṃpade //
1.2.d:
ज्ञानाय ज्ञानगम्याय सर्वज्ञानैकहेतवे ।
ज्ञाचेश्वराय ज्ञेयाय ज्ञात्रे विज्ञानसंपदे ॥
1.2.m: to knowledge, to him who is reachable through knowledge, the sole cause of all knowledge, / to the Lord of knowledge, to the object of knowledge, to the knower, the wealth of wisdom;

1.2.s:
dhyānāya dhyānagamyāya dhyātṛpātaharāya ca /
dhyāneśvarāya sudhiyedhyeyadhyātṛsvarupiṇe //
1.2.d:
ध्यानाय ध्यानगम्याय ध्यातृपातहराय च ।
ध्यानेश्वराय सुधियेध्येयध्यातृस्वरुपिणे ॥
1.2.m: to meditation, to him who is reachable through meditation, who removes the sins of the meditator, / to the Lord of meditation, whose nature is the object of meditation and the meditator for the wise!

1.2.s:
ādityavacandrāgnividhātṛdevāḥ siddhāśca yakṣāsuranāgasaṅghāḥ /
yacchaktiyuktāstamajaṃ purāṇaṃ satyaṃ stutīśaṃ satataṃ nato 'smi //
1.2.d:
आदित्यवचन्द्राग्निविधातृदेवाः सिद्धाश्च यक्षासुरनागसङ्घाः ।
यच्छक्तियुक्तास्तमजं पुराणं सत्यं स्तुतीशं सततं नतो ऽस्मि ॥
1.2.m: The gods beginning with the sun, the moon, fire, and the Creator, and the hosts of Siddhas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and Nāgas, / are endowed with his power—to that unborn, ancient, true Lord of praise I constantly bow.

1.2.s:
yo brahmarupī jagatāṃ vidhātā sa eva pātā dvijaviṣṇurupī /
kalpāntarudrākhyatamuḥ sa devaḥ śeteṃ'ghripānastamajaṃ bhajāmi //
1.2.d:
यो ब्रह्मरुपी जगतां विधाता स एव पाता द्विजविष्णुरुपी ।
कल्पान्तरुद्राख्यतमुः स देवः शेतेंऽघ्रिपानस्तमजं भजामि ॥
1.2.m: He who in the form of Brahmā is the creator of the worlds, is himself the protector in the form of Viṣṇu, O twice-born; / at the end of the aeon he assumes the form of Rudra; as that god who drinks with his foot reclines, I worship that unborn one.

1.2.s:
yannāmasaṃkīrttanato gajendro grāhograbandhānmumuce sa devaḥ /
virājamānaḥ svapade parākhye taṃ viṣṇumādyaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
1.2.d:
यन्नामसंकीर्त्तनतो गजेन्द्रो ग्राहोग्रबन्धान्मुमुचे स देवः ।
विराजमानः स्वपदे पराख्ये तं विष्णुमाद्यं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
1.2.m: By the praise of whose name the elephant-king Gajendra was released from the ferocious grip of the crocodile, that god / shining in his own abode called the supreme—in that primeval Viṣṇu I take refuge.

1.2.s:
śivasvarupī śivabhakti bhājāṃ yo viṣṇurupī haribhāvitānām /
saṃkalpapūrvātmakadehahetustaṃstameva nityaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
1.2.d:
शिवस्वरुपी शिवभक्ति भाजां यो विष्णुरुपी हरिभावितानाम् ।
संकल्पपूर्वात्मकदेहहेतुस्तंस्तमेव नित्यं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
1.2.m: He who takes the form of Śiva for those possessing devotion to Śiva, and the form of Viṣṇu for those meditating on Hari, / who is the cause of bodies assuming form by his mere resolve—in him alone do I constantly take refuge.

1.2.s:
yaḥ keśihantā narakāntakaśca bālo bhujāgreṇa dadhāra gotram /
devaṃ ca bhūmāravinodaśīlaṃ taṃ vāsudevaṃ satataṃ nato 'smi //
1.2.d:
यः केशिहन्ता नरकान्तकश्च बालो भुजाग्रेण दधार गोत्रम् ।
देवं च भूमारविनोदशीलं तं वासुदेवं सततं नतो ऽस्मि ॥
1.2.m: He who slew Keśin and killed Naraka, and as a boy lifted the mountain with the tip of his arm, / the god whose nature is playfulness in the world—to that Vāsudeva I constantly bow.

1.2.s:
lebhe 'vatīryogranṛsiṃharupīyodaityavakṣaḥ kaṭhinaṃ śilāvat /
vidāryasaṃrākṣitavānsvabhaktaṃ prahlādamīśaṃ tamajaṃ manāmi //
1.2.d:
लेभे ऽवतीर्योग्रनृसिंहरुपीयोदैत्यवक्षः कठिनं शिलावत् ।
विदार्यसंराक्षितवान्स्वभक्तं प्रह्लादमीशं तमजं मनामि ॥
1.2.m: Descending in the form of the fierce Nṛsiṃha, he tore open the chest of the demon, / hard as a stone, and protected his devotee Prahlāda—to that unborn Lord I bow.

1.2.s:
vyomādibhirmūṣitamātmasaṃjñaṃ nirañjanaṃ nityamameyatattvam /
jagadvidhātāramakarmakaṃ ca paraṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣama nato 'smi //
1.2.d:
व्योमादिभिर्मूषितमात्मसंज्ञं निरञ्जनं नित्यममेयतत्त्वम् ।
जगद्विधातारमकर्मकं च परं पुराणं पुरुषम नतो ऽस्मि ॥
1.2.m: Adorned with space and the rest, designated as the Self, immaculate, eternal, whose reality is immeasurable, / the creator of the universe, inactive, the supreme, ancient Person—to him I bow.

1.2.s:
brahmendrarudrānilavāyumartyagandharvayakṣāsuradevasaṃghaiḥ /
svamūrtibhedaiḥ sthita eka īśastamādimātmā namahaṃ bhajāmi //
1.2.d:
ब्रह्मेन्द्ररुद्रानिलवायुमर्त्यगन्धर्वयक्षासुरदेवसंघैः ।
स्वमूर्तिभेदैः स्थित एक ईशस्तमादिमात्मा नमहं भजामि ॥
1.2.m: Brahmā, Indra, Rudra, the wind-gods, mortals, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and hosts of deities / are the diverse forms through which he alone stands as the one Lord—that primeval Self I worship.

1.2.s:
yato bhinnamidaṃ sarvaṃ samudbhūtaṃ sthitaṃ ca vai /
yasminneṣyati paścācca tamasti śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
1.2.d:
यतो भिन्नमिदं सर्वं समुद्भूतं स्थितं च वै ।
यस्मिन्नेष्यति पश्चाच्च तमस्ति शरणं गतः ॥
1.2.m: From whom this whole diversified [universe] has arisen and in whom it is sustained, / and into whom it will ultimately go—to him I have gone for refuge.

1.2.s:
yaḥ sthito viśvarupeṇa saṅgīvātra pratīyate /
asaṅgī paripūrṇaśca tamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
1.2.d:
यः स्थितो विश्वरुपेण सङ्गीवात्र प्रतीयते ।
असङ्गी परिपूर्णश्च तमस्मि शरणं गतः ॥
1.2.m: He who, existing in the form of the universe, appears here as if attached, / yet is unattached and completely full—to him I have gone for refuge.

1.2.s:
hṛdi sthito 'pi yo devo māyayā mohitātmanām /
na jñāyate paraḥ śuddhastamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
1.2.d:
हृदि स्थितो ऽपि यो देवो मायया मोहितात्मनाम् ।
न ज्ञायते परः शुद्धस्तमस्मि शरणं गतः ॥
1.2.m: Even though dwelling in the heart, he who is supreme and pure is not known / by those whose minds are deluded by māyā—to him I have gone for refuge.

1.2.s:
sarvasaṃganivṛttānāṃ dhyānayogaratātmanām /
sarvatra bhāti jñānātmā tamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
1.2.d:
सर्वसंगनिवृत्तानां ध्यानयोगरतात्मनाम् ।
सर्वत्र भाति ज्ञानात्मा तमस्मि शरणं गतः ॥
1.2.m: To those who have ceased from all attachment and whose minds delight in the yoga of meditation, / he shines everywhere as the embodiment of knowledge—to him I have gone for refuge.

1.2.s:
dadhāra mandāraṃ pṛṣṭe nirode 'mṛtamanthane /
devatānāṃ hitārthāya taṃ kūrmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
1.2.d:
दधार मन्दारं पृष्टे निरोदे ऽमृतमन्थने ।
देवतानां हितार्थाय तं कूर्मं शरणं गतः ॥
1.2.m: He who held the Mandara mountain on his back in the ocean during the churning for nectar, / for the benefit of the gods—in that Kūrma I take refuge.

1.2.s:
draṣṭrāṅkureṇa yo 'nantaḥ samuddhṛtyārṇavāddharām /
tasthāvidaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ vārāhaṃ taṃ nato 'smyaham //
1.2.d:
द्रष्ट्राङ्कुरेण यो ऽनन्तः समुद्धृत्यार्णवाद्धराम् ।
तस्थाविदं जगत्कृत्स्नं वाराहं तं नतो ऽस्म्यहम् ॥
1.2.m: He who, the infinite one, lifted up the earth from the ocean with the tip of his tusk, / and restored this entire universe—to that Varāha I bow.

1.2.s:
prahlādaṃ gopayandaityaṃ śilātikaṭhinorasam /
vidārya hatavānyo hi taṃ nṛsiṃhaṃ nato 'smyaham //
1.2.d:
प्रह्लादं गोपयन्दैत्यं शिलातिकठिनोरसम् ।
विदार्य हतवान्यो हि तं नृसिंहं नतो ऽस्म्यहम् ॥
1.2.m: Protecting Prahlāda, he tore open and slew the demon / whose chest was excessively hard like stone—to that Nṛsiṃha I bow.

1.2.s:
labdhvā vairocanerbhūmiṃ dvābhyāṃ padbhyāmatītya yaḥ /
ābrahmabhuvanaṃ pādātsurebhyastaṃ nato 'jitam //
1.2.d:
लब्ध्वा वैरोचनेर्भूमिं द्वाभ्यां पद्भ्यामतीत्य यः ।
आब्रह्मभुवनं पादात्सुरेभ्यस्तं नतो ऽजितम् ॥
1.2.m: Having obtained the earth from the son of Virocana, he traversed it with two feet, / granting it up to the world of Brahmā from his foot to the gods—to that unconquered one I bow.

1.2.s:
haihayasyāparādhena hyekaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā /
kṣatriyānvayabhettā yo jāmadagnyaṃ nato 'smi tam //
1.2.d:
हैहयस्यापराधेन ह्येकविंशतिसंख्यया ।
क्षत्रियान्वयभेत्ता यो जामदग्न्यं नतो ऽस्मि तम् ॥
1.2.m: He who, because of the transgression of the Haihaya, destroyed the lineage of the Kṣatriyas / twenty-one times—to that Jāmadagnya I bow.

1.2.s:
āvirbhūtaścaturddhā yaḥ kapibhiḥ parivāritaḥ /
hatavānrākṣasānīkaṃ rāmacandraṃ nato 'smyaham //
1.2.d:
आविर्भूतश्चतुर्द्धा यः कपिभिः परिवारितः ।
हतवान्राक्षसानीकं रामचन्द्रं नतो ऽस्म्यहम् ॥
1.2.m: He who manifested in four forms, surrounded by monkeys, / and destroyed the army of the Rākṣasas—to that Rāmacandra I bow.

1.2.s:
mūrtidvayaṃ samāśritya bhūbhāramapahṛtya ca /
saṃjahāra kulaṃ svaṃ yastaṃ śrīkṛṣṇapyahaṃ bhaje //
1.2.d:
मूर्तिद्वयं समाश्रित्य भूभारमपहृत्य च ।
संजहार कुलं स्वं यस्तं श्रीकृष्णप्यहं भजे ॥
1.2.m: Assuming a pair of forms, removing the burden of the earth, / and bringing about the end of his own family—that Śrīkṛṣṇa do I worship.

1.2.s:
bhūmyādilokatritayaṃ saṃtṛtpātmānamātmani /
paśyanti nirmalaṃ śuddhaṃ tamīśānaṃ bhajāmyaham //
1.2.d:
भूम्यादिलोकत्रितयं संतृत्पात्मानमात्मनि ।
पश्यन्ति निर्मलं शुद्धं तमीशानं भजाम्यहम् ॥
1.2.m: In whom the three worlds beginning with the earth [subsist], who is satisfied within Himself, whom they see in the self as stainless and pure—that sovereign Lord I worship.

1.2.s:
yugānte pāpino śuddhānbhittvā tīkṣṇasudhārayā /
sthāpayāmāsa yo dharmaṃ kṛtādau tannamāmyaham //
1.2.d:
युगान्ते पापिनो शुद्धान्भित्त्वा तीक्ष्णसुधारया ।
स्थापयामास यो धर्मं कृतादौ तन्नमाम्यहम् ॥
1.2.m: Who, at the end of the yuga, having split the impious sinners with a sharp-edged blade, established dharma at the start of Kṛta [yuga]—to Him I bow.

1.2.s:
evamādīnyanekāni yasya rupāṇi pāṇḍavāḥ /
na śakyaṃ tena saṃkhyātuṃ koṭyabdairapi taṃ bhaje //
1.2.d:
एवमादीन्यनेकानि यस्य रुपाणि पाण्डवाः ।
न शक्यं तेन संख्यातुं कोट्यब्दैरपि तं भजे ॥
1.2.m: O Pāṇḍavas, manifold forms such as these are His; it is impossible to count them even in ten million years—Him I worship.

1.2.s:
mahimānaṃ tu yannāmnaḥ paraṃ gantuṃ munīśvarāḥ /
devāsurāśca manavaḥ kathaṃ taṃ śrullako bhaje //
1.2.d:
महिमानं तु यन्नाम्नः परं गन्तुं मुनीश्वराः ।
देवासुराश्च मनवः कथं तं श्रुल्लको भजे ॥
1.2.m: Even lordly sages, gods, asuras, and Manus cannot reach the limit of the greatness of His name; how then may a wretched one like me worship Him?

1.2.s:
yannāmaśravaṇenāpi mahāpātakino narāḥ /
pavitratāṃ prapadyante ta kathaṃ staumi cālpadhīḥ //
1.2.d:
यन्नामश्रवणेनापि महापातकिनो नराः ।
पवित्रतां प्रपद्यन्ते त कथं स्तौमि चाल्पधीः ॥
1.2.m: By even the hearing of whose name men guilty of the great sins attain purity—how then may I, dull of intellect, praise Him?

1.2.s:
yathākathañcidyannamni kīrtite vā śrute 'pi vā /
pāpinastu viśuddhāḥ syuḥ śaddhā mokṣamavānpuyuḥ //
1.2.d:
यथाकथञ्चिद्यन्नम्नि कीर्तिते वा श्रुते ऽपि वा ।
पापिनस्तु विशुद्धाः स्युः शद्धा मोक्षमवान्पुयुः ॥
1.2.m: When whose name is praised or even heard in any manner whatsoever, sinners become purified and the pure attain liberation.

1.2.s:
ātmanyātmānamādhāya yogino gatakalmaśāḥ /
paśyanti yaṃ jñānarupaṃ tamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
1.2.d:
आत्मन्यात्मानमाधाय योगिनो गतकल्मशाः ।
पश्यन्ति यं ज्ञानरुपं तमस्मि शरणं गतः ॥
1.2.m: Placing the self in the Self, yogins freed from taint see Him whose nature is knowledge; to Him I have gone for refuge.

1.2.s:
sāṅkhyāḥ sarveṣu paśyanti paripūraṇāntakaṃ harim /
tamādidevamajaraṃ jñānarupaṃ bhajāmyaham //
1.2.d:
साङ्ख्याः सर्वेषु पश्यन्ति परिपूरणान्तकं हरिम् ।
तमादिदेवमजरं ज्ञानरुपं भजाम्यहम् ॥
1.2.m: The Sāṅkhyas see in all things the all-filling, death-destroying Hari; that primeval, ageless God whose nature is knowledge I worship.

1.2.s:
sarvasattvamayaṃ śāntaṃ sarvadraṣṭāramīśvaram /
sahasraśīrṣakaṃ devaṃ vande bhāvātmakaṃ harim //
1.2.d:
सर्वसत्त्वमयं शान्तं सर्वद्रष्टारमीश्वरम् ।
सहस्रशीर्षकं देवं वन्दे भावात्मकं हरिम् ॥
1.2.m: Composed of all beings, peaceful, the all-seeing Lord, the thousand-headed God whose essence is existence, Hari, I praise.

1.2.s:
yadbhūtaṃ yacca vai bhāvyaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ jagat /
daśāṅgulaṃ yo 'tsyatiṣṭattamīśamajaraṃ bhade //
1.2.d:
यद्भूतं यच्च वै भाव्यं स्थावरं जङ्गमं जगत् ।
दशाङ्गुलं यो ऽत्स्यतिष्टत्तमीशमजरं भदे ॥
1.2.m: Whatever has been and whatever is to be, the immovable and movable world, who stood ten fingers' breadth beyond it—that ageless Lord I worship.

1.2.s:
aṇoraṇīyāṃsamajaṃ mahataśca mahattaram /
guhyādguhyatamaṃ devaṃ praṇamāmi punaḥ punaḥ //
1.2.d:
अणोरणीयांसमजं महतश्च महत्तरम् ।
गुह्याद्गुह्यतमं देवं प्रणमामि पुनः पुनः ॥
1.2.m: Subtler than the subtle, unborn, greater than the great, the God more secret than the secret, I bow to again and again.

1.2.s:
dhyātaḥ smṛtaḥ pūjito vā śṛtaḥ praṇamito 'pi vā /
svapadaṃ yo dadātīśastaṃ vande puruṣottamam //
1.2.d:
ध्यातः स्मृतः पूजितो वा शृतः प्रणमितो ऽपि वा ।
स्वपदं यो ददातीशस्तं वन्दे पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
1.2.m: Meditated upon, remembered, worshipped, heard of, or even bowed to, the Lord who bestows His own abode—that Puruṣottama I praise.

1.2.s:
iti stuvantaṃ paramaṃ pereśaṃ harṣāmbusaṃruddhavilocanāste /
munīśvarā nāradasaṃyutāstu sanandanādyāḥ prapudaṃ prajagmuḥ //
1.2.d:
इति स्तुवन्तं परमं पेरेशं हर्षाम्बुसंरुद्धविलोचनास्ते ।
मुनीश्वरा नारदसंयुतास्तु सनन्दनाद्याः प्रपुदं प्रजग्मुः ॥
1.2.m: While he thus praised the supreme Lord of lords, those lordly sages, Sanandana and the others accompanied by Nārada, their eyes veiled with tears of joy, experienced great delight.

1.2.s:
ya idaṃ prātarutyāya pāṭhedvai paurupaṃ stavam /
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde sanatkumāranāradasaṃvāde nāradakṛtaviṣṇustutirnāma dvitīyodhyāyaḥ
1.2.d:
य इदं प्रातरुत्याय पाठेद्वै पौरुपं स्तवम् ।
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे सनत्कुमारनारदसंवादे नारदकृतविष्णुस्तुतिर्नाम द्वितीयोध्यायः
1.2.m:
Whoever, having risen at dawn, recites this hymn to the Puruṣa, his self purified of all sins, goes to Viṣṇu's realm.

Thus in the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa, in the first part, in the first quarter, in the dialogue between Sanatkumāra and Nārada, the second chapter, entitled “The Praise of Viṣṇu Composed by Nārada.”

1.3.s:
nārada uvāca
kathaṃ sasarja brahmādīnādidevaḥ purā vibhuḥ /
tanmamākhyāhi sanaka sarvajño 'sti yato bhavān //
1.3.d:
नारद उवाच
कथं ससर्ज ब्रह्मादीनादिदेवः पुरा विभुः ।
तन्ममाख्याहि सनक सर्वज्ञो ऽस्ति यतो भवान् ॥
1.3.m:
Nārada said:
How did the all-pervading primeval God create Brahmā and the others in the past? Tell me that, O Sanaka, since you are omniscient.

1.3.s:
śrīsanaka uvācā
nārāyaṇo 'kṣaro 'nantaḥ sarvavyāpī nirañjanaḥ /
tenedamakhilaṃ vyātpaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam //
1.3.d:
श्रीसनक उवाचा
नारायणो ऽक्षरो ऽनन्तः सर्वव्यापी निरञ्जनः ।
तेनेदमखिलं व्यात्पं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
1.3.m:
Śrī Sanaka said:
Nārāyaṇa is imperishable, infinite, all-pervading, and taintless; by Him this entire universe, both immovable and movable, is pervaded.

1.3.s:
ādisarge mahāviṣṇuḥ svaprakāśo jaganmayaḥ /
guṇabhedamadhiṣṭhāya mūrttitrikamavāsṛjat //
1.3.d:
आदिसर्गे महाविष्णुः स्वप्रकाशो जगन्मयः ।
गुणभेदमधिष्ठाय मूर्त्तित्रिकमवासृजत् ॥
1.3.m: At the first creation, Mahāviṣṇu, self-luminous and consisting of the universe, having assumed the division of the qualities, brought forth the triad of forms.

1.3.s:
sṛṣṭyarthaṃ tu purā devo dakṣiṇāṅgātprajāpatim /
madhyerudrākhyamīthānaṃ jagadantakaraṃ mune //
1.3.d:
सृष्ट्यर्थं तु पुरा देवो दक्षिणाङ्गात्प्रजापतिम् ।
मध्येरुद्राख्यमीथानं जगदन्तकरं मुने ॥
1.3.m: For the purpose of creation the God of old brought forth Prajāpati from His right side, and from the middle [brought forth] the sovereign Lord named Rudra, who brings an end to the universe, O sage.

1.3.s:
pālanāyāsya jagato vāmāṅgādviṣṇumavyayam /
tamādidevamajaraṃ kecidāhuḥ śivābhidham /
kecidviṣṇuṃ sadā satyaṃ brahmāṇaṃ kecidūcire //
1.3.d:
पालनायास्य जगतो वामाङ्गाद्विष्णुमव्ययम् ।
तमादिदेवमजरं केचिदाहुः शिवाभिधम् ।
केचिद्विष्णुं सदा सत्यं ब्रह्माणं केचिदूचिरे ॥
1.3.m: For the preservation of this universe [He brought forth] the imperishable Viṣṇu from His left side. That primeval, ageless God some call by the name Śiva; some call Him Viṣṇu, ever real; some call Him Brahmā.

1.3.s:
tasya śaktiḥ parā viṣṇorjagatkāryapravartinī /
bhāvābhāvasvarupā sā vidyāvidyeti gīyate //
1.3.d:
तस्य शक्तिः परा विष्णोर्जगत्कार्यप्रवर्तिनी ।
भावाभावस्वरुपा सा विद्याविद्येति गीयते ॥
1.3.m: That supreme power of Viṣṇu, which sets in motion the workings of the universe and is of the nature of existence and non-existence, is sung of as knowledge and ignorance.

1.3.s:
yadā viśvaṃ mahāviṣṇorbhinnatvena pratīyate /
tadā hyavidyā saṃsiddhā bhavedduḥkhasya sādhanam //
1.3.d:
यदा विश्वं महाविष्णोर्भिन्नत्वेन प्रतीयते ।
तदा ह्यविद्या संसिद्धा भवेद्दुःखस्य साधनम् ॥
1.3.m: When the universe is perceived as distinct from Mahāviṣṇu, then indeed ignorance is established, becoming the cause of sorrow.

1.3.s:
jñātṛjñeyādyupādhiste yadā naśyati nārada /
sarvaikabhāvanā buddhiḥ sā vidyetyabhidhīyate //
1.3.d:
ज्ञातृज्ञेयाद्युपाधिस्ते यदा नश्यति नारद ।
सर्वैकभावना बुद्धिः सा विद्येत्यभिधीयते ॥
1.3.m: When the limiting adjunct consisting of knower, object of knowledge, and so on is destroyed for you, O Nārada, that intellect which contemplates the unity of all is designated knowledge.

1.3.s:
eṣaṃ māyā mahāviṣṇorbhinnā saṃsāradāyinī /
abhedabuddhyā dṛṣṭā cetsaṃsārakṣayakāriṇī //
1.3.d:
एषं माया महाविष्णोर्भिन्ना संसारदायिनी ।
अभेदबुद्ध्या दृष्टा चेत्संसारक्षयकारिणी ॥
1.3.m: This māyā of Mahāviṣṇu, [perceived as] differentiated, bestows worldly existence; if viewed with the intellect of non-differentiation, it brings an end to worldly existence.

1.3.s:
viṣṇuśaktisamudbhūtametatsarvaṃ varācaṃm /
yasmādbhinnamidaṃ sarvaṃ yacceṅgedyaccaneṅgati //
1.3.d:
विष्णुशक्तिसमुद्भूतमेतत्सर्वं वराचंम् ।
यस्माद्भिन्नमिदं सर्वं यच्चेङ्गेद्यच्चनेङ्गति ॥
1.3.m: All this, moving and unmoving, has arisen from the power of Viṣṇu; from Him all this is differentiated, both what stirs and what does not stir.

1.3.s:
upādhibhiryathākāśo bhinnatvena pratīyate /
avidyopādhiyogenatathedamakhilaṃ jagat //
1.3.d:
उपाधिभिर्यथाकाशो भिन्नत्वेन प्रतीयते ।
अविद्योपाधियोगेनतथेदमखिलं जगत् ॥
1.3.m: Just as space is perceived as divided on account of limiting adjuncts, so is this entire universe through connection with the limiting adjunct of ignorance.

1.3.s:
yathā harirjagadyāpī tasya śaktistathā mune /
dāhaśaktiryathāṅgāre svāśrayaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭati //
1.3.d:
यथा हरिर्जगद्यापी तस्य शक्तिस्तथा मुने ।
दाहशक्तिर्यथाङ्गारे स्वाश्रयं व्याप्य तिष्टति ॥
1.3.m: Just as Hari pervades the universe, so does His power, O sage, just as the power of burning in a glowing coal abides pervading its own substratum.

1.3.s:
umeti kecidāhustāṃ śaktiṃ lakṣmīṃ tathā pare /
bhāratītyapare caināṃ girijetyambiketi ca //
1.3.d:
उमेति केचिदाहुस्तां शक्तिं लक्ष्मीं तथा परे ।
भारतीत्यपरे चैनां गिरिजेत्यम्बिकेति च ॥
1.3.m: Some call that power Umā, and others Lakṣmī; others call Her Bhāratī, Girijā, and Ambikā;

1.3.s:
durgeti bhadrakālīti caṇḍī māheśvarītyapi /
kaumārī vaiṣṇavī ceti vārāhyendrī ca śāmbhavī //
1.3.d:
दुर्गेति भद्रकालीति चण्डी माहेश्वरीत्यपि ।
कौमारी वैष्णवी चेति वाराह्येन्द्री च शाम्भवी ॥
1.3.m: Durgā, Bhadrakālī, Caṇḍī, and Māheśvarī; Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, Aindrī, and Śāmbhavī;

1.3.s:
brāhmīti vidyāvidyeti māyeti ca tathā pare /
prakṛtiśca parā ceti vadanti paramarṣasyaḥ //
1.3.d:
ब्राह्मीति विद्याविद्येति मायेति च तथा परे ।
प्रकृतिश्च परा चेति वदन्ति परमर्षस्यः ॥
1.3.m: Brāhmī, knowledge, ignorance, and māyā; and others, the supreme ṛṣis, call Her Prakṛti and the Supreme.

1.3.s:
śeṣaśaktiḥ parā viṣṇorjagatsargādikāriṇī /
vyaktāvyaktasvarupeṇa jagahyāpya vyavasthitā //
1.3.d:
शेषशक्तिः परा विष्णोर्जगत्सर्गादिकारिणी ।
व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरुपेण जगह्याप्य व्यवस्थिता ॥
1.3.m: The ultimate, supreme power of Viṣṇu, bringing about the creation and so on of the universe, resides pervading the universe in both manifest and unmanifest form.

1.3.s:
prakṛtiścapumāṃścaiva kālaśceti vidhisthitiḥ /
sṛṣṭisthitivināśānāmekaḥ kāraṇatāṃ gataḥ //
1.3.d:
प्रकृतिश्चपुमांश्चैव कालश्चेति विधिस्थितिः ।
सृष्टिस्थितिविनाशानामेकः कारणतां गतः ॥
1.3.m: Prakṛti, Puruṣa, and Time are the fixed order; He, being one, has become the cause of creation, preservation, and destruction.

1.3.s:
yenedamakhilaṃ jātaṃ brahmarupadhareṇa vai /
tasmātparataro devo nityaityabhidhīyate //
1.3.d:
येनेदमखिलं जातं ब्रह्मरुपधरेण वै ।
तस्मात्परतरो देवो नित्यैत्यभिधीयते ॥
1.3.m: By whom this entire [world] was produced while bearing the form of Brahmā—the God higher than that is declared to be eternal.

1.3.s:
rakṣāṃ karoti yo devo nitya ityabhidhīyate /
rakṣāṃ karoti yo devo jagatāṃ parataḥ pumān //
1.3.d:
रक्षां करोति यो देवो नित्य इत्यभिधीयते ।
रक्षां करोति यो देवो जगतां परतः पुमान् ॥
1.3.m: The God who maintains protection is declared to be eternal; the God who maintains protection of the worlds is the Puruṣa beyond.

1.3.s: tasmātparataraṃ yattadavyayaṃ paramaṃ padam //
1.3.d: तस्मात्परतरं यत्तदव्ययं परमं पदम् ॥
1.3.m: Higher than that is that imperishable supreme abode.

1.3.s:
akṣaro nirguṇaḥ śuddhaḥ paripūrṇaḥ sanātanaḥ /
yaḥ paraḥ kālapupākhyo yogidhyeyaḥ parātparaḥ //
1.3.d:
अक्षरो निर्गुणः शुद्धः परिपूर्णः सनातनः ।
यः परः कालपुपाख्यो योगिध्येयः परात्परः ॥
1.3.m: Imperishable, devoid of qualities, pure, all-filling, eternal, He who is the supreme named Time, who is to be meditated on by yogins, higher than the high,

1.3.s:
paramātmā parānandaḥ sarvopādhivivarjitaḥ /
jñānaikavedyaḥ paramaḥ sañcidānandavigrahaḥ //
1.3.d:
परमात्मा परानन्दः सर्वोपाधिविवर्जितः ।
ज्ञानैकवेद्यः परमः सञ्चिदानन्दविग्रहः ॥
1.3.m: the supreme Self, supreme bliss, free from all limiting adjuncts, knowable through knowledge alone, supreme, whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss—

1.3.s:
yo 'sau śuddho 'pi paramo hyahṝṅkāreṇa saṃyutaḥ /
dehīti procyate mūḍhairaho 'jñānaviḍambanam //
1.3.d:
यो ऽसौ शुद्धो ऽपि परमो ह्यहॄङ्कारेण संयुतः ।
देहीति प्रोच्यते मूढैरहो ऽज्ञानविडम्बनम् ॥
1.3.m: even though He is pure and supreme, being conjoined with the 'I'-maker, He is called 'the embodied soul' by fools; oh, the mockery of ignorance!

1.3.s:
sa devaḥ paramaḥ śuddhaḥ sattvadiguṇabhedataḥ /
mūrtitrayaṃ samāpannaḥ sṛṣṭisthityantakāraṇam //
1.3.d:
स देवः परमः शुद्धः सत्त्वदिगुणभेदतः ।
मूर्तित्रयं समापन्नः सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तकारणम् ॥
1.3.m: That supreme, pure God, through the distinction of qualities such as sattva, has attained the threefold form that is the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution.

1.3.s:
yo 'sau brahmā jagatkartā yannābhikamalodbhavaḥ /
sa evānandarupātmā tasmānnāstyaparo mune //
1.3.d:
यो ऽसौ ब्रह्मा जगत्कर्ता यन्नाभिकमलोद्भवः ।
स एवानन्दरुपात्मा तस्मान्नास्त्यपरो मुने ॥
1.3.m: That Brahmā, the creator of the world, who arose from His navel-lotus, is Himself the self whose nature is bliss; there is none other than He, O sage.

1.3.s:
antaryāmī jagadyāpī sarvasākṣī nirañjanaḥ /
bhinnābhinnasvarupeṇa sthito vai parameśvaraḥ //
1.3.d:
अन्तर्यामी जगद्यापी सर्वसाक्षी निरञ्जनः ।
भिन्नाभिन्नस्वरुपेण स्थितो वै परमेश्वरः ॥
1.3.m: The inner controller, all-pervading in the universe, the witness of all, taintless, the supreme Lord indeed abides in a form both distinct and non-distinct.

1.3.s:
yasya śaktirmahāmāyā jagadvistrambhadhāriṇī /
viśvotpatternidānatvātprakṛtiḥ procyate budhaiḥ //
1.3.d:
यस्य शक्तिर्महामाया जगद्विस्त्रम्भधारिणी ।
विश्वोत्पत्तेर्निदानत्वात्प्रकृतिः प्रोच्यते बुधैः ॥
1.3.m: His power is Mahāmāyā, bearing the manifestation of the universe; because it is the primary cause of the origination of the universe, it is called Prakṛti by the wise.

1.3.s:
ādisarge mahāviṣṇorlokānkarttuṃ samudyataḥ /
prakṛtiḥ puruṣaśceti kālaśceti tridhā bhavet //
1.3.d:
आदिसर्गे महाविष्णोर्लोकान्कर्त्तुं समुद्यतः ।
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चेति कालश्चेति त्रिधा भवेत् ॥
1.3.m: At the first creation, Mahāviṣṇu, preparing to make the worlds, becomes threefold: Prakṛti, Puruṣa, and Time.

1.3.s:
paśyanti bhāvitātmāno yaṃ brahmatyabhisaṃjñitam /
śuddhaṃ yatparamaṃ dhāma tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
1.3.d:
पश्यन्ति भावितात्मानो यं ब्रह्मत्यभिसंज्ञितम् ।
शुद्धं यत्परमं धाम तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
1.3.m: Those whose minds are cultivated see Him who is designated as Brahman; that pure supreme realm is Viṣṇu's supreme abode.

1.3.s:
evaṃ śuddho 'kṣaro 'nantaḥ kālarupī maheśvaraḥ /
guṇarupīguṇādhārojagatāmādikṛdvibhuḥ //
1.3.d:
एवं शुद्धो ऽक्षरो ऽनन्तः कालरुपी महेश्वरः ।
गुणरुपीगुणाधारोजगतामादिकृद्विभुः ॥
1.3.m: Thus pure, imperishable, infinite, having the form of Time, the great Lord, having the form of qualities, the substratum of qualities, is the all-pervading originator of the worlds.

1.3.s:
pratṛtiḥ kṣobhamāpannā puruṣākhye jagadgurau /
mahānprādurabhūddhuddhistato 'haṃ samavarttata //
1.3.d:
प्रतृतिः क्षोभमापन्ना पुरुषाख्ये जगद्गुरौ ।
महान्प्रादुरभूद्धुद्धिस्ततो ऽहं समवर्त्तत ॥
1.3.m: Prakṛti underwent agitation in the guru of the universe named Puruṣa; the Great [principle], intellect, became manifest, and from it egoism arose.

1.3.s:
ahṝṅkārāśca sūkṣmāṇi tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi ca /
tanmātrebhyo hi jātāni bhūtāni jagataḥ kṛte //
1.3.d:
अहॄङ्काराश्च सूक्ष्माणि तन्मात्राणीन्द्रियाणि च ।
तन्मात्रेभ्यो हि जातानि भूतानि जगतः कृते ॥
1.3.m: From egoism came the subtle subtle elements and the senses; indeed from the subtle elements the gross elements were born for the sake of the universe.

1.3.s:
ākāśavāyyagrijalabhūmayo 'bjabhāvātmaja /
yathākramaṃ kāraṇatāmekaikasyopayānti ca //
1.3.d:
आकाशवाय्यग्रिजलभूमयो ऽब्जभावात्मज ।
यथाक्रमं कारणतामेकैकस्योपयान्ति च ॥
1.3.m: Space, wind, fire, water, and earth, O son of the lotus-born [Brahmā], / successively become the causal origin one of another.

1.3.s:
tato brahmā jagaddhātā tāmasānasṛjatprabhuḥ /
tiryagyonigatāñjantūnpaśupakṣimṛgādikān //
1.3.d:
ततो ब्रह्मा जगद्धाता तामसानसृजत्प्रभुः ।
तिर्यग्योनिगताञ्जन्तून्पशुपक्षिमृगादिकान् ॥
1.3.m: Then the lord Brahmā, the creator of the world, produced the beings endowed with tamas: / creatures born in animal wombs—beasts, birds, wild animals, and the rest.

1.3.s:
tamapyasādhakaṃ matvā devasargaṃ sanātanāt /
tato vaimānuṣaṃ sargaṃ kalpayāmāsa pahmajaḥ //
1.3.d:
तमप्यसाधकं मत्वा देवसर्गं सनातनात् ।
ततो वैमानुषं सर्गं कल्पयामास पह्मजः ॥
1.3.m: Deeming even that ineffective, the lotus-born then fashioned / the human creation distinct from the eternal divine creation.

1.3.s:
tato dakṣādikānputrānsṛṣṭisādhanatatparān /
ebhiḥ putrairidaṃ vyāptaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam //
1.3.d:
ततो दक्षादिकान्पुत्रान्सृष्टिसाधनतत्परान् ।
एभिः पुत्रैरिदं व्याप्तं सदेवासुरमानुषम् ॥
1.3.m: Then [he created] sons such as Dakṣa, intent upon accomplishing creation; / by these sons this [world], along with gods, asuras, and mortals, was overspread.

1.3.s:
bhurbhuvaśca tathā svaśca mahaśvaiva janastathā /
tapaśca satyamityevaṃ lokāḥ satyopari sthitāḥ //
1.3.d:
भुर्भुवश्च तथा स्वश्च महश्वैव जनस्तथा ।
तपश्च सत्यमित्येवं लोकाः सत्योपरि स्थिताः ॥
1.3.m: Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, as well as Mahaḥ, Janaḥ, / Tapaḥ, and Satyam—thus the worlds are established, with Satya at the top.

1.3.s:
atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva sutalaṃ ca talātalam /
mahātalaṃ ca viprendra tato 'dhacca rasātalam //
1.3.d:
अतलं वितलं चैव सुतलं च तलातलम् ।
महातलं च विप्रेन्द्र ततो ऽधच्च रसातलम् ॥
1.3.m: Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Talātala, / Mahātala, O best of brahmins, and below that Rasātala,

1.3.s:
pātālaṃ ceti saptaiva pātālāni kramādadhaḥ /
eṣa sarveṣu lokeṣu lokanāthāṃśca sṛṣṭavān //
1.3.d:
पातालं चेति सप्तैव पातालानि क्रमादधः ।
एष सर्वेषु लोकेषु लोकनाथांश्च सृष्टवान् ॥
1.3.m: and Pātāla—these are the seven subterranean realms in descending order. / He also created the world-guardians in all the worlds.

1.3.s:
kulācalānnadīścāsau tattallokanivāsinām /
varttanādīni sarvāṇi yathāyogyaṃmakalpayat //
1.3.d:
कुलाचलान्नदीश्चासौ तत्तल्लोकनिवासिनाम् ।
वर्त्तनादीनि सर्वाणि यथायोग्यंमकल्पयत् ॥
1.3.m: He created the ancestral mountain ranges, the rivers, / and fittingly arranged all means of sustenance and the like for the inhabitants of each realm.

1.3.s:
bhūtale madhyago meruḥ sarvadevasamāśrayaḥ /
lokālokaśca bhūmyante tanmadhye satpa sāgarāḥ //
1.3.d:
भूतले मध्यगो मेरुः सर्वदेवसमाश्रयः ।
लोकालोकश्च भूम्यन्ते तन्मध्ये सत्प सागराः ॥
1.3.m: In the middle of the earth stands Meru, the refuge of all the gods, / and Lokāloka is at the edge of the earth; within them lie the seven oceans.

1.3.s:
dvīpāśca satpa viprendra dvīpe kulācalāḥ /
bāhyā nadyaśca vikhyātā janāścāmarasannibhāḥ //
1.3.d:
द्वीपाश्च सत्प विप्रेन्द्र द्वीपे कुलाचलाः ।
बाह्या नद्यश्च विख्याता जनाश्चामरसन्निभाः ॥
1.3.m: There are seven continents, O best of brahmins; in each continent are ancestral mountains / and renowned outer rivers, and the people resemble immortals.

1.3.s:
jambūplakṣābhidhānau ca śālmalaśca kuśastathā /
krauñcaśākau puṣkaraśca te sarve devabhūmayaḥ //
1.3.d:
जम्बूप्लक्षाभिधानौ च शाल्मलश्च कुशस्तथा ।
क्रौञ्चशाकौ पुष्करश्च ते सर्वे देवभूमयः ॥
1.3.m: Those named Jambū and Plakṣa, and Śālmala and Kuśa, / Krauñca, Śāka, and Puṣkara—all of them are lands of the gods.

1.3.s:
ete dvīpāḥ samudraistu satpasatpabhirāvṛtāḥ /
lavaṇekṣusurāsarpirdadhikṣīrajalaiḥ samam //
1.3.d:
एते द्वीपाः समुद्रैस्तु सत्पसत्पभिरावृताः ।
लवणेक्षुसुरासर्पिर्दधिक्षीरजलैः समम् ॥
1.3.m: These continents are encircled by seven oceans equal to them, / with waters of salt, sugarcane juice, wine, clarified butter, curd, milk, and fresh water.

1.3.s:
ete dvīpāḥ samudrāśca pūrvasmāduttarerāḥ /
jñeyā dviguṇavistarā lokālokāñca parvatāt //
1.3.d:
एते द्वीपाः समुद्राश्च पूर्वस्मादुत्तरेराः ।
ज्ञेया द्विगुणविस्तरा लोकालोकाञ्च पर्वतात् ॥
1.3.m: Each of these continents and oceans beyond the previous one / should be known as twice as vast, up to Mount Lokāloka.

1.3.s:
kṣārodadherupattaraṃ yaddhi mādreścaiva dakṣiṇām /
jñeyaṃ tadbhārataṃ varṣaṃ sarvakarmaphalapradam //
1.3.d:
क्षारोदधेरुपत्तरं यद्धि माद्रेश्चैव दक्षिणाम् ।
ज्ञेयं तद्भारतं वर्षं सर्वकर्मफलप्रदम् ॥
1.3.m: That which lies north of the salt ocean and south of the Snowy Mountain / should be known as the realm of Bhārata, which bestows the fruit of all deeds.

1.3.s:
atra karmāṇi kurvanti trividhāni tu nārada /
tatphalaṃ bhujyate caiva bhogabhūmidhanakramāt //
1.3.d:
अत्र कर्माणि कुर्वन्ति त्रिविधानि तु नारद ।
तत्फलं भुज्यते चैव भोगभूमिधनक्रमात् ॥
1.3.m: Here mortals perform three kinds of actions, O Nārada; / and their fruit is enjoyed in succession across lands of enjoyment and wealth.

1.3.s:
bhārate tu kṛtaṃ karma śubhaṃ vāśubhameva ca /
tatphalaṃ kṣayi viprendra bhujyate 'nyatrajantubhiḥ //
1.3.d:
भारते तु कृतं कर्म शुभं वाशुभमेव च ।
तत्फलं क्षयि विप्रेन्द्र भुज्यते ऽन्यत्रजन्तुभिः ॥
1.3.m: Whatever deed is done in Bhārata, whether auspicious or inauspicious, / its perishable fruit is enjoyed by living beings elsewhere, O best of brahmins.

1.3.s:
adyāpi devā icchanti janma bhāratabhūtale /
saṃcitaṃ sumahatpuṇyamakṣayyamamalaṃ śubham //
1.3.d:
अद्यापि देवा इच्छन्ति जन्म भारतभूतले ।
संचितं सुमहत्पुण्यमक्षय्यममलं शुभम् ॥
1.3.m: Even today the gods desire birth on the soil of Bhārata / through very great, imperishable, spotless, and auspicious merit accumulated [by them]:

1.3.s:
kadā labhāmahe janma varṣabhāratabhūmiṣu /
kadā puṇyena mahatā yāsyāma paramaṃ padam //
1.3.d:
कदा लभामहे जन्म वर्षभारतभूमिषु ।
कदा पुण्येन महता यास्याम परमं पदम् ॥
1.3.m: “When shall we attain birth in the lands of the realm of Bhārata? / When, through great merit, shall we attain the supreme abode?

1.3.s:
dānairvāvividhairyajñaistapobhirvāthavā harim /
jagadīśaṃsameṣyāmo nityānandamanāmayam //
1.3.d:
दानैर्वाविविधैर्यज्ञैस्तपोभिर्वाथवा हरिम् ।
जगदीशंसमेष्यामो नित्यानन्दमनामयम् ॥
1.3.m: When, through various gifts, sacrifices, or austerities, shall we reach Hari, / the Lord of the universe, who is eternal bliss and free from all affliction?”

1.3.s:
yo bhāratabhuvaṃ prāpya viṣṇupūjāparo bhavet /
na tasya sadṛśo 'nyo 'sti triṣu lokeṣu nāradā //
1.3.d:
यो भारतभुवं प्राप्य विष्णुपूजापरो भवेत् ।
न तस्य सदृशो ऽन्यो ऽस्ति त्रिषु लोकेषु नारदा ॥
1.3.m: Whoever, having attained the land of Bhārata, is devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, / there is none equal to him in the three worlds, O Nārada.

1.3.s:
harikīrtanaśīlo vā tadbhaktānāṃ piyo 'pi vā /
śukṣaṣurvāpi mahataḥ savedyo divijairapi //
1.3.d:
हरिकीर्तनशीलो वा तद्भक्तानां पियो ऽपि वा ।
शुक्षषुर्वापि महतः सवेद्यो दिविजैरपि ॥
1.3.m: Whether one is habituated to chanting the praise of Hari, or dear to his devotees, / or eager to serve great souls, he is worthy of worship even by the gods.

1.3.s:
haripūjārato nityaṃ bhaktaḥ pūjāsto 'ṣi vā /
bhaktocchiṣṭānnasevī ca yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam //
1.3.d:
हरिपूजारतो नित्यं भक्तः पूजास्तो ऽषि वा ।
भक्तोच्छिष्टान्नसेवी च याति विष्णोः परं पदम् ॥
1.3.m: Constantly devoted to Hari’s worship, or a devotee seated in worship, / or one who partakes of the food remnants left by devotees, he goes to Viṣṇu's supreme abode.

1.3.s:
nārāyaṇeti kṛṣṇeti vāsudeveti yo vadet /
ahiṃsādiparaḥ śantiḥ so 'pi vandyaḥ surottamaiḥ //
1.3.d:
नारायणेति कृष्णेति वासुदेवेति यो वदेत् ।
अहिंसादिपरः शन्तिः सो ऽपि वन्द्यः सुरोत्तमैः ॥
1.3.m: Whoever utters, “Nārāyaṇa,” “Kṛṣṇa,” or “Vāsudeva,” / devoted to non-violence and the like, peaceful—he too is worthy of veneration by the foremost gods.

1.3.s:
śiveti nīlakaṇṭheti śaṅkaretica yaḥ smaret /
sarvabhūtahito nityaṃ so 'bhyarcyo divijaiḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.3.d:
शिवेति नीलकण्ठेति शङ्करेतिच यः स्मरेत् ।
सर्वभूतहितो नित्यं सो ऽभ्यर्च्यो दिविजैः स्मृतः ॥
1.3.m: Whoever remembers [him] as “Śiva,” “Nīlakaṇṭha,” and “Śaṅkara,” / ever intent on the welfare of all beings, he is considered worthy of worship by the gods.

1.3.s:
gurubhaktaḥ śivadhyānī svāśramācāratatparaḥ /
anasūyuḥśucirdakṣo yaḥ so 'pyarcyaḥsureśvaraiḥ //
1.3.d:
गुरुभक्तः शिवध्यानी स्वाश्रमाचारतत्परः ।
अनसूयुःशुचिर्दक्षो यः सो ऽप्यर्च्यःसुरेश्वरैः ॥
1.3.m: Devoted to his guru, meditating on Śiva, intent on the conduct of his own stage of life, / free from malice, pure, and capable—he too is worthy of worship by the lords of gods.

1.3.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ hitakaraḥ śradhdāvānvarṇadharmayoḥ /
vedavādarato nityaṃ sa jñeyaḥ paṅkipāvanaḥ //
1.3.d:
ब्राह्मणानां हितकरः श्रध्दावान्वर्णधर्मयोः ।
वेदवादरतो नित्यं स ज्ञेयः पङ्किपावनः ॥
1.3.m: Beneficial to brahmins, faithful to the duties of caste and life-stage, / ever devoted to the discourse of the Vedas, he should be known as one who purifies a row [of diners].

1.3.s:
abhedadarśī deveśe nārāyaṇaśivātmake /
sarvaṃ yo brahmaṇa nityamasmadādiṣu kā kathā //
1.3.d:
अभेददर्शी देवेशे नारायणशिवात्मके ।
सर्वं यो ब्रह्मण नित्यमस्मदादिषु का कथा ॥
1.3.m: He who perceives no difference in the Lord of gods consisting of Nārāyaṇa and Śiva, / [viewing] all as Brahman constantly—what need to speak of us and the like?

1.3.s:
goṣu kṣānto brahmacārī paranindāvivarjitaḥ /
aparigrahaśī laśca devapūjyaḥ sa nārada //
1.3.d:
गोषु क्षान्तो ब्रह्मचारी परनिन्दाविवर्जितः ।
अपरिग्रहशी लश्च देवपूज्यः स नारद ॥
1.3.m: Patient toward cows, celibate, free from censuring others, / and disposed to non-acceptance of gifts—he is worthy of worship by the gods, O Nārada.

1.3.s:
steyādidoṣavimukhaḥ kṛtajñaḥ satyavāk śuciḥ /
paropakāranirataḥ pūjanīyaḥ surāsuraiḥ //
1.3.d:
स्तेयादिदोषविमुखः कृतज्ञः सत्यवाक् शुचिः ।
परोपकारनिरतः पूजनीयः सुरासुरैः ॥
1.3.m: Averse to vices such as theft, grateful, truthful in speech, pure, / and devoted to helping others, he is worthy of worship by gods and asuras.

1.3.s:
vedārthaśravaṇe buddhiḥ purāṇaśravaṇe tathā /
satsaṃge 'pi ca yasyāsti so 'pi vandyaḥ surottamaiḥ //
1.3.d:
वेदार्थश्रवणे बुद्धिः पुराणश्रवणे तथा ।
सत्संगे ऽपि च यस्यास्ति सो ऽपि वन्द्यः सुरोत्तमैः ॥
1.3.m: One whose intellect is applied to hearing the meaning of the Vedas, hearing the Purāṇas, / and to the company of the good—he too is worthy of veneration by the foremost gods.

1.3.s:
evamādīnyanekāni karmāṇi śraddhayānvitaḥ /
karoti bhārate varṣe saṃbandho 'smābhireva ca //
1.3.d:
एवमादीन्यनेकानि कर्माणि श्रद्धयान्वितः ।
करोति भारते वर्षे संबन्धो ऽस्माभिरेव च ॥
1.3.m: Endowed with faith, he performs many such actions / in the realm of Bhārata; his connection is indeed with us.

1.3.s:
eteṣvanyatamo vipramātmānaṃ nārabhettu yaḥ /
sa eva duṣkṛtirmūḍho nāstyanyo 'smādacetanaḥ //
1.3.d:
एतेष्वन्यतमो विप्रमात्मानं नारभेत्तु यः ।
स एव दुष्कृतिर्मूढो नास्त्यन्यो ऽस्मादचेतनः ॥
1.3.m: Whoever does not apply himself to any one of these, O brahmin, / is an evildoer, a fool; there is none more insensate than he.

1.3.s:
saṃprāpya bhārate janma satkarma suparāṅmukhaḥ /
pīyūṣakalaśaṃ suktvā viṣabhāṇḍamupāśritaḥ //
1.3.d:
संप्राप्य भारते जन्म सत्कर्म सुपराङ्मुखः ।
पीयूषकलशं सुक्त्वा विषभाण्डमुपाश्रितः ॥
1.3.m: Having obtained birth in Bhārata, one who turns away from good deeds / is like one who abandons a vessel of nectar and resorts to a pot of poison.

1.3.s:
śrutismṛtyuditairddharmairnātmānaṃ pāvayettu yaḥ /
sa evātmavidhātī syātpāpināmagraṇīrmune //
1.3.d:
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितैर्द्धर्मैर्नात्मानं पावयेत्तु यः ।
स एवात्मविधाती स्यात्पापिनामग्रणीर्मुने ॥
1.3.m: Whoever does not purify himself through the duties taught by the revealed texts and tradition / is indeed a destroyer of his own soul, foremost among sinners, O sage.

1.3.s:
karmabhūmiṃ samāsādya yo na dharmaṃ samācaret /
sa ca sarvādhamaḥ prokto vedavidbhirmunīśvara //
1.3.d:
कर्मभूमिं समासाद्य यो न धर्मं समाचरेत् ।
स च सर्वाधमः प्रोक्तो वेदविद्भिर्मुनीश्वर ॥
1.3.m: Having reached the land of action, whoever does not practice righteousness / is declared by knowers of the Veda to be the lowest of all, O lord of sages.

1.3.s:
śubhaṃ karma samutsṛjya duṣkarmāṇi karoti yaḥ /
kāmadhenuṃ parityajya arkakṣīraṃ saṃ mārgati //
1.3.d:
शुभं कर्म समुत्सृज्य दुष्कर्माणि करोति यः ।
कामधेनुं परित्यज्य अर्कक्षीरं सं मार्गति ॥
1.3.m: Abandoning good deeds, whoever performs evil deeds / gives up the wish-granting cow and seeks the milk of the swallow-wort.

1.3.s:
evaṃ bhāratabhūbhāgaṃ praśaṃsanti divaukasaḥ /
brahmādyā api viprendra svabhogakṣayabhīravaḥ //
1.3.d:
एवं भारतभूभागं प्रशंसन्ति दिवौकसः ।
ब्रह्माद्या अपि विप्रेन्द्र स्वभोगक्षयभीरवः ॥
1.3.m: Thus the dwellers of heaven, even Brahmā and the others, / afraid of the exhaustion of their own enjoyments, praise the land of Bhārata, O best of brahmins.

1.3.s:
tasmātpuṇyatamaṃ jñeyaṃ bhārataṃ varṣamuttamam /
devānāṃ durlabhaṃ vāpi sarvakarmaphalapradam //
1.3.d:
तस्मात्पुण्यतमं ज्ञेयं भारतं वर्षमुत्तमम् ।
देवानां दुर्लभं वापि सर्वकर्मफलप्रदम् ॥
1.3.m: Therefore the excellent realm of Bhārata should be known as the most sacred, / difficult to obtain even for gods, bestowing the fruit of all actions.

1.3.s:
asminpuṇye ca bhūbhāge yastu satkarmasūdyataḥ /
na tasya sadṛśaṃ kaścitriṣu vidyate //
1.3.d:
अस्मिन्पुण्ये च भूभागे यस्तु सत्कर्मसूद्यतः ।
न तस्य सदृशं कश्चित्रिषु विद्यते ॥
1.3.m: Whoever is intent upon good deeds in this sacred part of the earth, / none equal to him is to be found in the three [worlds].

1.3.s:
asmiñjāto naro yastu svaṅkarmakṣapaṇodyataḥ /
nararupaparicchannaḥ sa harirnātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.3.d:
अस्मिञ्जातो नरो यस्तु स्वङ्कर्मक्षपणोद्यतः ।
नररुपपरिच्छन्नः स हरिर्नात्र संशयः ॥
1.3.m: That man born here who is intent on the exhaustion of his karma / is Hari disguised in human form; of this there is no doubt.

1.3.s:
paraṃ lokaphalaṃ prepsuḥ kiryātkarmāṇyatandritaḥ /
nivedya haraye bhaktyā tatphalaṃ hyakṣayaṃ smṛtam //
1.3.d:
परं लोकफलं प्रेप्सुः किर्यात्कर्माण्यतन्द्रितः ।
निवेद्य हरये भक्त्या तत्फलं ह्यक्षयं स्मृतम् ॥
1.3.m: Desiring the fruit of the higher world, one should unwearyingly perform actions, / having offered them to Hari with devotion; for its fruit is taught to be imperishable.

1.3.s:
virāgī cetkarmaphaleṣvapi kiñcitra kārayet /
arpayetsukṛtaṃ karma prīyatāmitiṃ me hariḥ //
1.3.d:
विरागी चेत्कर्मफलेष्वपि किञ्चित्र कारयेत् ।
अर्पयेत्सुकृतं कर्म प्रीयतामितिं मे हरिः ॥
1.3.m: If one is dispassionate, one should not cause anything to be done for the sake of the fruits of actions; / one should offer one's well-done action, thinking, “May Hari be pleased with me.”

1.3.s:
ābrahmabhuvanāllokāḥ punarutpattidāyakāḥ /
phalāgṛdhnuḥ karmaṇāṃ tatprātproti paramaṃ padam //
1.3.d:
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरुत्पत्तिदायकाः ।
फलागृध्नुः कर्मणां तत्प्रात्प्रोति परमं पदम् ॥
1.3.m: Worlds up to the realm of Brahmā cause rebirth; / not longing for the fruit of actions, one attains that supreme abode.

1.3.s:
vedoditāni karmāṇi kuryādīśvaratuṣṭaye /
yathāśramaṃ tyaktukāmaḥ prānpoti padamavyayam //
1.3.d:
वेदोदितानि कर्माणि कुर्यादीश्वरतुष्टये ।
यथाश्रमं त्यक्तुकामः प्रान्पोति पदमव्ययम् ॥
1.3.m: One should perform the actions ordained by the Vedas for the satisfaction of the Lord; / relinquishing desire according to one's stage of life, one attains the imperishable abode.

1.3.s:
niṣkāmo vā sakāmo vā kuryātkarma yathāvidhi /
svāśramācāraśūnyaśca patitaḥ procyate budhaiḥ //
1.3.d:
निष्कामो वा सकामो वा कुर्यात्कर्म यथाविधि ।
स्वाश्रमाचारशून्यश्च पतितः प्रोच्यते बुधैः ॥
1.3.m: Desireless or desiring, one should perform duty according to rule; / one devoid of the conduct of his stage of life is declared fallen by the wise.

1.3.s:
sadācāraparo vipro varddhate brahmatejasā /
tasya viṣṇuśca tuṣṭaḥ syādbhaktiyuktasya nārada //
1.3.d:
सदाचारपरो विप्रो वर्द्धते ब्रह्मतेजसा ।
तस्य विष्णुश्च तुष्टः स्याद्भक्तियुक्तस्य नारद ॥
1.3.m: A brahmin devoted to good conduct thrives with brahma-splendour; / and Viṣṇu is pleased with him when he is endowed with devotion, O Nārada.

1.3.s:
bhārate janma saṃprāpya nātmānaṃ tārayetu yaḥ /
pacyate niraye dhore sa tvācandrākratārakam //
1.3.d:
भारते जन्म संप्राप्य नात्मानं तारयेतु यः ।
पच्यते निरये धोरे स त्वाचन्द्राक्रतारकम् ॥
1.3.m: Having obtained birth in Bhārata, whoever does not save himself / is roasted in terrible hell for as long as the moon, the sun, and the stars endure.

1.3.s:
vāsadevaparo dharmo vāsudevaparaṃ tapaḥ /
vāsudevaparaṃ jñānaṃ vāsudevaparā gatiḥ //
1.3.d:
वासदेवपरो धर्मो वासुदेवपरं तपः ।
वासुदेवपरं ज्ञानं वासुदेवपरा गतिः ॥
1.3.m: Dharma has Vāsudeva as its highest goal; austerity has Vāsudeva as its highest goal; / knowledge has Vāsudeva as its highest goal; the supreme destination is Vāsudeva.

1.3.s:
vāsudevātmakaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
ābrahmastambaparyantaṃ tasmādanyatra vidyate //
1.3.d:
वासुदेवात्मकं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तं तस्मादन्यत्र विद्यते ॥
1.3.m:
All this world, both moving and unmoving, consists of Vāsudeva;
from Brahmā down to a clump of grass, nothing exists apart from him.

1.3.s:
sa eva dhātā tripurāntakaśca sa eva devāsurayajñarupaḥ /
sa evabrahmāṇḍamidaṃ tato 'nyanna kiñcidasti vyatiriktarupam //
1.3.d:
स एव धाता त्रिपुरान्तकश्च स एव देवासुरयज्ञरुपः ।
स एवब्रह्माण्डमिदं ततो ऽन्यन्न किञ्चिदस्ति व्यतिरिक्तरुपम् ॥
1.3.m:
He alone is the Creator and the destroyer of Tripura; he alone has the form of the sacrifice of the gods and asuras;
he alone is this cosmic egg; there is no other distinct form apart from him.

1.3.s:
asmātparaṃ nāparamasti kiñcidyasmādaṇīyānnatathā mahīyān /
vyātpaṃ hi tenedamidaṃ vicitraṃ taṃ devadevaṃ praṇametsamīṅyam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde sṛṣṭibharatakhaṇḍaprāśastyabhūgolānāṃ varṇanaṃ nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.3.d:
अस्मात्परं नापरमस्ति किञ्चिद्यस्मादणीयान्नतथा महीयान् ।
व्यात्पं हि तेनेदमिदं विचित्रं तं देवदेवं प्रणमेत्समीङ्यम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे सृष्टिभरतखण्डप्राशस्त्यभूगोलानां वर्णनं नाम तृतीयो ऽध्यायः
1.3.m:
There is nothing higher than him, nor anything other, since nothing is subtler or greater than he.
For this manifold [world] is pervaded by him; one should bow to that worshipful God of gods.

Thus ends the third chapter, named 'Description of Creation, the Greatness of Bhāratakhaṇḍa, and the Geography of the Earth', in the First Quarter of the First Part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.4.s:
sanaka uvāca
śraddhāpūrvāḥ sarvadharmā manorathaphalapradāḥ /
śraddhayāsādhyate sarvaṃ śraddhayā tuṣyate hariḥ //
1.4.d:
सनक उवाच
श्रद्धापूर्वाः सर्वधर्मा मनोरथफलप्रदाः ।
श्रद्धयासाध्यते सर्वं श्रद्धया तुष्यते हरिः ॥

1.4.s:
bhaktirbhaktyaiva karttavyātathā karmāṇi bhaktitaḥ /
karmaścaddhāvihīnāni na sidhyantiṃ dvijo tamāḥ //
1.4.d:
भक्तिर्भक्त्यैव कर्त्तव्यातथा कर्माणि भक्तितः ।
कर्मश्चद्धाविहीनानि न सिध्यन्तिं द्विजो तमाः ॥
1.4.m:
Devotion should be performed only with devotion, and likewise actions [done] with devotion;
actions devoid of faith do not succeed, O best of the twice-born.

1.4.s:
yathā'loko hi jantūnāṃ ceṣṭākāraṇatāṃ gataḥ /
tathaiva sarvasiddhīnāṃ bhaktiḥ paramakāraṇam //
1.4.d:
यथाऽलोको हि जन्तूनां चेष्टाकारणतां गतः ।
तथैव सर्वसिद्धीनां भक्तिः परमकारणम् ॥
1.4.m:
Just as light has become the cause of activity for living beings,
even so devotion is the supreme cause of all accomplishments.

1.4.s:
yathā samasta lokānāṃ jīvanaṃ salilaṃ smṛtam /
tathā samastasiddhīnāṃ jīvanaṃ bhaktiriṣyate //
1.4.d:
यथा समस्त लोकानां जीवनं सलिलं स्मृतम् ।
तथा समस्तसिद्धीनां जीवनं भक्तिरिष्यते ॥
1.4.m:
Just as water is declared to be the life of all worlds,
even so devotion is regarded as the life of all accomplishments.

1.4.s:
yathā bhūmiṃ samāśritya sarve jīvanti jantavaḥ /
tathā bhaktiṃ samāśritya sarvakāryyāṇi sādhayet //
1.4.d:
यथा भूमिं समाश्रित्य सर्वे जीवन्ति जन्तवः ।
तथा भक्तिं समाश्रित्य सर्वकार्य्याणि साधयेत् ॥
1.4.m:
Just as all living beings live depending on the earth,
even so one should accomplish all undertakings depending on devotion.

1.4.s:
śraddhāvāṃllabhate dharṃmaṃ śraddhāvātarthamāpnuyāt /
śraddhayā sādhyate kāmaḥ śraddhāvānmokṣamānpuyāt //
1.4.d:
श्रद्धावांल्लभते धर्ंमं श्रद्धावातर्थमाप्नुयात् ।
श्रद्धया साध्यते कामः श्रद्धावान्मोक्षमान्पुयात् ॥
1.4.m:
One who has faith attains religious duty; one who has faith obtains wealth;
desire is fulfilled through faith; one who has faith attains liberation.

1.4.s:
na dānairna tapobhirvā yajñairvā bahudakṣiṇaiḥ /
bhaktihīnermuniśceṣṭha tuṣyate bhagavānhariḥ //
1.4.d:
न दानैर्न तपोभिर्वा यज्ञैर्वा बहुदक्षिणैः ।
भक्तिहीनेर्मुनिश्चेष्ठ तुष्यते भगवान्हरिः ॥
1.4.m:
Neither by gifts nor by austerities nor by sacrifices with bountiful sacrificial fees,
if devoid of devotion, O best of sages, is the Blessed Hari pleased.

1.4.s:
merumātrasuvarṇānāṃ koṭikoṭisahasraśaḥ /
dattā cāpyarthanāśāya yatobhaktivivarjitā //
1.4.d:
मेरुमात्रसुवर्णानां कोटिकोटिसहस्रशः ।
दत्ता चाप्यर्थनाशाय यतोभक्तिविवर्जिता ॥
1.4.m:
Even thousands of tens of millions of Meru-sized masses of gold,
if given without devotion, lead only to the destruction of wealth.

1.4.s:
abhaktyā yattapastaptaiḥ kevalaṃ kāyaśoṣaṇam /
abhaktyā yaddhutaṃ havyaṃ bhasmani nyastahavyavat //
1.4.d:
अभक्त्या यत्तपस्तप्तैः केवलं कायशोषणम् ।
अभक्त्या यद्धुतं हव्यं भस्मनि न्यस्तहव्यवत् ॥
1.4.m:
The austerity that is undertaken without devotion is merely the drying up of the body;
the offering that is poured without devotion is like an offering cast upon ashes.

1.4.s:
yatkiñcitkurute karṃmaśraddhayāpyaṇumātrumātrakam /.
tannāma jāyate puṃsāṃ śāśvataṃ pratīdāyakam //
1.4.d:
यत्किञ्चित्कुरुते कर्ंमश्रद्धयाप्यणुमात्रुमात्रकम् ॥
तन्नाम जायते पुंसां शाश्वतं प्रतीदायकम् ॥
1.4.m:
Whatever action a man performs with faith, even if minute as an atom,
that indeed becomes eternal and a source of delight for people.

1.4.s:
aśvameghasahasraṃ vā karṃma vedoditaṃ kṛtam /
tatsarvaṃ niṣphalaṃ brahmanyadi bhaktivivarjitam //
1.4.d:
अश्वमेघसहस्रं वा कर्ंम वेदोदितं कृतम् ।
तत्सर्वं निष्फलं ब्रह्मन्यदि भक्तिविवर्जितम् ॥
1.4.m:
Whether a thousand horse-sacrifices or any action prescribed by the Veda is performed,
all of that is fruitless, O brāhmaṇa, if it is devoid of devotion.

1.4.s:
haribhaktiḥ parā nṝṇāṃ kāmadhenūpamā smṛtā /
tasyāṃ satyāṃ pibantyajñāḥ saṃsāragaralaṃ hyaho //
1.4.d:
हरिभक्तिः परा नॄणां कामधेनूपमा स्मृता ।
तस्यां सत्यां पिबन्त्यज्ञाः संसारगरलं ह्यहो ॥
1.4.m:
Supreme devotion to Hari is considered for men to be like the wish-fulfilling cow;
while it is present, the ignorant—alas!—drink the poison of worldly existence.

1.4.s:
asārabhūte saṃsāre sārametadajātmaja /
bhagavadbhaktasaṅgaśca haribhaktistitikṣutā //
1.4.d:
असारभूते संसारे सारमेतदजात्मज ।
भगवद्भक्तसङ्गश्च हरिभक्तिस्तितिक्षुता ॥
1.4.m:
In this essenceless cycle of rebirth, this is the essence, O son of the Unborn:
the company of the devotees of the Blessed One, devotion to Hari, and forbearance.

1.4.s:
asūyopetamanasāṃ bhaktidānādikarṃma yat /
avehi niṣphalaṃ brahaṃsteṣāṃ dūrataro hariḥ //
1.4.d:
असूयोपेतमनसां भक्तिदानादिकर्ंम यत् ।
अवेहि निष्फलं ब्रहंस्तेषां दूरतरो हरिः ॥
1.4.m:
The acts of devotion, gifting, and so forth, of those whose minds are filled with malice—
know, O brāhmaṇa, that these are fruitless; Hari is far away from them.

1.4.s:
pariśriyābhitatpānāṃ dambhācāraratātmanām /
mṛṣā tu kurvatāṃ karma teṣāṃ dūrataro hariḥ //
1.4.d:
परिश्रियाभितत्पानां दम्भाचाररतात्मनाम् ।
मृषा तु कुर्वतां कर्म तेषां दूरतरो हरिः ॥
1.4.m:
Of those who are consumed by the wealth of others, whose minds are devoted to deceitful conduct,
and who perform action falsely—Hari is far away from them.

1.4.s:
pṛcchatāṃ ca mahādharṃmānvadatāṃ vai mṛṣā ca tān /
dharmeṣvabhaktimanasāṃ teṣāṃ dūrataro hariḥ //
1.4.d:
पृच्छतां च महाधर्ंमान्वदतां वै मृषा च तान् ।
धर्मेष्वभक्तिमनसां तेषां दूरतरो हरिः ॥
1.4.m:
Of those who inquire about great religious duties and yet declare them falsely,
and whose minds have no devotion to religious duties—Hari is far away from them.

1.4.s:
vedapraṇihito dharṃmo dharṃmo vedo nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ /
tatrāśraddhāparā ye tu teṣāṃ dūrataro hariḥ //
1.4.d:
वेदप्रणिहितो धर्ंमो धर्ंमो वेदो नारायणः परः ।
तत्राश्रद्धापरा ये तु तेषां दूरतरो हरिः ॥
1.4.m:
Religious duty is established by the Veda; religious duty is the Veda, and Nārāyaṇa is supreme;
as for those who have no faith in that, Hari is far away from them.

1.4.s:
yasya dharṃmavihīnāni dinānyāyānti yānti ca /
sa lohakārabhastreva śvasannapi na jīvati //
1.4.d:
यस्य धर्ंमविहीनानि दिनान्यायान्ति यान्ति च ।
स लोहकारभस्त्रेव श्वसन्नपि न जीवति ॥
1.4.m:
He whose days come and go devoid of religious duty,
even though breathing, does not truly live, like a blacksmith's bellows.

1.4.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣākhyāḥ puruṣārthāḥ sanātanāḥ /
śraddhāvatāṃ hi sidhyanti nānyathā brahmanandanā //
1.4.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाख्याः पुरुषार्थाः सनातनाः ।
श्रद्धावतां हि सिध्यन्ति नान्यथा ब्रह्मनन्दना ॥
1.4.m:
The eternal aims of human life called religious duty, wealth, desire, and liberation
are accomplished indeed for those who possess faith, and not otherwise, O son of Brahmā.

1.4.s:
svācāramanatikramya haribhaktiparo hi yaḥ /
sa yāti viṣṇubhavanaṃ yadvai paśyanti sūrayaḥ //
1.4.d:
स्वाचारमनतिक्रम्य हरिभक्तिपरो हि यः ।
स याति विष्णुभवनं यद्वै पश्यन्ति सूरयः ॥
1.4.m:
He who, without transgressing his own proper conduct, is devoted to devotion to Hari,
goes to the abode of Viṣṇu, which the wise ever behold.

1.4.s:
kurvanvedoditāndharṃmānmunīndra svāśramocitān /
haridhyānaparoyastu sa yāti paramaṃ padam //
1.4.d:
कुर्वन्वेदोदितान्धर्ंमान्मुनीन्द्र स्वाश्रमोचितान् ।
हरिध्यानपरोयस्तु स याति परमं पदम् ॥
1.4.m:
Performing the duties ordained by the Veda and proper to his own stage of life, O lord of sages,
he who is devoted to meditation on Hari goes to the supreme abode.

1.4.s:
ācāraprabhavo dharmaḥ dharṃmasya prabhuracyutaḥ /
āśramācārayuktena pūjitaḥ sarvadā hariḥ //
1.4.d:
आचारप्रभवो धर्मः धर्ंमस्य प्रभुरच्युतः ।
आश्रमाचारयुक्तेन पूजितः सर्वदा हरिः ॥
1.4.m:
Religious duty originates from proper conduct; Acyuta is the lord of religious duty;
Hari is always worshipped by one who is endowed with the proper conduct of his stage of life.

1.4.s:
yaḥ svācāraparibhraṣṭaḥ sāṅgavedāntago 'pi vā /
sa eva patito jñeyo yataḥ karmabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
1.4.d:
यः स्वाचारपरिभ्रष्टः साङ्गवेदान्तगो ऽपि वा ।
स एव पतितो ज्ञेयो यतः कर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥
1.4.m:
He who has fallen away from his own proper conduct, even if he has mastered the Vedānta with the limbs [of the Veda],
is to be known as fallen, because he is excluded from sacred rites.

1.4.s:
haribhaktipari vāpi haridhyānaparo 'pi vā /
bhraṣṭo yaḥ svāśramācārātpatitaḥ so 'bhidhīyate //
1.4.d:
हरिभक्तिपरि वापि हरिध्यानपरो ऽपि वा ।
भ्रष्टो यः स्वाश्रमाचारात्पतितः सो ऽभिधीयते ॥
1.4.m:
Even if one is intent on devotion to Hari or intent on meditation on Hari,
if he has fallen away from the conduct of his stage of life, he is declared to be fallen.

1.4.s:
vedo vā haribhaktirvā bhaktirvāpi maheśvare /
ācārātpatitaṃ mūḍhaṃ na punāti dvijottama //
1.4.d:
वेदो वा हरिभक्तिर्वा भक्तिर्वापि महेश्वरे ।
आचारात्पतितं मूढं न पुनाति द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.4.m:
Neither the Veda nor devotion to Hari nor devotion to the Great Lord
purifies the fool who has fallen from proper conduct, O best of the twice-born.

1.4.s:
puṇyakṣetrābhigamanaṃ puṇyatīrthaniṣevaṇam /
yajño vā vividho brahmaṃstyaktācāraṃna rakṣati //
1.4.d:
पुण्यक्षेत्राभिगमनं पुण्यतीर्थनिषेवणम् ।
यज्ञो वा विविधो ब्रह्मंस्त्यक्ताचारंन रक्षति ॥
1.4.m:
Going to sacred fields, resorting to sacred fords,
or various sacrifices do not protect him who has abandoned proper conduct, O brāhmaṇa.

1.4.s:
ācārātprāpyate svarga ācārātprāpyate sukham /
ācārātprāpyate mokṣa ācārātkiṃ na labhyate //
1.4.d:
आचारात्प्राप्यते स्वर्ग आचारात्प्राप्यते सुखम् ।
आचारात्प्राप्यते मोक्ष आचारात्किं न लभ्यते ॥
1.4.m:
From proper conduct heaven is attained; from proper conduct happiness is attained;
from proper conduct liberation is attained; what is not obtained from proper conduct?

1.4.s:
ācārāṇāntu sarveṣāṃ yogānāṃ caiva sattam /
haribhaktepari tathā nidānaṃ bhaktiriṣyate //
1.4.d:
आचाराणान्तु सर्वेषां योगानां चैव सत्तम् ।
हरिभक्तेपरि तथा निदानं भक्तिरिष्यते ॥
1.4.m:
Of all codes of conduct and of all yogas, O best of men,
and superior to devotion to Hari, devotion [itself] is regarded as the primary cause.

1.4.s:
bhaktyaiva pūjyate viṣṇurvāñchitārthaphalapradaḥ /
tasmātsamastalokānāṃ bhaktirmāteti gīyate //
1.4.d:
भक्त्यैव पूज्यते विष्णुर्वाञ्छितार्थफलप्रदः ।
तस्मात्समस्तलोकानां भक्तिर्मातेति गीयते ॥
1.4.m:
Only through devotion is Viṣṇu worshipped, the giver of the fruit of desired aims;
therefore devotion is sung of as the mother of all the worlds.

1.4.s:
jīvanti jantavaḥ sarve yathā mātarāśritāḥ /
tathā bhaktiṃ samāśritya sarve jīvanti dhārṃmikāḥ //
1.4.d:
जीवन्ति जन्तवः सर्वे यथा मातराश्रिताः ।
तथा भक्तिं समाश्रित्य सर्वे जीवन्ति धार्ंमिकाः ॥
1.4.m:
Just as all living beings live depending on their mother,
even so all righteous people live depending on devotion.

1.4.s:
svāśramācārayuktasya haribhaktiryadā bhavet /
na tasya triṣu lokeṣu sadṛśo 'styajanandana //
1.4.d:
स्वाश्रमाचारयुक्तस्य हरिभक्तिर्यदा भवेत् ।
न तस्य त्रिषु लोकेषु सदृशो ऽस्त्यजनन्दन ॥
1.4.m:
When devotion to Hari arises in one who is endowed with the conduct of his stage of life,
there is no one equal to him in the three worlds, O son of the Unborn.

1.4.s:
bhaktyā sidhyanti karṃmāṇi karṃmāṇi karṃmābhistuṣyate hariḥ /
tasmiṃstuṣṭe bhavejjñānaṃ jñānānmokṣamavāpyate //
1.4.d:
भक्त्या सिध्यन्ति कर्ंमाणि कर्ंमाणि कर्ंमाभिस्तुष्यते हरिः ।
तस्मिंस्तुष्टे भवेज्ज्ञानं ज्ञानान्मोक्षमवाप्यते ॥
1.4.m:
Through devotion actions succeed; through actions Hari is pleased;
when he is pleased, knowledge arises; from knowledge liberation is attained.

1.4.s:
bhaktistu bhagavadbhaktasaṅgena khalu jāyate /
tatsaṅgaṃ prāpyate pumbhiḥ sukṛtaiḥ pūrvasañcitaiḥ //
1.4.d:
भक्तिस्तु भगवद्भक्तसङ्गेन खलु जायते ।
तत्सङ्गं प्राप्यते पुम्भिः सुकृतैः पूर्वसञ्चितैः ॥
1.4.m:
Devotion indeed arises through the company of the devotees of the Blessed One;
that company is obtained by men through previously accumulated merits.

1.4.s:
varṇāśramācāraratā bhagavadbhaktilālasāḥ /
kāmādidoṣanir muktāste santo lokaśikṣakāḥ //
1.4.d:
वर्णाश्रमाचाररता भगवद्भक्तिलालसाः ।
कामादिदोषनिर् मुक्तास्ते सन्तो लोकशिक्षकाः ॥
1.4.m:
Devoted to the proper conduct of their caste and stage of life, longing for devotion to the Blessed One,
freed from faults such as desire—such good people are the teachers of the world.

1.4.s:
sastaṅgaḥ paramo brahmanna labhyetākṛtātmanām /
yadi labhyeta vijñeyaṃ puṇyaṃ janmāntarārjitam //
1.4.d:
सस्तङ्गः परमो ब्रह्मन्न लभ्येताकृतात्मनाम् ।
यदि लभ्येत विज्ञेयं पुण्यं जन्मान्तरार्जितम् ॥
1.4.m:
The supreme company of the good, O brāhmaṇa, is not to be obtained by unrefined souls;
if it is obtained, it should be known to be the merit earned in another birth.

1.4.s:
pūrvārjitāni pāpāni nāśamāyānti yasya vai /
satsaṅgatirbhavettasya nānyathā ghaṭate hi sā //
1.4.d:
पूर्वार्जितानि पापानि नाशमायान्ति यस्य वै ।
सत्सङ्गतिर्भवेत्तस्य नान्यथा घटते हि सा ॥
1.4.m:
He whose previously accumulated sins come to an end
attains the company of the good; it does not happen otherwise.

1.4.s:
ravirhi raśimajālena divā hantibahistamaḥ /
santaḥ sūktimarīcyoścāntardhvāntaṃ hi sarvadā //
1.4.d:
रविर्हि रशिमजालेन दिवा हन्तिबहिस्तमः ।
सन्तः सूक्तिमरीच्योश्चान्तर्ध्वान्तं हि सर्वदा ॥
1.4.m:
By day the sun destroys external darkness with its web of rays;
the good always destroy inner darkness with the rays of their wise sayings.

1.4.s:
durlabhāḥ puruṣā loke bhagavadbhaktilālasāḥ /
teṣāṃ saṅgo bhavedyasya tasya śāntirhi śāśvatī //
1.4.d:
दुर्लभाः पुरुषा लोके भगवद्भक्तिलालसाः ।
तेषां सङ्गो भवेद्यस्य तस्य शान्तिर्हि शाश्वती ॥
1.4.m:
Rare in this world are men who long for devotion to the Blessed One;
he who attains their company indeed finds eternal peace.

1.4.s:
nārada uvāca
kiṃlakṣaṇā bhāgavatāste ca kiṃ karṃma kurvate /
teṣāṃ loko bhavetkīdṛktatsarvaṃ brūhi tattvataḥ //
1.4.d:
नारद उवाच
किंलक्षणा भागवतास्ते च किं कर्ंम कुर्वते ।
तेषां लोको भवेत्कीदृक्तत्सर्वं ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः ॥
1.4.m:
Nārada said:
What are the characteristics of the devotees of the Blessed One, and what action do they perform?
What kind of world do they attain? Tell me all that in truth.

1.4.s:
tvaṃ hi bhakto rameśasya devadevasya citriṇaḥ /
etānnigadituṃ śaktastvato nāstyadhiko 'paraḥ //
1.4.d:
त्वं हि भक्तो रमेशस्य देवदेवस्य चित्रिणः ।
एतान्निगदितुं शक्तस्त्वतो नास्त्यधिको ऽपरः ॥
1.4.m:
For you are a devotee of the Lord of Ramā, the wonderful God of gods;
there is none other higher than you capable of proclaiming these things.

1.4.s:
sanaka uvāca
śṛṇu brahmanparaṃ guhyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyasya dhīmanaḥ ña /
yamuvāca jagannātho yoganidrāvimocitaḥ //
1.4.d:
सनक उवाच
शृणु ब्रह्मन्परं गुह्यं मार्कण्डेयस्य धीमनः ञ ।
यमुवाच जगन्नाथो योगनिद्राविमोचितः ॥
1.4.m:
Sanaka said:
Hear, O brāhmaṇa, the supreme secret of the wise Mārkaṇḍeya,
which the Lord of the World, released from his yogic sleep, spoke to him.

1.4.s:
yo 'sau viṣṇuḥ paraṃ jyotirdevadevaḥ sanātanaḥ /
jagatkarttā śivabrahma svarupavān //
1.4.d:
यो ऽसौ विष्णुः परं ज्योतिर्देवदेवः सनातनः ।
जगत्कर्त्ता शिवब्रह्म स्वरुपवान् ॥
1.4.m:
He who is that Viṣṇu, the supreme light, the eternal God of gods,
the creator of the universe, who possesses the nature of Śiva and Brahmā—

1.4.s:
yugānte raudrarupeṇa brahmāṇḍagrāhitaḥ /
jagatyekārṇavībhūte naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame //
1.4.d:
युगान्ते रौद्ररुपेण ब्रह्माण्डग्राहितः ।
जगत्येकार्णवीभूते नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे ॥
1.4.m: At the end of the yuga, having swallowed the universe in a fierce form, / when the world had become a single ocean and the moving and unmoving had perished,

1.4.s:
bhagavāneva śeṣātmā śete vaṭadale hariḥ /
asaṃkhyātābjajanmādyairābhūṣitatanūrūhaḥ //
1.4.d:
भगवानेव शेषात्मा शेते वटदले हरिः ।
असंख्याताब्जजन्माद्यैराभूषिततनूरूहः ॥
1.4.m: the Lord alone, Hari, whose self is Śeṣa, lay on a banyan leaf, / the hair of his body adorned by innumerable lotus-born [Brahmās] and others,

1.4.s:
pādāṅguṣṭāgraniryātagaṅgāśītāmbupāvanaḥ /
sūkṣmātsūkṣmataro devo brahmāṇḍagrāsaṃbṛṃhitaḥ //
1.4.d:
पादाङ्गुष्टाग्रनिर्यातगङ्गाशीताम्बुपावनः ।
सूक्ष्मात्सूक्ष्मतरो देवो ब्रह्माण्डग्रासंबृंहितः ॥
1.4.m: purifying with the cool water of the Gaṅgā issuing from the tip of his big toe, / the God subtler than the subtlest, magnified by devouring the cosmic egg.

1.4.s:
vaṭacchade śayāno 'bhūtsarvaśaktisamanvitaḥ /
tasminsthāne mahābhāgo nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
mārkaṇḍeyaḥ sthinastasya līlāḥ paśyanmahe śituḥ //
1.4.d:
वटच्छदे शयानो ऽभूत्सर्वशक्तिसमन्वितः ।
तस्मिन्स्थाने महाभागो नारायणपरायणः ।
मार्कण्डेयः स्थिनस्तस्य लीलाः पश्यन्महे शितुः ॥
1.4.m: Equipped with all powers, he lay upon the banyan leaf; / in that place stayed the highly fortunate Mārkaṇḍeya, devoted to Nārāyaṇa, / beholding the pastimes of that great ruler.

1.4.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
tasminkāle mahāghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame /
harirekaḥ sthita iti mune pūrvaṃ hi śuśruma //
1.4.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
तस्मिन्काले महाघोरे नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे ।
हरिरेकः स्थित इति मुने पूर्वं हि शुश्रुम ॥
1.4.m: The ṛṣis said: / At that terrible time, when the moving and unmoving had perished, / Hari alone remained: so have we heard before, O sage.

1.4.s:
jagatyekārṇavībhūte naṣṭe sthāvarañjagame /
sarvagrastena hariṇā kimarthaṃ so 'vaśeṣitaḥ //
1.4.d:
जगत्येकार्णवीभूते नष्टे स्थावरञ्जगमे ।
सर्वग्रस्तेन हरिणा किमर्थं सो ऽवशेषितः ॥
1.4.m: When the world had become a single ocean and the moving and unmoving had perished, / why was he left remaining by Hari, the consumer of all?

1.4.s:
paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hyatraṃ varttate 'tīva sūta naḥ /
harikīrtisudhāpāne kasyālasyaṃ prajā yate //
1.4.d:
परं कौतूहलं ह्यत्रं वर्त्तते ऽतीव सूत नः ।
हरिकीर्तिसुधापाने कस्यालस्यं प्रजा यते ॥
1.4.m: Indeed, a supreme curiosity exists in us regarding this, O Sūta; / who feels lethargy in drinking the nectar of Hari's praises?

1.4.s:
sūta uvāca
āsīnmunirmahābhāgo mṛkaṇḍuriti viśrutaḥ /
śālagrāme mahātīrthe so 'tapyata mahātapāḥ //
1.4.d:
सूत उवाच
आसीन्मुनिर्महाभागो मृकण्डुरिति विश्रुतः ।
शालग्रामे महातीर्थे सो ऽतप्यत महातपाः ॥
1.4.m: Sūta said: / There was a fortunate sage renowned as Mṛkaṇḍu; / at the great sacred ford Śālagrāma, he performed severe austerities, an ascetic of great asceticism,

1.4.s:
yugānāma yutaṃ brahmangṛṇanbrahma sanātanam //ṭa
nirāhāraḥ kṣamāyuktaḥ satyasandho jitendriyaḥ //
1.4.d:
युगानाम युतं ब्रह्मन्गृणन्ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥ट
निराहारः क्षमायुक्तः सत्यसन्धो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.4.m: chanting the eternal Brahman for ten thousand yugas, O Brahman, / taking no food, endowed with forbearance, true to his word, his senses conquered.

1.4.s:
ātmavatsarvabhūtāni paśyanviṣayaniḥspṛhaḥ /
sarvabhūtahito dānta statāpa sumahattapaḥ //
1.4.d:
आत्मवत्सर्वभूतानि पश्यन्विषयनिःस्पृहः ।
सर्वभूतहितो दान्त स्तताप सुमहत्तपः ॥
1.4.m: Seeing all beings as himself, free from desire for sense-objects, / devoted to the welfare of all beings, self-restrained, he performed exceedingly great austerities.

1.4.s:
tattāpaḥśaṅkitāḥ sarve devā indrādayastadā /
pareśaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmurnārāyaṇamanāmayam //
1.4.d:
तत्तापःशङ्किताः सर्वे देवा इन्द्रादयस्तदा ।
परेशं शरणं जग्मुर्नारायणमनामयम् ॥
1.4.m: Alarmed by his asceticism, all the gods, Indra and the others, then / took refuge in the supreme lord, the flawless Nārāyaṇa.

1.4.s:
kṣīrābdheruttaraṃ tīraṃ saṃprāpyatrivivaukasaḥ /
tuṣṭuvurdevadeveśaṃ pahmanābhaṃ jagadgurum //
1.4.d:
क्षीराब्धेरुत्तरं तीरं संप्राप्यत्रिविवौकसः ।
तुष्टुवुर्देवदेवेशं पह्मनाभं जगद्गुरुम् ॥
1.4.m: Having reached the northern shore of the milk-ocean, the gods / praised the Lord of gods, the lotus-navelled, the world-teacher.

1.4.s:
devā ūcuḥ
nārāyaṇākṣarānanta śaraṇāgatapālaka /
mṛkaṇḍutapasā trastānpāhi naḥ śaraṇāgatān //
1.4.d:
देवा ऊचुः
नारायणाक्षरानन्त शरणागतपालक ।
मृकण्डुतपसा त्रस्तान्पाहि नः शरणागतान् ॥
1.4.m: The gods said: / O Nārāyaṇa, imperishable, endless, protector of those who seek refuge! / Protect us who have sought refuge, terrified by the asceticism of Mṛkaṇḍu.

1.4.s:
jaya devādhideveśa jaya śaṅkhagadādhara /
jayo lokasvarupāya jayo brahmāṇḍahetave //
1.4.d:
जय देवाधिदेवेश जय शङ्खगदाधर ।
जयो लोकस्वरुपाय जयो ब्रह्माण्डहेतवे ॥
1.4.m: Victory, O Lord of the gods of gods! Victory, O holder of the conch and mace! / Victory to the one whose form is the worlds, victory to the cause of the universe!

1.4.s:
namaste devadeveśa namaste lokapāvana /
namaste lokanāthāya namaste lokasākṣiṇe //
1.4.d:
नमस्ते देवदेवेश नमस्ते लोकपावन ।
नमस्ते लोकनाथाय नमस्ते लोकसाक्षिणे ॥
1.4.m: Homage to you, O Lord of the gods of gods! Homage to you, purifier of the worlds! / Homage to the lord of the worlds, homage to the witness of the worlds!

1.4.s:
namaste dhyānagamyāya namaste dhyānahetave /
namaste dhyānarupāya namaste dhyānapākṣiṇe //
1.4.d:
नमस्ते ध्यानगम्याय नमस्ते ध्यानहेतवे ।
नमस्ते ध्यानरुपाय नमस्ते ध्यानपाक्षिणे ॥
1.4.m: Homage to you who are reachable through meditation! Homage to the cause of meditation! / Homage to the one whose form is meditation! Homage to the witness of meditation!

1.4.s:
keśihantre namastubhyaṃ madhuhantre parātmane /
namo bhūmyādirūpāya namaścaitanyarupiṇe //
1.4.d:
केशिहन्त्रे नमस्तुभ्यं मधुहन्त्रे परात्मने ।
नमो भूम्यादिरूपाय नमश्चैतन्यरुपिणे ॥
1.4.m: Homage to you, the slayer of Keśin, the slayer of Madhu, the supreme self! / Homage to the one whose form is the earth and the rest! Homage to the one whose form is consciousness!

1.4.s:
namo jyeṣṭāya śuddhāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane /
arupāya svarupāya bahurupāya te namaḥ //
1.4.d:
नमो ज्येष्टाय शुद्धाय निर्गुणाय गुणात्मने ।
अरुपाय स्वरुपाय बहुरुपाय ते नमः ॥
1.4.m: Homage to the eldest, the pure, the quality-less, the self of qualities! / Homage to you who are formless, whose form is the self, whose forms are manifold!

1.4.s:
namo brahmaṇyadevāya gobrāhmaṇahitāya ca /
jagaddhitāya kṛṣṇāya govindāya namonamaḥ //
1.4.d:
नमो ब्रह्मण्यदेवाय गोब्राह्मणहिताय च ।
जगद्धिताय कृष्णाय गोविन्दाय नमोनमः ॥
1.4.m: Homage to the god devoted to Brahman, and beneficent to cows and brahmins, / to the benefactor of the universe, to Kṛṣṇa, to Govinda, homage, homage!

1.4.s:
namo hikṣamagarbhāya namo brahmādirupiṇe /
namaḥ sūryyādirupāya havyakavyabhuje namaḥ //
1.4.d:
नमो हिक्षमगर्भाय नमो ब्रह्मादिरुपिणे ।
नमः सूर्य्यादिरुपाय हव्यकव्यभुजे नमः ॥
1.4.m: Homage indeed to the one whose womb is forgiveness, homage to the one whose forms are Brahmā and the rest, / homage to the one whose forms are the sun and the rest, homage to the eater of ancestral and divine oblations!

1.4.s:
namo nityāya vandyāya sadānandaikarupiṇe /
namaḥ smṛtārtināśāya bhūyo bhūyo namo namaḥ //
1.4.d:
नमो नित्याय वन्द्याय सदानन्दैकरुपिणे ।
नमः स्मृतार्तिनाशाय भूयो भूयो नमो नमः ॥
1.4.m: Homage to the eternal, to the praiseworthy, whose sole form is constant bliss! / Homage to the destroyer of affliction upon remembrance, again and again, homage, homage!

1.4.s:
evaṃ devastutiṃ śrutvā bhagavānkamalāpatiḥ /
pratyakṣatāmagātteṣāṃ śaṅkacatragadādharaḥ //
1.4.d:
एवं देवस्तुतिं श्रुत्वा भगवान्कमलापतिः ।
प्रत्यक्षतामगात्तेषां शङ्कचत्रगदाधरः ॥
1.4.m: Having heard this praise from the gods, the blessed Lord, the consort of Kamalā, / holding the conch, discus, and mace, became visible to their eyes,

1.4.s:
vikacāmbujapatrākṣaṃ sūryyakoṭisamaprabham /
sarvālaṅkārasaṃyuktaṃ śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam //
1.4.d:
विकचाम्बुजपत्राक्षं सूर्य्यकोटिसमप्रभम् ।
सर्वालङ्कारसंयुक्तं श्रीवत्साङ्कितवक्षसम् ॥
1.4.m: with eyes like the petals of a blooming lotus, with radiance like ten million suns, / adorned with all ornaments, his chest marked with the śrīvatsa,

1.4.s:
pītāmbaradharaṃ saumyaṃ svarṇayajñopavītinam /
stṛyamānaṃ munivaraiḥ pārṣadapravarāvṛttam //
1.4.d:
पीताम्बरधरं सौम्यं स्वर्णयज्ञोपवीतिनम् ।
स्तृयमानं मुनिवरैः पार्षदप्रवरावृत्तम् ॥
1.4.m: wearing yellow garments, gentle, wearing a golden sacred thread, / praised by eminent sages, surrounded by foremost attendants.

1.4.s:
taṃ dṛṣyvā devasaṃghāste tattejohatatejasaḥ /
namaścakrurmudā yuktā aṣṭāṅgauravaniṃ gatāḥ //
1.4.d:
तं दृष्य्वा देवसंघास्ते तत्तेजोहततेजसः ।
नमश्चक्रुर्मुदा युक्ता अष्टाङ्गौरवनिं गताः ॥
1.4.m: Seeing him, those hosts of gods, their own splendor overshadowed by his splendor, / bowed, filled with joy, falling to the earth with eight limbs.

1.4.s:
tataḥ prasanno bhagavānmeghagaṃbhīranisvanaḥ /
uvāca prīṇayandevānnatānindrapurogamān //
1.4.d:
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान्मेघगंभीरनिस्वनः ।
उवाच प्रीणयन्देवान्नतानिन्द्रपुरोगमान् ॥
1.4.m: Then the gracious Lord, with a voice deep as a thundercloud, / spoke, gladdening the bowed gods, with Indra at their head.

1.4.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
jāne vo mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ mṛkaṇḍutapasoṅgam /
yuṣmānna bādhate devāḥ sa ṛṣiḥ sajjanāgrāṇīḥ //
1.4.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
जाने वो मानसं दुःखं मृकण्डुतपसोङ्गम् ।
युष्मान्न बाधते देवाः स ऋषिः सज्जनाग्राणीः ॥
1.4.m: The Blessed Lord said: / I know the mental distress within you arising from Mṛkaṇḍu's austerities; / that sage, the foremost among the virtuous, will not harm you, O gods.

1.4.s:
saṃpadbhiḥ saṃyutā vāpi vipadbhiścāpi sajjanāḥ /
sarvathānyaṃ na bādhante svapne 'pi surasattamāḥ //
1.4.d:
संपद्भिः संयुता वापि विपद्भिश्चापि सज्जनाः ।
सर्वथान्यं न बाधन्ते स्वप्ने ऽपि सुरसत्तमाः ॥
1.4.m: Whether endowed with prosperity or struck with adversity, good people / in no way harm another, even in a dream, O best of gods.

1.4.s:
satataṃ bādhyamāno 'pi viṣayākhyairarātibhiḥ /
avidhāyātmano rakṣāmanyāndveṣṭi kathaṃ sudhīḥ //
1.4.d:
सततं बाध्यमानो ऽपि विषयाख्यैररातिभिः ।
अविधायात्मनो रक्षामन्यान्द्वेष्टि कथं सुधीः ॥
1.4.m: Constantly afflicted though he is by the enemies known as the sense-objects, / without securing his own protection, how could a wise man hate others?

1.4.s:
tāpatrayābhidhānena bādhyamāno hi mānavaḥ /
anyaṃ krīḍayituṃ śaktaḥ kathaṃ bhavati sattamaḥ //
1.4.d:
तापत्रयाभिधानेन बाध्यमानो हि मानवः ।
अन्यं क्रीडयितुं शक्तः कथं भवति सत्तमः ॥
1.4.m: When a man is afflicted by the so-called threefold suffering, / how could that best of beings be capable of tormenting another?

1.4.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā bādhate yaḥ sadā parān /
nityaṃ kāmādibhiryukto mūḍhadhīḥ procyate tu saḥ //
1.4.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा बाधते यः सदा परान् ।
नित्यं कामादिभिर्युक्तो मूढधीः प्रोच्यते तु सः ॥
1.4.m: He who constantly harms others in action, mind, or speech, / always joined with desire and the rest, is called foolish of intellect.

1.4.s:
yo lokahitakṛnmartyo gatāsuryo vimatsaraḥ /
niḥśaṅgaḥ procyate sadbhirihāmātra ca sattamāḥ //
1.4.d:
यो लोकहितकृन्मर्त्यो गतासुर्यो विमत्सरः ।
निःशङ्गः प्रोच्यते सद्भिरिहामात्र च सत्तमाः ॥
1.4.m: That mortal who acts for the welfare of the world, devoid of malice, free from envy, / is called detached by the good, here and in the hereafter, O best of beings.

1.4.s:
saśaṅkaḥ sarvadā duḥkhī niḥśaṅkaḥ sukhamānpuyāt /
gacchadhvaṃ svālayaṃ svasthāḥ krīḍayiṣyati vo na saḥ //
1.4.d:
सशङ्कः सर्वदा दुःखी निःशङ्कः सुखमान्पुयात् ।
गच्छध्वं स्वालयं स्वस्थाः क्रीडयिष्यति वो न सः ॥
1.4.m: One filled with suspicion is always miserable; one free from suspicion attains happiness. / Go to your own abode in good cheer; he will not torment you.

1.4.s:
bhavatāṃ rakṣakaścāhaṃ viharadhvaṃ yathāsukham /
iti datvā varaṃ teṣāmatasīkusumaprabhaḥ //
1.4.d:
भवतां रक्षकश्चाहं विहरध्वं यथासुखम् ।
इति दत्वा वरं तेषामतसीकुसुमप्रभः ॥
1.4.m: And I am your protector; sport at your pleasure! / Having thus granted a boon to them, the Lord, radiant as the atasī flower,

1.4.s:
paśyatāmeva devānāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata /
tuṣṭātmānaḥ suragaṇāṃ yayurnākaṃ yathāgatam //
1.4.d:
पश्यतामेव देवानां तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।
तुष्टात्मानः सुरगणां ययुर्नाकं यथागतम् ॥
1.4.m: vanished right there while the gods were looking on. / With joyful minds, the hosts of gods went to heaven as they had come.

1.4.s:
mṛkaṇḍorapi tuṣṭātmā hariḥ pratyakṣatāmagāt /
arupaṃ paramaṃ brahmasvaprakāśaṃ nirañjanam //
1.4.d:
मृकण्डोरपि तुष्टात्मा हरिः प्रत्यक्षतामगात् ।
अरुपं परमं ब्रह्मस्वप्रकाशं निरञ्जनम् ॥
1.4.m: Hari, pleased in his heart, also appeared visibly to Mṛkaṇḍu: / the formless, supreme Brahman, self-luminous, taintless.

1.4.s:
atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ pītavāsasamacyacutam /
divyāyudhadharaṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛkaṇḍurvismito 'bhavat //
1.4.d:
अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पीतवाससमच्यचुतम् ।
दिव्यायुधधरं दृष्ट्वा मृकण्डुर्विस्मितो ऽभवत् ॥
1.4.m: Seeing Acyuta resembling the atasī blossom, clad in yellow garments, / holding divine weapons, Mṛkaṇḍu was filled with wonder.

1.4.s:
dhyānādunmīlya nayanaṃ apaśyaddharimagrataḥ /
prasannavadanaṃ śāntaṃ dhātāraṃ viśvatejasam //
1.4.d:
ध्यानादुन्मील्य नयनं अपश्यद्धरिमग्रतः ।
प्रसन्नवदनं शान्तं धातारं विश्वतेजसम् ॥
1.4.m: Opening his eyes from meditation, he saw Hari before him, / with a gracious countenance, peaceful, the creator, possessed of all-pervading splendor.

1.4.s:
romāñcitaśarīro 'sāvānandāśruvilocanaḥ /
nanāma daṇḍavadbhūmau devadeva sanātanam //
1.4.d:
रोमाञ्चितशरीरो ऽसावानन्दाश्रुविलोचनः ।
ननाम दण्डवद्भूमौ देवदेव सनातनम् ॥
1.4.m: His body covered in goosebumps, his eyes full of tears of joy, / he bowed like a staff upon the ground to the eternal God of gods.

1.4.s:
aśrubhiḥ kṣālayaṃstasya caraṇau harṣasaṃbhavaiḥ /
śirasyañcalimādhāya stotuṃ samupacakrame //
1.4.d:
अश्रुभिः क्षालयंस्तस्य चरणौ हर्षसंभवैः ।
शिरस्यञ्चलिमाधाय स्तोतुं समुपचक्रमे ॥
1.4.m: Washing his feet with the tears born of his delight, / placing his folded hands upon his head, he began to praise him.

1.4.s:
mṛkaṇḍuruvāca
namaḥ pareśāya parātmarupiṇe parātparasprātparataḥ parāya /
apārapārāya parānukartre namaḥ parebhyaḥ parapāraṇāya //
1.4.d:
मृकण्डुरुवाच
नमः परेशाय परात्मरुपिणे परात्परस्प्रात्परतः पराय ।
अपारपाराय परानुकर्त्रे नमः परेभ्यः परपारणाय ॥
