1.4.m: Mṛkaṇḍu said: / Homage to the supreme lord, whose form is the supreme self, higher than the highest, beyond the beyond! / To the shore of the shoreless, the imitator of the supreme, homage to the transcender of the supreme!

1.4.s:
yo nāmajātyādivikalpahīnaḥ śabdādidoṣavyatirekarupaḥ /
bahusvarupo 'pi nirañjano yastamīśamīḍhyaṃ paramaṃ bhajāmi //
1.4.d:
यो नामजात्यादिविकल्पहीनः शब्दादिदोषव्यतिरेकरुपः ।
बहुस्वरुपो ऽपि निरञ्जनो यस्तमीशमीढ्यं परमं भजामि ॥
1.4.m: He who is free from conceptual distinctions such as name and genus, whose nature is distinct from defects such as sound, / who, though having many forms, is taintless—I worship that praise-worthy supreme Lord.

1.4.s:
devāntavedyaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ hiraṇyagarbhādijagatsvarupam /
anūpamaṃ bhakti janānukampinaṃ bhajāmi sarveśvaramādimīḍyam //
1.4.d:
देवान्तवेद्यं पुरुषं पुराणं हिरण्यगर्भादिजगत्स्वरुपम् ।
अनूपमं भक्ति जनानुकम्पिनं भजामि सर्वेश्वरमादिमीड्यम् ॥
1.4.m: I worship the primal, praise-worthy ruler of all, knowable beyond the gods, the ancient Puruṣa, / whose forms are the universe beginning with Hiraṇyagarbha, incomparable, compassionate to devoted folk.

1.4.s:
paśyanti yaṃ vītasamastadoṣā dhyānaikaniṣṭhā vigataspṛhāśca /
nivṛttamohāḥ paramaṃ pavitraṃ nato 'smi saṃsāranirvarttakaṃ tam //
1.4.d:
पश्यन्ति यं वीतसमस्तदोषा ध्यानैकनिष्ठा विगतस्पृहाश्च ।
निवृत्तमोहाः परमं पवित्रं नतो ऽस्मि संसारनिर्वर्त्तकं तम् ॥
1.4.m: Whom those whose defects are entirely removed, who are solely intent on meditation, free from desire, / and free from delusion behold, the supremely pure: to that terminator of saṃsāra I bow.

1.4.s:
smṛtārtināśanaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaraṇāgatapālakam /
jagatsevyaṃ jagāddhāma pareśaṃ karuṇākaram //
1.4.d:
स्मृतार्तिनाशनं विष्णुं शरणागतपालकम् ।
जगत्सेव्यं जगाद्धाम परेशं करुणाकरम् ॥
1.4.m: [I worship] Viṣṇu, the destroyer of distress upon remembrance, the protector of those who seek refuge, / worshipped by the universe, the abode of the universe, the supreme lord, the ocean of compassion.

1.4.s:
evaṃ stutaḥ sa bhagavānviṣṇustena maharṣiṇā /
avāpa paramāṃ tuṣṭiṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ //
1.4.d:
एवं स्तुतः स भगवान्विष्णुस्तेन महर्षिणा ।
अवाप परमां तुष्टिं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ॥
1.4.m: Praised thus by that great sage, the blessed Lord Viṣṇu, / the bearer of the conch, discus, and mace, attained the highest satisfaction.

1.4.s:
ayāliṅgya muniṃ devaścaturbhirdīrghabāhubhiḥ /
uvāca paramaṃ prītyā varaṃ baraya suvrata //
1.4.d:
अयालिङ्ग्य मुनिं देवश्चतुर्भिर्दीर्घबाहुभिः ।
उवाच परमं प्रीत्या वरं बरय सुव्रत ॥
1.4.m: Embracing the sage with his four long arms, / the God spoke with supreme affection: 'Choose a boon, O you of noble vows!'

1.4.s:
prīto 'smi tapasā tena stotreṇa ca tavānagha /
manasā yadabhipretaṃ varaṃ varaya suvrata //
1.4.d:
प्रीतो ऽस्मि तपसा तेन स्तोत्रेण च तवानघ ।
मनसा यदभिप्रेतं वरं वरय सुव्रत ॥
1.4.m: "I am pleased with that asceticism of yours and with your hymn, O sinless one. / Choose the boon that is desired by your mind, O you of noble vows!"

1.4.s:
mṛkaṇḍurūvāca
devadeva jagannātha kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ /
tvaddarśanamapuṇyānāṃ durlabhaṃ ca yataḥ smṛtam //
1.4.d:
मृकण्डुरूवाच
देवदेव जगन्नाथ कृतार्थो ऽस्मि न संशयः ।
त्वद्दर्शनमपुण्यानां दुर्लभं च यतः स्मृतम् ॥
1.4.m: Mṛkaṇḍu said: / "O God of gods, Lord of the world, I am fulfilled, there is no doubt, / since the sight of you is remembered to be difficult for the meritless to attain.

1.4.s:
brahmādyā yaṃ na vaśyanti yoginaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ /
dharmiṣṭā dīkṣitāśvāpi vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ //
1.4.d:
ब्रह्माद्या यं न वश्यन्ति योगिनः संशितव्रताः ।
धर्मिष्टा दीक्षिताश्वापि वीतरागा विमत्सराः ॥
1.4.m: You whom Brahmā and the others, yogins of strict vows, / the most righteous, the initiated, and those free from passion and free from envy do not see,

1.4.s:
taṃ paśyāmi paraṃ dhāma kimato 'nyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe /
etenaiva kṛtārtho 'smi janārdana jagaddharo //
1.4.d:
तं पश्यामि परं धाम किमतो ऽन्यं वरं वृणे ।
एतेनैव कृतार्थो ऽस्मि जनार्दन जगद्धरो ॥
1.4.m: that supreme abode I behold—what other boon could I choose than this? / By this alone I am fulfilled, O Janārdana, Upholder of the world!

1.4.s:
yatrāmasmṛtimātreṇa mahāpātakino 'pi ye /
tatpade paramaṃ yānni te dṛṣṭvā kiṣunācyuta //
1.4.d:
यत्रामस्मृतिमात्रेण महापातकिनो ऽपि ये ।
तत्पदे परमं यान्नि ते दृष्ट्वा किषुनाच्युत ॥
1.4.m: By mere remembrance of whose name even perpetrators of great sins / go to that supreme abode—having seen you, what [more could be asked], O Acyuta?"

1.4.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
satyatpruktaṃ tvayā brahmānprīno 'smi tava paṇḍita /
madṛrśanaṃ hi viphalaṃ na kadācidbhaviṣyati //
1.4.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
सत्यत्प्रुक्तं त्वया ब्रह्मान्प्रीनो ऽस्मि तव पण्डित ।
मदृर्शनं हि विफलं न कदाचिद्भविष्यति ॥
1.4.m: The Blessed One said: / "Truth has been spoken by you, O brahmin; I am pleased with you, O learned one! / For the sight of me will never be fruitless.

1.4.s:
viṣṇirbhaktakuṭumbīti vadanti vivudhāḥ sadā /
tadeva pālayiṣyāmi majjano nānṛtaṃ vadet //
1.4.d:
विष्णिर्भक्तकुटुम्बीति वदन्ति विवुधाः सदा ।
तदेव पालयिष्यामि मज्जनो नानृतं वदेत् ॥
1.4.m: 'Viṣṇu regards his devotees as his family,' so the wise always say. / I shall uphold that very saying; my people must not speak untruth.

1.4.s:
tasmāttvattapasātuṣṭo yāsyāmi tava putratām /
samastaguṇasaṃyukto dīrghajīvī svarupavān //
1.4.d:
तस्मात्त्वत्तपसातुष्टो यास्यामि तव पुत्रताम् ।
समस्तगुणसंयुक्तो दीर्घजीवी स्वरुपवान् ॥
1.4.m: Therefore, pleased by your asceticism, I shall become your son, / endowed with all virtues, long-lived, and handsome.

1.4.s:
mama janma kule yasya katatkulaṃ mokṣagāmi vai /
mayi tuṣṭe muniśreṣṭha kimasādhyaṃ jagatraye //
1.4.d:
मम जन्म कुले यस्य कतत्कुलं मोक्षगामि वै ।
मयि तुष्टे मुनिश्रेष्ठ किमसाध्यं जगत्रये ॥
1.4.m: The lineage in which I take birth certainly attains liberation. / When I am pleased, O best of sages, what is impossible in the three worlds?"

1.4.s:
ityuktvā devadevaśo muneratasya samīkṣataḥ /
antardadhe mṛkaṇḍuśca tapasaḥ samavartata //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde bhaktivarṇanaprasaṅgena mārkaṇḍeyacaritārambho nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
1.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा देवदेवशो मुनेरतस्य समीक्षतः ।
अन्तर्दधे मृकण्डुश्च तपसः समवर्तत ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे भक्तिवर्णनप्रसङ्गेन मार्कण्डेयचरितारम्भो नाम चतुर्थो ऽध्यायः
1.4.m:
Having spoken thus while that sage looked on, the God of gods / vanished, and Mṛkaṇḍu desisted from his asceticism.

Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled 'The Beginning of the Story of Mārkaṇḍeya' in the context of the description of devotion, in the first quarter of the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.5.s:
nārada uvāca
brahmankathaṃ sa bhagavānmṛkaṇḍoḥ putratāṃ gataḥ /
kiṃ cakāra ca tadbruhi harirbhārgavavaṃśajaḥ //
1.5.d:
नारद उवाच
ब्रह्मन्कथं स भगवान्मृकण्डोः पुत्रतां गतः ।
किं चकार च तद्ब्रुहि हरिर्भार्गववंशजः ॥
1.5.m: Nārada said: / "O brahmin, how did the Blessed One become the son of Mṛkaṇḍu, / and what did Hari do, born into the lineage of Bhṛgu? Tell me that.

1.5.s:
śrūyate capurāṇeṣu mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ /
apaśyadvaiṣṇavīṃ māyāṃ cirañjīvyasya saṃplave //
1.5.d:
श्रूयते चपुराणेषु मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः ।
अपश्यद्वैष्णवीं मायां चिरञ्जीव्यस्य संप्लवे ॥
1.5.m: And it is heard in the Purāṇas that the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya / saw the Vaiṣṇava illusion while living through the deluge as a long-lived one."

1.5.s:
sanaka uvāca
śruṇu nārada vakṣaayāmi kathāmetāṃ sanātanīm /
viṣṇubhaktisamāyuktāṃ mārkuṇḍeyamuniṃ prati //
1.5.d:
सनक उवाच
श्रुणु नारद वक्षअयामि कथामेतां सनातनीम् ।
विष्णुभक्तिसमायुक्तां मार्कुण्डेयमुनिं प्रति ॥
1.5.m: Sanaka said: / "Listen, O Nārada, I shall tell this eternal narrative / connected with devotion to Viṣṇu concerning the sage Mārkaṇḍeya.

1.5.s:
tapaso 'nte mṛkaṇḍuste mṛkaṇḍustu bhāryāmudūhya sattamaḥ /
gārhasthyamakaroddhṛṣṭaḥ śānto dāntaḥ kṛtārthakaḥ //
1.5.d:
तपसो ऽन्ते मृकण्डुस्ते मृकण्डुस्तु भार्यामुदूह्य सत्तमः ।
गार्हस्थ्यमकरोद्धृष्टः शान्तो दान्तः कृतार्थकः ॥
1.5.m: At the end of his asceticism, Mṛkaṇḍu, best of the virtuous, married a wife / and, delighted, tranquil, self-controlled, and fulfilled, entered upon the householder's life.

1.5.s:
tasya bhāryā śucirdakṣā nityaṃ patiparāyaṇā /
manasā vacasā cāpi dehena ca pativratā //
1.5.d:
तस्य भार्या शुचिर्दक्षा नित्यं पतिपरायणा ।
मनसा वचसा चापि देहेन च पतिव्रता ॥
1.5.m: His wife was pure, capable, always devoted to her husband, / and devoted to her husband in mind, word, and body.

1.5.s:
kāle dadhāra sā garbhaṃ haritejoṃśasaṃbhavam /
ruṣuve daśamāsānte putraṃ tejasvināṃ param //
1.5.d:
काले दधार सा गर्भं हरितेजोंशसंभवम् ।
रुषुवे दशमासान्ते पुत्रं तेजस्विनां परम् ॥
1.5.m: In due course, she conceived an embryo born of a portion of Hari's fiery splendour; / at the end of ten months she gave birth to a son, foremost among the splendid.

1.5.s:
sa ṛṣiḥ paramaprīto dṛṣṭvā putraṃ sulakṣaṇam /
jātakaṃ kārayāmāsa maṅgalaṃ vidhipūrvakam //
1.5.d:
स ऋषिः परमप्रीतो दृष्ट्वा पुत्रं सुलक्षणम् ।
जातकं कारयामास मङ्गलं विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
1.5.m: Extremely pleased upon seeing the son endowed with auspicious marks, that sage / had the birth ceremony and auspicious rites performed according to rule.

1.5.s:
sa bālo vavṛdhe tatra śuklapakṣa ivīḍupaḥ /
tatastu pañcame varṣe upanīya mudānvitaḥ //
1.5.d:
स बालो ववृधे तत्र शुक्लपक्ष इवीडुपः ।
ततस्तु पञ्चमे वर्षे उपनीय मुदान्वितः ॥
1.5.m: The boy grew up there like the moon in the bright fortnight; / then, in his fifth year, having performed the sacred thread ceremony with joy,

1.5.s:
śikṣāṃ cakāra viprendra vaidikīṃ dharmasaṃhitām /
namaskāryā dvijāḥ putra sadādṛṣṭā vidhānataḥ //
1.5.d:
शिक्षां चकार विप्रेन्द्र वैदिकीं धर्मसंहिताम् ।
नमस्कार्या द्विजाः पुत्र सदादृष्टा विधानतः ॥
1.5.m: [the father] imparted instruction, O best of brahmins, in the Vedic code of conduct: / 'Son, whenever seen, the twice-born are always to be bowed down to according to rule.

1.5.s:
trikālaṃ sūryamabhyarcya salilāñcalidānataḥ /
vaidikaṃ karma tartavyaṃ vedādhyayanapūrvakam //
1.5.d:
त्रिकालं सूर्यमभ्यर्च्य सलिलाञ्चलिदानतः ।
वैदिकं कर्म तर्तव्यं वेदाध्ययनपूर्वकम् ॥
1.5.m: Worshipping the sun at the three junctures of the day by offering handfuls of water, / Vedic rites are to be performed preceded by study of the Veda.

1.5.s:
brahmacaryeṇa tapasā pūjanīyo hariḥ sadā /
niṣiddhaṃ varjanīyaṃ syādṛṣṭasaṃbhāṣaṇādikam //
1.5.d:
ब्रह्मचर्येण तपसा पूजनीयो हरिः सदा ।
निषिद्धं वर्जनीयं स्यादृष्टसंभाषणादिकम् ॥
1.5.m: Hari is always to be worshipped with celibacy and asceticism; / what is prohibited, such as speaking with the wicked, should be avoided.

1.5.s:
sādhubhiḥ saha vastavyaṃ viṣṇubhaktiparaiḥ sadā /
na dveṣaḥ kasyacitkāryaḥ sarveṣāṃ hitamācaret //
1.5.d:
साधुभिः सह वस्तव्यं विष्णुभक्तिपरैः सदा ।
न द्वेषः कस्यचित्कार्यः सर्वेषां हितमाचरेत् ॥
1.5.m: One must always dwell with the virtuous who are devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu; / hatred must not be directed at anyone; one should act for the good of all.

1.5.s:
ijyādhyaṃyanadānāni sadā kāryāṇi te suta /
evaṃ pitrā samādiṣṭo mārkaṇḍeyo munīśvaraḥ //
1.5.d:
इज्याध्यंयनदानानि सदा कार्याणि ते सुत ।
एवं पित्रा समादिष्टो मार्कण्डेयो मुनीश्वरः ॥
1.5.m: Sacrifices, study, and gifts are always to be performed by you, my son.' / Instructed thus by his father, Mārkaṇḍeya, lord of sages,

1.5.s:
cacāra dharmaṃ satataṃ sadā saṃcintayanharim /
mārkaṇḍeyo mahābhāgo dayāvāndharmavatsalaḥ //
1.5.d:
चचार धर्मं सततं सदा संचिन्तयन्हरिम् ।
मार्कण्डेयो महाभागो दयावान्धर्मवत्सलः ॥
1.5.m: constantly practised righteousness, always meditating on Hari. / The illustrious Mārkaṇḍeya was compassionate, fond of righteousness,

1.5.s:
ātmavānsatyasandhaśca mārtaṇḍasadṛśaprabhaḥ /
vaśīṃ śānto mahājñānī sarvatattvārthakovidaḥ //
1.5.d:
आत्मवान्सत्यसन्धश्च मार्तण्डसदृशप्रभः ।
वशीं शान्तो महाज्ञानी सर्वतत्त्वार्थकोविदः ॥
1.5.m: self-possessed, true to his promise, of radiance like the sun, / master of his senses, tranquil, of great knowledge, and skilled in the meaning of all principles.

1.5.s:
tapaścacāraṃ mahāmacyutaprītikāraṇam /
ārādhito jagannātho mākraṇḍeyena dhīmatā //
1.5.d:
तपश्चचारं महामच्युतप्रीतिकारणम् ।
आराधितो जगन्नाथो माक्रण्डेयेन धीमता ॥
1.5.m: He performed great asceticism to cause pleasure to Acyuta; / the Lord of the world was worshipped by the wise Mārkaṇḍeya.

1.5.s:
purāṇasaṃhitāṃ karttudattavānvaramacyutaḥ /
mārkaṇḍeyo muni tapaścacāraṃ paramamacyutaprītikāraṇam /
mārkaṇḍeyo munistasmānnārāyaṇa iti smṛtaḥ //
1.5.d:
पुराणसंहितां कर्त्तुदत्तवान्वरमच्युतः ।
मार्कण्डेयो मुनि तपश्चचारं परममच्युतप्रीतिकारणम् ।
मार्कण्डेयो मुनिस्तस्मान्नारायण इति स्मृतः ॥
1.5.m: Acyuta granted him a boon to compose a Purāṇic compendium; / the sage Mārkaṇḍeya performed supreme asceticism to cause pleasure to Acyuta; / therefore the sage Mārkaṇḍeya is remembered as Nārāyaṇa.

1.5.s:
cirajīvī mahābhakto devadevasya cakriṇaḥ /
jagatyekārṇavībhūte svaprabhāvaṃ janārddanaḥ //
1.5.d:
चिरजीवी महाभक्तो देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ।
जगत्येकार्णवीभूते स्वप्रभावं जनार्द्दनः ॥
1.5.m: He was long-lived, a great devotee of the discus-bearing God of gods. / When the world had become a single cosmic ocean, Janārdana,

1.5.s:
tasya darśayituṃ vigrāstaṃ na saṃhṛtavānhariḥ /
mṛkaṇḍutanayo dhīmānviṣṇubhaktisamanvitaḥ //
1.5.d:
तस्य दर्शयितुं विग्रास्तं न संहृतवान्हरिः ।
मृकण्डुतनयो धीमान्विष्णुभक्तिसमन्वितः ॥
1.5.m: in order to show him his majesty, did not dissolve him, O brahmins. / The wise son of Mṛkaṇḍu, endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu,

1.5.s:
tasmiñjale mahāghore sthitavāñchīrṇapatravat /
mārkaṇḍeyaḥ sthitastāvadyāvacchete hariḥ svayam //
1.5.d:
तस्मिञ्जले महाघोरे स्थितवाञ्छीर्णपत्रवत् ।
मार्कण्डेयः स्थितस्तावद्यावच्छेते हरिः स्वयम् ॥
1.5.m: remained in that dreadful water like a dry leaf; / Mārkaṇḍeya remained for as long as Hari himself slept.

1.5.s:
tasya pramāṇaṃ vakṣyāmi kālasya vadataḥ śruṇu /
daśabhiḥ pañcabhiścaiva nimeṣaiḥ parikīrtitā //
1.5.d:
तस्य प्रमाणं वक्ष्यामि कालस्य वदतः श्रुणु ।
दशभिः पञ्चभिश्चैव निमेषैः परिकीर्तिता ॥
1.5.m: I shall tell the measure of that time as I speak; listen: / It is proclaimed that by fifteen winks of the eye

1.5.s:
kāṣṭātatriṃśato jñeyā kalā pahmajanandana /
tatriṃśato kṣaṇo jñeyastaiḥ paṅbharghaṭikā smṛtā //
1.5.d:
काष्टातत्रिंशतो ज्ञेया कला पह्मजनन्दन ।
तत्रिंशतो क्षणो ज्ञेयस्तैः पङ्भर्घटिका स्मृता ॥
1.5.m: a kāṣṭhā is formed; from thirty [of them] a kalā is known, O son of the Lotus-born; / from thirty [of them] a kṣaṇa is known; by five of these a ghaṭikā is remembered.

1.5.s:
tadvayena muhūrttaṃ syāddinaṃ tatriṃśatā bhavet /
triṃśaddinerbhavenyāsaḥ pakṣadvitayasaṃyutaḥ //
1.5.d:
तद्वयेन मुहूर्त्तं स्याद्दिनं तत्रिंशता भवेत् ।
त्रिंशद्दिनेर्भवेन्यासः पक्षद्वितयसंयुतः ॥
1.5.m: By two of these a muhūrta is made; by thirty of these a day is formed; / by thirty days a month is formed, consisting of two fortnights.

1.5.s:
ṛturmāsadvayena syāttatrayeṇāyanaṃ smṛtam /
taddayena bhavedabdaḥ sa devānāṃ dinaṃ bhavet //
1.5.d:
ऋतुर्मासद्वयेन स्यात्तत्रयेणायनं स्मृतम् ।
तद्दयेन भवेदब्दः स देवानां दिनं भवेत् ॥
1.5.m: A season consists of two months; by three of them a solstice is remembered; / by two of these a year is formed, which constitutes a day of the gods.

1.5.s:
uttaraṃ divasaṃ prāhū rātrirvai dakṣiṇāyanam /
mānuṣeṇaiva māsena pitṝṇāṃ dinamucyate //
1.5.d:
उत्तरं दिवसं प्राहू रात्रिर्वै दक्षिणायनम् ।
मानुषेणैव मासेन पितॄणां दिनमुच्यते ॥
1.5.m: They say the northern course is the day, and the southern course is the night. / By a single human month, a day of the ancestors is proclaimed.

1.5.s:
tasmātsuryendusaṃyoge jñātavyaṃ kalpamuttamam /
divyairvarṣasahasrairdvādaśabhirdaivataṃ yugam //
1.5.d:
तस्मात्सुर्येन्दुसंयोगे ज्ञातव्यं कल्पमुत्तमम् ।
दिव्यैर्वर्षसहस्रैर्द्वादशभिर्दैवतं युगम् ॥
1.5.m: Therefore, by the conjunction of the sun and the moon, an excellent kalpa is to be known. / By twelve thousand divine years a divine yuga is formed.

1.5.s:
daive yugasahasre dve brāhmaḥ kalpau tu tau nṛṇām /
ekasatpatisaṃkhyātairdivyairmanvantaraṃ yugaiḥ //
1.5.d:
दैवे युगसहस्रे द्वे ब्राह्मः कल्पौ तु तौ नृणाम् ।
एकसत्पतिसंख्यातैर्दिव्यैर्मन्वन्तरं युगैः ॥
1.5.m: Two thousand divine yugas are two kalpas of Brahmā for men. / A manvantara is reckoned by seventy-one divine yugas;

1.5.s:
caturddaśabhiretaiśca brahmaṇo divasaṃmune /
yāvatpramāṇaṃ divasaṃ tāvadrātriḥ prakīrtitā //
1.5.d:
चतुर्द्दशभिरेतैश्च ब्रह्मणो दिवसंमुने ।
यावत्प्रमाणं दिवसं तावद्रात्रिः प्रकीर्तिता ॥
1.5.m: and by fourteen of these, O sage, a day of Brahmā [is completed]. / For as long as the day extends, so long is the night proclaimed to last.

1.5.s:
nāśamāyāti viprendra tasminkāle jagannayam /
manuṣeṇa sahasreṇa yatpramāṇaṃ bhavecchṛṇu //
1.5.d:
नाशमायाति विप्रेन्द्र तस्मिन्काले जगन्नयम् ।
मनुषेण सहस्रेण यत्प्रमाणं भवेच्छृणु ॥
1.5.m: At that time, O best of brahmins, the three worlds go to destruction. / Listen to what the measure is by a thousand human [years]:

1.5.s:
caturyugasahasrāṇi brahmaṇo divasaṃ mune /
tadvanmāso vatsaraśca jñeyastasyāpi vedhasaḥ //
1.5.d:
चतुर्युगसहस्राणि ब्रह्मणो दिवसं मुने ।
तद्वन्मासो वत्सरश्च ज्ञेयस्तस्यापि वेधसः ॥
1.5.m: A thousand four-age cycles are a day of Brahmā, O sage; / likewise the month and year of the Creator are to be known.

1.5.s:
parārddhadvayakālastu tanmatena bhavedvijāḥ /
viṣṇorahastu vijñeyaṃ tāvadrātriḥ prakīrtitā //
1.5.d:
परार्द्धद्वयकालस्तु तन्मतेन भवेद्विजाः ।
विष्णोरहस्तु विज्ञेयं तावद्रात्रिः प्रकीर्तिता ॥
1.5.m: The period of two halves of his life [lasts] according to that measure, O twice-born; / and that is to be known as a single day of Viṣṇu, and for so long his night is proclaimed.

1.5.s:
mṛkaṇḍutanayastāvatsthitaḥ saṃjīrṇaparṇavat /
tasminghore jalamaye viṣṇuśaktyupabṛṃhitaḥ /
ātmānaṃ paramaṃ dhyāyansthitavānharisānnidhau //
1.5.d:
मृकण्डुतनयस्तावत्स्थितः संजीर्णपर्णवत् ।
तस्मिन्घोरे जलमये विष्णुशक्त्युपबृंहितः ।
आत्मानं परमं ध्यायन्स्थितवान्हरिसान्निधौ ॥
1.5.m: For that long the son of Mṛkaṇḍu remained like a dry leaf, / strengthened by the power of Viṣṇu in that dreadful, water-filled expanse, / remaining in the presence of Hari while meditating on the Supreme Self.

1.5.s:
atha kāle samāyāte yoganidrāvimocitaḥ /
sṛṣṭavānbrahmarupeṇa jagadetaccarācaram //
1.5.d:
अथ काले समायाते योगनिद्राविमोचितः ।
सृष्टवान्ब्रह्मरुपेण जगदेतच्चराचरम् ॥
1.5.m: Then, when the time arrived, [Hari,] released from yogic sleep, / created this world of moving and unmoving beings in the form of Brahmā.

1.5.s:
saṃhṛtaṃ tu jalaṃ vīkṣya sṛṣṭaṃ viśvaṃ mṛkaṇḍujaḥ /
vismitaḥ paramaprīto vavande caraṇau hareḥ //
1.5.d:
संहृतं तु जलं वीक्ष्य सृष्टं विश्वं मृकण्डुजः ।
विस्मितः परमप्रीतो ववन्दे चरणौ हरेः ॥
1.5.m: Beholding the water withdrawn and the universe created, the son of Mṛkaṇḍu / was astonished, filled with extreme joy, and bowed to the feet of Hari.

1.5.s:
śirasyañjalimādhāya mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ /
tuṣṭāva vāgbhiriṣṭābhiḥ sadānandaikavigraham //
1.5.d:
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः ।
तुष्टाव वाग्भिरिष्टाभिः सदानन्दैकविग्रहम् ॥
1.5.m: Placing his folded hands upon his head, the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya / praised the embodiment of sole eternal bliss with pleasing words.

1.5.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
sahasraśirasaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam /
vāsudevamanādhāraṃ praṇato 'smijanārdanam //
1.5.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
सहस्रशिरसं देवं नारायणमनामयम् ।
वासुदेवमनाधारं प्रणतो ऽस्मिजनार्दनम् ॥
1.5.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I bow to the thousand-headed God, Nārāyaṇa, the free from illness, / to Vāsudeva, the supportless, to Janārdana;

1.5.s:
ameyamajaraṃ nityaṃ sadānandaikavigraham /
apratarkyamanirdeśyaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam //
1.5.d:
अमेयमजरं नित्यं सदानन्दैकविग्रहम् ।
अप्रतर्क्यमनिर्देश्यं प्रणतो ऽस्मि जनार्द्दनम् ॥
1.5.m: to the immeasurable, ageless, eternal one, whose sole form is constant bliss, / unthinkable and undefinable, I bow to Janārdana;

1.5.s:
akṣaraṃ paramaṃ nityaṃ viśākṣaṃ viśvasambhavam /
sarvatattvamayaṃ śāntaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam //
1.5.d:
अक्षरं परमं नित्यं विशाक्षं विश्वसम्भवम् ।
सर्वतत्त्वमयं शान्तं प्रणतो ऽस्मि जनार्द्दनम् ॥
1.5.m: to the imperishable, supreme, eternal, all-seeing origin of the universe, / composed of all principles, tranquil, I bow to Janārdana;

1.5.s:
purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ siddhaṃ sarvajñānaikabhājanam /
parātparataraṃ rupaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam //
1.5.d:
पुराणं पुरुषं सिद्धं सर्वज्ञानैकभाजनम् ।
परात्परतरं रुपं प्रणतो ऽस्मि जनार्द्दनम् ॥
1.5.m: to the ancient Person, the perfected, the sole vessel of all knowledge, / the form higher than the highest, I bow to Janārdana;

1.5.s:
parañjyotiḥ paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ padam /
sarvaikarupaṃ paramaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanamam //
1.5.d:
परञ्ज्योतिः परं धाम पवित्रं परमं पदम् ।
सर्वैकरुपं परमं प्रणतो ऽस्मि जनार्द्दनमम् ॥
1.5.m: to the supreme light, the supreme abode, the pure, the supreme abode, / the sole form of all, the supreme, I bow to Janārdana;

1.5.s:
taṃ sadānandacinmātraṃ parāṇāṃ paramaṃ padam /
sarvaṃ sanātanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam //
1.5.d:
तं सदानन्दचिन्मात्रं पराणां परमं पदम् ।
सर्वं सनातनं श्रेष्ठं प्रणतो ऽस्मि जनार्द्दनम् ॥
1.5.m: to him who is constant bliss and pure consciousness, the supreme abode of the highest, / the all, the eternal, the most excellent, I bow to Janārdana;

1.5.s:
saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ śāntaṃ māyātītaṃ sumāyinam /
arupaṃ bahurupaṃ taṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam //
1.5.d:
सगुणं निर्गुणं शान्तं मायातीतं सुमायिनम् ।
अरुपं बहुरुपं तं प्रणतो ऽस्मि जनार्द्दनम् ॥
1.5.m: endowed with qualities, devoid of qualities, tranquil, beyond illusion yet possessing excellent illusion, / formless and manifold in form, to that Janārdana I bow;

1.5.s:
yatratadbhagavānviśvaṃ sṛjatyavatti hanti ca /
tamādidevamīśānaṃ praṇato 'smi janārddanam //
1.5.d:
यत्रतद्भगवान्विश्वं सृजत्यवत्ति हन्ति च ।
तमादिदेवमीशानं प्रणतो ऽस्मि जनार्द्दनम् ॥
1.5.m: in whom the Blessed One creates, preserves, and destroys this universe, / to that primal God, the Lord, I bow to Janārdana.

1.5.s:
pareśa paramānanda śaraṇāgatavatsala /
trāhi māṃ karuṇāsindho manotīti namo 'stute //
1.5.d:
परेश परमानन्द शरणागतवत्सल ।
त्राहि मां करुणासिन्धो मनोतीति नमो ऽस्तुते ॥
1.5.m: O Supreme Lord, O supreme bliss, affectionate to those who have come for refuge, / save me, O ocean of compassion! Beyond the mind, homage be to you!

1.5.s:
evaṃ stavantaṃ viprendraṃ mārkaṇḍeyajagadgurum /
uvāca parayā prītyā śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ //
1.5.d:
एवं स्तवन्तं विप्रेन्द्रं मार्कण्डेयजगद्गुरुम् ।
उवाच परया प्रीत्या शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ॥
1.5.m: To the best of brahmins, Mārkaṇḍeya, teacher of the world, who was praising him thus, / the wielder of the conch, discus, and mace spoke with supreme affection.

1.5.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
loke bhāgavatā ye ca bhagavadbhaktamānasāḥ /
teṣāṃ tuṣṭo na sandeho rakṣāmyetāṃśca sarvadā //
1.5.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
लोके भागवता ये च भगवद्भक्तमानसाः ।
तेषां तुष्टो न सन्देहो रक्षाम्येतांश्च सर्वदा ॥
1.5.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
Those who are Bhāgavatas in the world, whose minds are devoted to the Blessed One— / I am pleased with them, there is no doubt, and I protect them at all times.

1.5.s:
ahameva dvijaśreṣṭha nityaṃ pracchannavigrahaḥ /
bhagavadbhaktarupeṇa lokākrakṣāmi sarvadā //
1.5.d:
अहमेव द्विजश्रेष्ठ नित्यं प्रच्छन्नविग्रहः ।
भगवद्भक्तरुपेण लोकाक्रक्षामि सर्वदा ॥
1.5.m: It is I myself, O best of the twice-born, whose form is ever concealed, / who always protect the worlds in the form of a devotee of the Blessed One.

1.5.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
kiṃlakṣaṇā bhāgavatā jāyante kena karṃmaṇā /
etadicchāmyadaṃ śrotuṃ kautuhalaparo yataḥ //
1.5.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
किंलक्षणा भागवता जायन्ते केन कर्ंमणा ।
एतदिच्छाम्यदं श्रोतुं कौतुहलपरो यतः ॥
1.5.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
What are the characteristics of Bhāgavatas, and by what action do they arise? / I wish to hear this, as I am filled with curiosity.

1.5.s:
śrībhagavānuvācā
lakṣaṇaṃ bhāgavatānāṃ śruṇuṣva munisattam /
vaktuṃ teṣāṃ prabhāvaṃ hi śakyate nābdakoṭibhiḥ //
1.5.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाचा
लक्षणं भागवतानां श्रुणुष्व मुनिसत्तम् ।
वक्तुं तेषां प्रभावं हि शक्यते नाब्दकोटिभिः ॥
1.5.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
Hear the characteristics of Bhāgavatas, O best of sages; / indeed, their power cannot be described even in tens of millions of years.

1.5.s:
yo hitāḥ sarvajantūnāṃ gatāsūyā aamatsarā /
viśino nispṛhāḥ śāntāste vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
यो हिताः सर्वजन्तूनां गतासूया अअमत्सरा ।
विशिनो निस्पृहाः शान्तास्ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who are benevolent to all living beings, free from malice and free from envy, / self-controlled, desireless, and tranquil—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
karṃmaṇā manasā vācā parapīḍāṃ na kurvate /
aparigrahaśīlāśca te vai bhāgavatāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.5.d:
कर्ंमणा मनसा वाचा परपीडां न कुर्वते ।
अपरिग्रहशीलाश्च ते वै भागवताः स्मृताः ॥
1.5.m: Those who do not inflict harm on others by deed, thought, or word, / and are habituated to non-acceptance of gifts—they indeed are considered Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
satkathāśravaṇe yeṣāṃ vartate sāttvikī matiḥ /
tadbhaktaviṣṇubhaktāśca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
सत्कथाश्रवणे येषां वर्तते सात्त्विकी मतिः ।
तद्भक्तविष्णुभक्ताश्च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those whose minds are lucidly devoted to hearing virtuous discourses, / and who are devoted to his devotees and devoted to Viṣṇu—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
mātāpitrośca śuśruṣāṃ kurvanti ye narottamāḥ /
gaṅgāviśveśvaradhiyā te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
मातापित्रोश्च शुश्रुषां कुर्वन्ति ये नरोत्तमाः ।
गङ्गाविश्वेश्वरधिया ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those best of men who render service to mother and father / with the thought that they are the Gaṅgā and Viśveśvara—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
ye tu devārccanaratā ye tu tatsādhakāḥ smṛtāḥ /
pūjāṃ dṛṣṭvānumodante te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
ये तु देवार्च्चनरता ये तु तत्साधकाः स्मृताः ।
पूजां दृष्ट्वानुमोदन्ते ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who are devoted to worshiping the gods, those who are known as practitioners of that, / and who rejoice on seeing worship—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
vratināṃ ca yatīnāṃ ca paricaryāparāśaaca ye /
viyuktaparanindāśca te va bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
व्रतिनां च यतीनां च परिचर्यापराशअच ये ।
वियुक्तपरनिन्दाश्च ते व भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who are dedicated to serving those who observe vows and ascetics, / and who are free from speaking ill of others—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
sarveṣāṃ hitavākyāni ye vadanti narottamāḥ /
ye guṇagrāhiṇo loke te vai bhāgavatāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.5.d:
सर्वेषां हितवाक्यानि ये वदन्ति नरोत्तमाः ।
ये गुणग्राहिणो लोके ते वै भागवताः स्मृताः ॥
1.5.m: Those best of men who speak words beneficial to everyone, / and who appreciate good qualities in the world—they indeed are considered Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
ātmavatsarvabhūtāni ye paśyanti narottamāḥ /
tulyāḥ śatruṣu mitreṣu te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
आत्मवत्सर्वभूतानि ये पश्यन्ति नरोत्तमाः ।
तुल्याः शत्रुषु मित्रेषु ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those best of men who view all beings as themselves, / and are equal toward enemies and friends—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
dharṃmaśāstrapravaktāraḥ satyavākyaratāśca ye /
satāṃ śuśrūṣavo ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
धर्ंमशास्त्रप्रवक्तारः सत्यवाक्यरताश्च ये ।
सतां शुश्रूषवो ये च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who expound the treatises on dharma, who are devoted to truthful speech, / and who desire to serve the virtuous—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
vyākurvate purāṇāni tāni śṛṇvanti ye tathā /
tadvaktari ca bhaktā ye te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
व्याकुर्वते पुराणानि तानि शृण्वन्ति ये तथा ।
तद्वक्तरि च भक्ता ये ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who expound the Purāṇas and likewise hear them, / and are devoted to their speaker—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
ye gobrāhmaṇaśuśrūṣaāṃ kurvate satataṃ narāḥ /
tīrthayātrāparā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
ये गोब्राह्मणशुश्रूषआं कुर्वते सततं नराः ।
तीर्थयात्रापरा ये च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those men who continually render service to cows and brahmins, / and who are dedicated to pilgrimages to sacred fords—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
anyeṣāmudayaṃ dṛṣṭvā ye 'bhinavandanti mānavāḥ /
harināmaparā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
अन्येषामुदयं दृष्ट्वा ये ऽभिनवन्दन्ति मानवाः ।
हरिनामपरा ये च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those humans who rejoice upon seeing the prosperity of others, / and who are devoted to the name of Hari—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
ārāmāropaṇaratāstaḍāparirakṣakāḥ /
kāsārakūpakarttāraste vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
आरामारोपणरतास्तडापरिरक्षकाः ।
कासारकूपकर्त्तारस्ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those engaged in planting groves, who protect water reservoirs, / and who make pools and wells—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
ye vai taḍāgakarttāro devasahmāni kurvate /
goyatrīniratā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
ये वै तडागकर्त्तारो देवसह्मानि कुर्वते ।
गोयत्रीनिरता ये च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who construct water reservoirs, build dwellings for the gods, / and are devoted to the gāyatrī—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
ye 'bhinandanti nāmāni hareḥ śrutvātiharṣitāḥ /
romāñcitaśarīrāśca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
ये ऽभिनन्दन्ति नामानि हरेः श्रुत्वातिहर्षिताः ।
रोमाञ्चितशरीराश्च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who, hearing the names of Hari, rejoice with utmost delight, / their bodies horripilating—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
tulasīkāvanaṃ dṛṣṭvā ye namaskurvate narāḥ /
tatkāṣṭāṅkitakarṇā ye te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
तुलसीकावनं दृष्ट्वा ये नमस्कुर्वते नराः ।
तत्काष्टाङ्कितकर्णा ये ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those men who bow upon seeing a grove of tulasī, / and whose ears are marked with its wood—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
tulasīgandhamāghrāya santoṣaṃ kurvate tu ye /
tanmūlamṛttikāṃ ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
तुलसीगन्धमाघ्राय सन्तोषं कुर्वते तु ये ।
तन्मूलमृत्तिकां ये च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who feel joy upon smelling the fragrance of tulasī, / and who [revere] the earth at its root—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
āśramācācaraniratāstathaivātithipūjakāḥ /
ye ca vedārthavaktāraste vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
आश्रमाचाचरनिरतास्तथैवातिथिपूजकाः ।
ये च वेदार्थवक्तारस्ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those devoted to the practices of their stage of life, likewise those who worship guests, / and those who explain the meaning of the Veda—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
śivāpriyāḥ śivāsaktāḥ śivapādārccane ratāḥ /
tripuṇḍradhāriṇo ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
शिवाप्रियाः शिवासक्ताः शिवपादार्च्चने रताः ।
त्रिपुण्ड्रधारिणो ये च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those dear to Śiva, attached to Śiva, devoted to worshiping Śiva's feet, / and who wear the tripuṇḍra—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
vyāharanti ca nāmāni hareḥ śambhormahātmanaḥ /
rudrākṣālaṅkṛtā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
व्याहरन्ति च नामानि हरेः शम्भोर्महात्मनः ।
रुद्राक्षालङ्कृता ये च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who utter the names of Hari and the great-souled Śambhu, / and who are adorned with rudrākṣa beads—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
ye yajanti mahādevaṃ ṛtubhirbahudakṣiṇaiḥ /
hariṃ vā parayā bhaktyā te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
ये यजन्ति महादेवं ऋतुभिर्बहुदक्षिणैः ।
हरिं वा परया भक्त्या ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those who worship Mahādeva with sacrifices accompanied by abundant priestly gifts, / or Hari with supreme devotion—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
viditāni ca śāstrāṇi parārthaṃ gravadanti ye /
sarvatra guṇabhājo ye te vai bhāgavatāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.5.d:
विदितानि च शास्त्राणि परार्थं ग्रवदन्ति ये ।
सर्वत्र गुणभाजो ये ते वै भागवताः स्मृताः ॥
1.5.m: Those who, having understood the scriptures, proclaim them for the sake of others, / and who recognize virtue everywhere—they indeed are considered Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
śive ca parameśe ca viṣṇau ca paramātmani /
samabuddhyā pravarttante te vai bhāgavatāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.5.d:
शिवे च परमेशे च विष्णौ च परमात्मनि ।
समबुद्ध्या प्रवर्त्तन्ते ते वै भागवताः स्मृताः ॥
1.5.m: Those who act with an attitude of equality toward Śiva, the supreme Lord, / and toward Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self—they indeed are considered Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
śivāgrikāryaniratāḥ pañcākṣarajape ratāḥ /
śivadhyānaratā ye ca te vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
शिवाग्रिकार्यनिरताः पञ्चाक्षरजपे रताः ।
शिवध्यानरता ये च ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those devoted to the ritual fire of Śiva, dedicated to the recitation of the five-syllable mantra, / and absorbed in meditation on Śiva—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
pānīyadānaniratā ye 'nnadānaratāstathā /
ekādarśīvrataratā vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
पानीयदाननिरता ये ऽन्नदानरतास्तथा ।
एकादर्शीव्रतरता वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those devoted to giving water, and likewise those devoted to giving food, / and those dedicated to the vow of the eleventh lunar day—they are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
godānaniratā ye ca kanyādānaratāśca ye /
madarthaṃ karṃmakarttāraste vai bhāgavatottamāḥ //
1.5.d:
गोदाननिरता ये च कन्यादानरताश्च ये ।
मदर्थं कर्ंमकर्त्तारस्ते वै भागवतोत्तमाः ॥
1.5.m: Those devoted to the gift of cows, and those devoted to giving away a daughter [in marriage], / and who perform actions for my sake—they indeed are the best of Bhāgavatas.

1.5.s:
ete bhāgavatā vipra kecidatra prakīrtitāḥ /
mayāpi gadituṃ śakyā nābdakoṭiśatairapi //
1.5.d:
एते भागवता विप्र केचिदत्र प्रकीर्तिताः ।
मयापि गदितुं शक्या नाब्दकोटिशतैरपि ॥
1.5.m: These Bhāgavatas, O brahmin, have been proclaimed in part here; / they cannot be fully described by me even in hundreds of tens of millions of years.

1.5.s:
tasmāttvamapi viprendra suśīlo bhava sarvadā /
sarvabhūtāśrayo dānto metro dharṃmaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.5.d:
तस्मात्त्वमपि विप्रेन्द्र सुशीलो भव सर्वदा ।
सर्वभूताश्रयो दान्तो मेत्रो धर्ंमपरायणः ॥
1.5.m: Therefore, O best of brahmins, you too be ever of good conduct, / a refuge to all beings, self-restrained, friendly, and devoted to dharma.

1.5.s:
punaryugāntaparyyantaṃ dharṃmaṃ sarvaṃ samācaran /
manmūrttidhyānanirataḥ paraṃ nirvāṇamāpsyasi //
1.5.d:
पुनर्युगान्तपर्य्यन्तं धर्ंमं सर्वं समाचरन् ।
मन्मूर्त्तिध्याननिरतः परं निर्वाणमाप्स्यसि ॥
1.5.m: Practicing all dharma until the end of the age once more, / absorbed in meditation on my form, you will attain supreme nirvāṇa.

1.5.s:
evaṃ mṛkaṇḍuputrasya svabhaktasya kṛpānidhiḥ /
dattvā varaṃ sa deveśastatraivāntaradhīyata //
1.5.d:
एवं मृकण्डुपुत्रस्य स्वभक्तस्य कृपानिधिः ।
दत्त्वा वरं स देवेशस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
1.5.m: Having thus granted a boon to the son of Mṛkaṇḍu, his own devotee, / that Lord of the gods, a treasure of compassion, vanished right there.

1.5.s:
mārkaṇḍeyo mahābhāgo haribhaktirataḥ sadā /
cacāra paramaṃ dharmamīje ca vidhivanmakhaiḥ //
1.5.d:
मार्कण्डेयो महाभागो हरिभक्तिरतः सदा ।
चचार परमं धर्ममीजे च विधिवन्मखैः ॥
1.5.m: The fortunate Mārkaṇḍeya, constantly devoted to devotion to Hari, / practiced the supreme dharma and sacrificed with rites according to the injunctions.

1.5.s:
śālaprāme mahākṣetre tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ /
dhyānakṣapitakarmā tu paraṃ nirvāṇamātpavān //
1.5.d:
शालप्रामे महाक्षेत्रे तताप परमं तपः ।
ध्यानक्षपितकर्मा तु परं निर्वाणमात्पवान् ॥
1.5.m: In the great sacred field of Śālagrāma he performed supreme austerity; / with his karma destroyed by meditation, he attained supreme nirvāṇa.

1.5.s:
tasmājjantuṣu sarveṣu hitakṛddharipūjakaḥ /
īpsivaṃ manasā yadyanattadānprotyasaṃśayam //
1.5.d:
तस्माज्जन्तुषु सर्वेषु हितकृद्धरिपूजकः ।
ईप्सिवं मनसा यद्यनत्तदान्प्रोत्यसंशयम् ॥
1.5.m: Therefore, one who acts for the welfare of all beings and worships Hari / undoubtedly obtains whatever is desired in the mind.

1.5.s:
sanaka uvāca
etatsarvaṃ nigaditaṃ tvayā pṛṣṭaṃ dvijottama /
bhagavadbhakti māhātmyaṃ kimanyacchrotumicchasi //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde mārkaṇḍeyavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.5.d:
सनक उवाच
एतत्सर्वं निगदितं त्वया पृष्टं द्विजोत्तम ।
भगवद्भक्ति माहात्म्यं किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे मार्कण्डेयवर्णनं नाम पञ्चमो ऽध्यायः
1.5.m:
Sanaka said: / All this that you asked, O best of the twice-born, has been told, / the eulogy of greatness of devotion to the Blessed Lord. What else do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the fifth chapter, named ‘The Description of Mārkaṇḍeya’, in the first quarter of the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.6.s:
sūta uvāca
bhagavadbhaktimāhātmyaṃ śrutvā prītastu nāradaḥ /
punaḥ papraccha sanakaṃ jñānavijñānapāragam //
1.6.d:
सूत उवाच
भगवद्भक्तिमाहात्म्यं श्रुत्वा प्रीतस्तु नारदः ।
पुनः पप्रच्छ सनकं ज्ञानविज्ञानपारगम् ॥
1.6.m: Sūta said: / Having heard the eulogy of greatness of devotion to the Blessed Lord, Nārada was delighted, / and again asked Sanaka, who had reached the far shore of knowledge and experiential wisdom:

1.6.s:
nārada uvāca
kṣetrāṇāmuttamaṃ kṣetraṃ tīrthānāṃ ca tathottamam /
parayā dayayā tathavaṃ brūhiṃ śāstrārthapāraga //
1.6.d:
नारद उवाच
क्षेत्राणामुत्तमं क्षेत्रं तीर्थानां च तथोत्तमम् ।
परया दयया तथवं ब्रूहिं शास्त्रार्थपारग ॥
1.6.m: Nārada said: / Tell me in supreme compassion, O master of the meaning of scriptures, / about the sacred field supreme among sacred fields, and likewise the sacred ford supreme among sacred fords.

1.6.s:
sanaka uvāca
śuṇu brahmantaraṃ guhyaṃ sarvasaṃpatkaraṃ param /
duḥsvanpanāśanaṃ puṇyaṃ dharmyaṃ pāpaharaṃ śubham //
1.6.d:
सनक उवाच
शुणु ब्रह्मन्तरं गुह्यं सर्वसंपत्करं परम् ।
दुःस्वन्पनाशनं पुण्यं धर्म्यं पापहरं शुभम् ॥
1.6.m: Sanaka said: / Listen to the secret of Brahman, supreme, granting all prosperity, / destroying bad dreams, holy, righteous, removing sins, and auspicious;

1.6.s:
śrotavyaṃ munibhirnityaṃ duṣṭagrahanivāraṇam /
sarvarogapraśamanamāyurvardhdanakāraṇam //
1.6.d:
श्रोतव्यं मुनिभिर्नित्यं दुष्टग्रहनिवारणम् ।
सर्वरोगप्रशमनमायुर्वर्ध्दनकारणम् ॥
1.6.m: which must ever be heard by sages, averting malign planets, / pacifying all diseases, and being the cause of lengthening life.

1.6.s:
kṣetrāṇāmuttamaṃ kṣetraṃ tīrthānāṃ ca tathottamam /
gaṅgāyamunayoryogaṃ vadanti paramarṣayaḥ //
1.6.d:
क्षेत्राणामुत्तमं क्षेत्रं तीर्थानां च तथोत्तमम् ।
गङ्गायमुनयोर्योगं वदन्ति परमर्षयः ॥
1.6.m: The sacred field supreme among sacred fields, and likewise the sacred ford supreme among sacred fords, / is said by the great seers to be the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā.

1.6.s:
sitāsitodakaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmādyāḥ sarvadevatāḥ /
munayo manavaścaiva sevante puṇyakāṅkṣiṇaḥ //
1.6.d:
सितासितोदकं तीर्थं ब्रह्माद्याः सर्वदेवताः ।
मुनयो मनवश्चैव सेवन्ते पुण्यकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
1.6.m: The sacred ford of white and dark waters is resorted to by all deities beginning with Brahmā, / by sages, and by the Manus, desirous of merit.

1.6.s:
gaṅgā puṇyanadī jñeyā yato viṣṇupadodbhavā /
ravijā yamunā brahmaṃstayoryogaḥ śubhāvahaḥ //
1.6.d:
गङ्गा पुण्यनदी ज्ञेया यतो विष्णुपदोद्भवा ।
रविजा यमुना ब्रह्मंस्तयोर्योगः शुभावहः ॥
1.6.m: The Gaṅgā is known as a holy river because she arose from the foot of Viṣṇu. / The Yamunā was born of the Sun, O learned one; their confluence brings good fortune.

1.6.s:
smṛtārtināśinī gaṅgā nadīnāṃ pravarā mune /
sarvapāpakṣayakarī sarvopadra vanāśinī //
1.6.d:
स्मृतार्तिनाशिनी गङ्गा नदीनां प्रवरा मुने ।
सर्वपापक्षयकरी सर्वोपद्र वनाशिनी ॥
1.6.m: Remembered, the Gaṅgā destroys distress; she is the foremost of rivers, O sage, / destroying all sins and removing all adversities.

1.6.s:
yāni kṣetrāṇi puṇyāni samudrānte mahītale /
teṣāṃ puṇyatamaṃ jñeyaṃ prayāgākhyaṃ mahāmune //
1.6.d:
यानि क्षेत्राणि पुण्यानि समुद्रान्ते महीतले ।
तेषां पुण्यतमं ज्ञेयं प्रयागाख्यं महामुने ॥
1.6.m: Among whatever holy sacred fields there are on the earth bordered by the ocean, / the most sacred of them, O great sage, is known by the name Prayāga,

1.6.s:
iyāja vedhā yajñena yatra devaṃ ramāpatim /
tathaiva munayaḥ sarve cakraśca vividhānmakhān //
1.6.d:
इयाज वेधा यज्ञेन यत्र देवं रमापतिम् ।
तथैव मुनयः सर्वे चक्रश्च विविधान्मखान् ॥
1.6.m: where the Creator worshipped the Lord, the husband of Ramā, with sacrifice, / and likewise all the sages performed diverse sacrifices.

1.6.s:
sarvatīrthābhiṣekāṇi yāni puṇyāni tāni vai /
gaṅgābindvabhiṣekasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
1.6.d:
सर्वतीर्थाभिषेकाणि यानि पुण्यानि तानि वै ।
गङ्गाबिन्द्वभिषेकस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥
1.6.m: Whatever merits there are in ablutions at all sacred fords / do not indeed equal a sixteenth part of an ablution with a drop of the Gaṅgā.

1.6.s:
gaṅgā gaṅgeti yo brūyādyojanānāṃ śate sthitaḥ /
so 'pi mucyeta pāpebhyaḥ kimu gaṅgābhiṣekavān //
1.6.d:
गङ्गा गङ्गेति यो ब्रूयाद्योजनानां शते स्थितः ।
सो ऽपि मुच्येत पापेभ्यः किमु गङ्गाभिषेकवान् ॥
1.6.m: He who says ‘Gaṅgā, Gaṅgā’ though situated hundreds of leagues away / is freed even so from sins; how much more one who bathes in the Gaṅgā?

1.6.s:
viṣṇupādodbhavā devī viśveśvaraśiraḥ sthitā /
saṃsevyā munibhirdevaḥ kiṃ punaḥ pāmarairjanai //
1.6.d:
विष्णुपादोद्भवा देवी विश्वेश्वरशिरः स्थिता ।
संसेव्या मुनिभिर्देवः किं पुनः पामरैर्जनै ॥
1.6.m: The goddess who arose from the foot of Viṣṇu resides upon the head of the Lord of the Universe; / she is to be resorted to by sages and deities; what then of common folk?

1.6.s:
yatsaikataṃ lalāṭe tu dhriyate manujottamaiḥ /
tatraiva netraṃ vijñeyaṃ vidhyarddhādhaḥ samujjvalat //
1.6.d:
यत्सैकतं ललाटे तु ध्रियते मनुजोत्तमैः ।
तत्रैव नेत्रं विज्ञेयं विध्यर्द्धाधः समुज्ज्वलत् ॥
1.6.m: The sand from her that is borne on the forehead by the best of men / should be known as an eye itself, shining brightly below the crescent moon.

1.6.s:
yanmajjana mahāpuṇyaṃ durlabhaṃ tridivaukasām /
sārupyadāyakaṃ viṣṇoḥ kimasmātkathyate parama //
1.6.d:
यन्मज्जन महापुण्यं दुर्लभं त्रिदिवौकसाम् ।
सारुप्यदायकं विष्णोः किमस्मात्कथ्यते परम ॥
1.6.m: Immersion in her brings great merit, hard to attain even for the dwellers of heaven; / it grants the form of Viṣṇu. What higher thing than this can be told?

1.6.s:
yatra strātāḥ pāpino 'pi sarvapāpavivarjitāḥ /
mahadvimānamāruḍhāḥ prayānti paramaṃ padam //
1.6.d:
यत्र स्त्राताः पापिनो ऽपि सर्वपापविवर्जिताः ।
महद्विमानमारुढाः प्रयान्ति परमं पदम् ॥
1.6.m: Bathing in which even sinners, completely freed from all sins / and having mounted a great aerial car, go to the supreme abode;

1.6.s:
yatra snātā mahātmānaḥ pitṛmātṛkulāni vai /
sahasrāṇi samuddhṛtya viṣṇuloke vrajanti vai //
1.6.d:
यत्र स्नाता महात्मानः पितृमातृकुलानि वै ।
सहस्राणि समुद्धृत्य विष्णुलोके व्रजन्ति वै ॥
1.6.m: bathing in which noble-souled persons uplift thousands / of their paternal and maternal ancestral lines and indeed go to the world of Viṣṇu.

1.6.s:
sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu yo gaṅgāṃ smarati dvica /
puṇyakṣetreṣu sarveṣau sthitavānnātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.6.d:
स स्नातः सर्वतीर्थेषु यो गङ्गां स्मरति द्विच ।
पुण्यक्षेत्रेषु सर्वेषौ स्थितवान्नात्र संशयः ॥
1.6.m: He has bathed in all sacred fords, O twice-born, who remembers the Gaṅgā; / he has resided in all sacred fields, of this there is no doubt.

1.6.s:
yatra snātaṃ naraṃ dṛṣṭvā pāpo 'pi svargabhūmibhāk /
madaṅgasparśemātreṇa devānāmādhapo bhavet //
1.6.d:
यत्र स्नातं नरं दृष्ट्वा पापो ऽपि स्वर्गभूमिभाक् ।
मदङ्गस्पर्शेमात्रेण देवानामाधपो भवेत् ॥
1.6.m: Seeing a man who has bathed in her, even a sinner becomes an heir to the realm of heaven; / merely by touching my limb he would become the sovereign of the gods.

1.6.s:
tulasīmūlasaṃbhūtā dvijapādodbhāvā tathā /
gaṅgodbhavā tu mṛllokānnayatyacyutarupatām //
1.6.d:
तुलसीमूलसंभूता द्विजपादोद्भावा तथा ।
गङ्गोद्भवा तु मृल्लोकान्नयत्यच्युतरुपताम् ॥
1.6.m: The earth born of the root of the tulasī, and also that arisen from the feet of twice-born men, / and that born of the Gaṅgā leads people to the likeness of Acyuta.

1.6.s:
gaṅgā ca tulasī caiva haribhaktiracañcalā /
atyantadurllabhā nṝṇāṃ bhaktirddharmapravaktari //
1.6.d:
गङ्गा च तुलसी चैव हरिभक्तिरचञ्चला ।
अत्यन्तदुर्ल्लभा नॄणां भक्तिर्द्धर्मप्रवक्तरि ॥
1.6.m: The Gaṅgā, the tulasī, unswerving devotion to Hari, / and devotion toward an expounder of righteous duty are exceedingly hard for mortals to attain.

1.6.s:
saddharmavaktuḥ padasaṃbhavāṃ mṛdaṃ gaṅgodbhavāṃ caiva tathā tulasyāḥ /
mūlodbhavāṃ bhaktiyuto manuṣyo dhṛtvā śirasyeti padaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ //
1.6.d:
सद्धर्मवक्तुः पदसंभवां मृदं गङ्गोद्भवां चैव तथा तुलस्याः ।
मूलोद्भवां भक्तियुतो मनुष्यो धृत्वा शिरस्येति पदं च विष्णोः ॥
1.6.m: A man who, endowed with devotion, carries on his head the earth born from the feet / of an expounder of true duty, that born of the Gaṅgā, and that born from the root of the tulasī, goes to the abode of Viṣṇu.

1.6.s:
kadā yāsyāmyahaṃ gaṅgāṃ kadā paśyāmi tāmaham /
vāñcchatyapi ca yo hyevaṃ so 'pi viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet //
1.6.d:
कदा यास्याम्यहं गङ्गां कदा पश्यामि तामहम् ।
वाञ्च्छत्यपि च यो ह्येवं सो ऽपि विष्णुपदं व्रजेत् ॥
1.6.m: He who even longs thus: ‘When shall I go to the Gaṅgā? When shall I see her?’ / even he would go to the abode of Viṣṇu.

1.6.s:
gaṅgāyā mahimā brahmanvaktuṃ varṣaśatairapi /
na śakyate viṣṇunāpi kimanyairbahubhāṣitaiḥ //
1.6.d:
गङ्गाया महिमा ब्रह्मन्वक्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ।
न शक्यते विष्णुनापि किमन्यैर्बहुभाषितैः ॥
1.6.m: The greatness of the Gaṅgā cannot be fully told even in hundreds of years, O Brahman, / even by Viṣṇu; what need then of many words by others?

1.6.s:
aho māyā jagatsarvaṃ mohayatyetadadbhutam /
yato vai narakaṃ yānti gaṅgānātri sthite 'pi hi //
1.6.d:
अहो माया जगत्सर्वं मोहयत्येतदद्भुतम् ।
यतो वै नरकं यान्ति गङ्गानात्रि स्थिते ऽपि हि ॥
1.6.m: Ah, wonderful is this māyā that deludes the entire world, / since people indeed go to hell even while the name of the Gaṅgā exists!

1.6.s:
saṃsāraduḥkha vicchedi gaṅgānāma prakīrtitam /
tathā tulasyā bhaktiśca harikīrtipravaktari //
1.6.d:
संसारदुःख विच्छेदि गङ्गानाम प्रकीर्तितम् ।
तथा तुलस्या भक्तिश्च हरिकीर्तिप्रवक्तरि ॥
1.6.m: The name of the Gaṅgā is celebrated as cutting off the sorrow of worldly existence; / likewise devotion to the tulasī, and toward one who proclaims the glory of Hari.

1.6.s:
sakṛdapyuccaredyastu gaṅgetyevākṣaradvayam /
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati //
1.6.d:
सकृदप्युच्चरेद्यस्तु गङ्गेत्येवाक्षरद्वयम् ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति ॥
1.6.m: He who utters even once just the two syllables ‘Gaṅgā’, / completely freed from all sins, goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

1.6.s:
yojanatritayaṃ yastu gaṅgāyāmadhigacchati /
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryalokaṃ sameti hi //
1.6.d:
योजनत्रितयं यस्तु गङ्गायामधिगच्छति ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः सूर्यलोकं समेति हि ॥
1.6.m: He who walks three leagues toward the Gaṅgā, / completely freed from all sins, attains the world of the Sun.

1.6.s:
seyaṃ gaṅgā mahāpuṇyā nadī bhaktyā niṣevitā /
meṣataulimṛgākarṣu pāvayatyakhilaṃ jagat //
1.6.d:
सेयं गङ्गा महापुण्या नदी भक्त्या निषेविता ।
मेषतौलिमृगाकर्षु पावयत्यखिलं जगत् ॥
1.6.m: This very Gaṅgā, a river of great merit, attended to with devotion, / purifies the whole world in Aries, Libra, and Capricorn.

1.6.s:
godāvarī bhīmarathī kṛṣṇā revā sarasvatī /
tuṅgabhadrā ca kāverī kāliṃndī bāhudā tathā //
1.6.d:
गोदावरी भीमरथी कृष्णा रेवा सरस्वती ।
तुङ्गभद्रा च कावेरी कालिंन्दी बाहुदा तथा ॥
1.6.m: The Godāvarī, Bhīmarathī, Kṛṣṇā, Revā, Sarasvatī, / Tuṅgabhadrā, Kāverī, Kālindī, and Bāhudā;

1.6.s:
vetravatī tāmraparṇī sarayūśca dvijottama /
evamādiṣu tīrtheṣu gaṅgā mukhyatamā smṛtā //
1.6.d:
वेत्रवती ताम्रपर्णी सरयूश्च द्विजोत्तम ।
एवमादिषु तीर्थेषु गङ्गा मुख्यतमा स्मृता ॥
1.6.m: the Vetravatī, Tāmraparṇī, and Sarayū, O best of the twice-born— / among these and other sacred fords, the Gaṅgā is held to be the foremost.

1.6.s:
yathā sarvagato viṣṇurjagavdyāpya pratiṣṭitaḥ /
tatheyaṃ vyāpinī gaṅgā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī //
1.6.d:
यथा सर्वगतो विष्णुर्जगव्द्याप्य प्रतिष्टितः ।
तथेयं व्यापिनी गङ्गा सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी ॥
1.6.m: Just as all-pervading Viṣṇu stands pervading the world, / so this all-pervasive Gaṅgā destroys all sins.

1.6.s:
aho gaṅgā jagaddhātrī snānapānādibhirjagat /
punāti pāvanītyeṣā na kathaṃ sevyate nṛbhiḥ //
1.6.d:
अहो गङ्गा जगद्धात्री स्नानपानादिभिर्जगत् ।
पुनाति पावनीत्येषा न कथं सेव्यते नृभिः ॥
1.6.m: Ah, the Gaṅgā is the supporter of the world; through bathing, drinking, and the like, / she purifies the world; being such a purifier, why is she not resorted to by men?

1.6.s:
tīrthānāmuttamaṃ tīrthaṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ kṣetramuttamam /
vārāṇasīti vikhyātaṃ sarvadevaniṣevitam //
1.6.d:
तीर्थानामुत्तमं तीर्थं क्षेत्राणां क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् ।
वाराणसीति विख्यातं सर्वदेवनिषेवितम् ॥
1.6.m: The sacred ford supreme among sacred fords, the sacred field supreme among sacred fields, / is renowned as Vārāṇasī, resorted to by all the gods.

1.6.s:
te eva śravaṇe dhanye saṃvidāte bahuśrutam /
iha śrutimatāṃ puṃsāṃ kāśī yābhyāṃ śrutāsakṛt //
1.6.d:
ते एव श्रवणे धन्ये संविदाते बहुश्रुतम् ।
इह श्रुतिमतां पुंसां काशी याभ्यां श्रुतासकृत् ॥
1.6.m: Blessed indeed are those two ears that acquire extensive sacred knowledge, / by which Kāśī has been repeatedly heard in this world by men of scriptural learning.

1.6.s:
ye yaṃ smaranti saṃsthānamavimuktaṃ dvijottamam /
nirdhūtasarvapāpāste śivalokaṃ vrajanti vai //
1.6.d:
ये यं स्मरन्ति संस्थानमविमुक्तं द्विजोत्तमम् ।
निर्धूतसर्वपापास्ते शिवलोकं व्रजन्ति वै ॥
1.6.m: Those who remember that abode Avimukta, O best of the twice-born, / having shaken off all sins, indeed go to the world of Śiva.

1.6.s:
yojanānāṃ śatastho 'pi avimuktaṃ smaredyadi /
bahupātakapūrṇo 'pi padaṃ gacchatyanāmayam //
1.6.d:
योजनानां शतस्थो ऽपि अविमुक्तं स्मरेद्यदि ।
बहुपातकपूर्णो ऽपि पदं गच्छत्यनामयम् ॥
1.6.m: Even if stationed a hundred leagues away, if one should remember Avimukta, / though filled with many sins, one goes to the disease-free abode.

1.6.s:
prāṇaprayāṇasamaye yo 'vimuktaṃ smaredvūja /
so 'pi pāpavinirmuktaḥ śaivaṃ padamavānpuyāt //
1.6.d:
प्राणप्रयाणसमये यो ऽविमुक्तं स्मरेद्वूज ।
सो ऽपि पापविनिर्मुक्तः शैवं पदमवान्पुयात् ॥
1.6.m: At the time of the departure of the vital breaths, he who remembers Avimukta, O twice-born, / even he, freed from sin, would attain the abode of Śiva.

1.6.s:
kāśīsmaraṇajaṃ puṇyaṃ bhuktvā svarge tadantataḥ /
pṛthivyāmekarāḍū bhūtvā kāśīṃ prāpya ca muktibhāk //
1.6.d:
काशीस्मरणजं पुण्यं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गे तदन्ततः ।
पृथिव्यामेकराडू भूत्वा काशीं प्राप्य च मुक्तिभाक् ॥
1.6.m: Having enjoyed in heaven the merit born of remembering Kāśī, at the end thereof, / having become sole ruler on earth and reached Kāśī, one shares in liberation.

1.6.s:
bahunātra kimuktena vārāṇasyā guṇānprati /
nāmāpi gṛhṇātāṃ kāśyāścaturvargo na dūrataḥ //
1.6.d:
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन वाराणस्या गुणान्प्रति ।
नामापि गृह्णातां काश्याश्चतुर्वर्गो न दूरतः ॥
1.6.m: What is the use of speaking much here concerning the virtues of Vārāṇasī? / Even for those who utter the name of Kāśī, the four goals of life are not far off.

1.6.s:
gaṅgāyamunayoryogo 'dhikaḥ kāśyā api dvijā /
yasya darśanamātreṇa narā yānti parāṃ gatim //
1.6.d:
गङ्गायमुनयोर्योगो ऽधिकः काश्या अपि द्विजा ।
यस्य दर्शनमात्रेण नरा यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
1.6.m: The confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā is superior even to Kāśī, O twice-born; / merely by seeing it, men go to the supreme state.

1.6.s:
makarasthe ravau gaṅgā yatra kutrāvagāhitā /
punāti strānapānādyairnayantīndrapuraṃ jagat //
1.6.d:
मकरस्थे रवौ गङ्गा यत्र कुत्रावगाहिता ।
पुनाति स्त्रानपानाद्यैर्नयन्तीन्द्रपुरं जगत् ॥
1.6.m: When the sun is in Capricorn, the Gaṅgā, plunged into anywhere, / purifies through bathing, drinking, and the like, leading the world to Indra's city.

1.6.s:
yo gaṅgāṃ bhajate nityaṃ śaṅkaro lokaśaṅkaraḥ /
liṅgarupīṃ kathaṃ tasyā mahimā parikīrtyate //
1.6.d:
यो गङ्गां भजते नित्यं शङ्करो लोकशङ्करः ।
लिङ्गरुपीं कथं तस्या महिमा परिकीर्त्यते ॥
1.6.m: Śaṅkara, who brings peace to the world, ever worships the Gaṅgā / that has the form of the liṅga; how can her greatness be fully proclaimed?

1.6.s:
harirupadharaṃ liṅgaṃ liṅgarupadharo hariḥ /
īṣadapyantaraṃ nāsti bhedakṛccānayoḥ kudhīḥ //
1.6.d:
हरिरुपधरं लिङ्गं लिङ्गरुपधरो हरिः ।
ईषदप्यन्तरं नास्ति भेदकृच्चानयोः कुधीः ॥
1.6.m: The liṅga bears the form of Hari, and Hari bears the form of the liṅga; / there is not the slightest difference, and one who makes a distinction between these two is evil-minded.

1.6.s:
anādinidhane deve hariśaṅkarasaṃjñite /
ajñānasāgare magnā bhedaṃ kurvanti pāpinaḥ //
1.6.d:
अनादिनिधने देवे हरिशङ्करसंज्ञिते ।
अज्ञानसागरे मग्ना भेदं कुर्वन्ति पापिनः ॥
1.6.m: Between the two beginningless and endless gods designated Hari and Śaṅkara, / sinners, drowned in an ocean of ignorance, make a division.

1.6.s:
yo devo jagatāmaśaḥ kāraṇānāṃ ca kāraṇam /
yugānte nigadantyetadrudrarupadharo hariḥ //
1.6.d:
यो देवो जगतामशः कारणानां च कारणम् ।
युगान्ते निगदन्त्येतद्रुद्ररुपधरो हरिः ॥
1.6.m: The God who is the Lord of the worlds and the cause of all causes— / at the end of a yuga, it is proclaimed, this is Hari assuming the form of Rudra.

1.6.s:
rudro vai viṣṇurupeṇa pālayatyakhilañjagat /
brahmarupeṇa sṛjati prānteḥ hayetatrayaṃ haraḥ //
1.6.d:
रुद्रो वै विष्णुरुपेण पालयत्यखिलञ्जगत् ।
ब्रह्मरुपेण सृजति प्रान्तेः हयेतत्रयं हरः ॥
1.6.m: Indeed, Rudra protects the entire universe in the form of Viṣṇu; / he creates in the form of Brahmā, and at the end Hara destroys this triad.

1.6.s:
hariśaṅkarayormadhye brahmaṇaścāpi yo naraḥ /
bhedaṃ karoti so 'bhyeti narakaṃ bhṛśadāruṇam //
1.6.d:
हरिशङ्करयोर्मध्ये ब्रह्मणश्चापि यो नरः ।
भेदं करोति सो ऽभ्येति नरकं भृशदारुणम् ॥
1.6.m: A man who makes a distinction between Hari and Śaṅkara, / or even Brahmā, goes to a most terrible hell.

1.6.s:
haraṃ hariṃ vidhātāraṃ yaḥ paśyatyekarupiṇam /
sa yāti paraṃmānandaṃ śāstrāṇāmeṣa viṣvayaḥ //
1.6.d:
हरं हरिं विधातारं यः पश्यत्येकरुपिणम् ।
स याति परंमानन्दं शास्त्राणामेष विष्वयः ॥
1.6.m: He who sees Hara, Hari, and the Creator as possessing a single form / attains supreme bliss; this is the settled conclusion of the scriptures.

1.6.s:
yo 'sāvanādiḥ sarvajño jagatāmādikṛdvibhuḥ /
nityaṃ saṃnihitastatra liṅgarupī janārdanaḥ //
1.6.d:
यो ऽसावनादिः सर्वज्ञो जगतामादिकृद्विभुः ।
नित्यं संनिहितस्तत्र लिङ्गरुपी जनार्दनः ॥
1.6.m: He who is beginningless, omniscient, the all-pervading origin of the worlds— / Janārdana is ever-present there in the form of a liṅga.

1.6.s:
kāśīviśveśvaraṃ liṅgajyotirliṅgaṃ taducyate /
taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ jyotirāproti manujottamaḥ //
1.6.d:
काशीविश्वेश्वरं लिङ्गज्योतिर्लिङ्गं तदुच्यते ।
तं दृष्ट्वा परमं ज्योतिराप्रोति मनुजोत्तमः ॥
1.6.m: The Viśveśvara liṅga of Kāśī is called a Jyotirliṅga; / seeing it, the best of men attains the supreme light.

1.6.s:
kāśīpradakṣiṇā yena kṛtā trailokyapāvanī /
satpadvīpāsābdhiśailā bhūḥ parikramitāmunā //
1.6.d:
काशीप्रदक्षिणा येन कृता त्रैलोक्यपावनी ।
सत्पद्वीपासाब्धिशैला भूः परिक्रमितामुना ॥
1.6.m: By whom the circumambulation of Kāśī, purifier of the three worlds, is performed, / by him the earth with its seven continents, oceans, and mountains has been circumambulated.

1.6.s:
dhātumṛddārapāṣāṇalekhyādyā mūrtayo 'malāḥ /
śivasya vācyutasyāpi tāsu saṃnihito hariḥ //
1.6.d:
धातुमृद्दारपाषाणलेख्याद्या मूर्तयो ऽमलाः ।
शिवस्य वाच्युतस्यापि तासु संनिहितो हरिः ॥
1.6.m: Flawless images made of metal, clay, wood, stone, paintings, and the like, / whether of Śiva or Acyuta—in them Hari is ever present.

1.6.s:
tulasīkānanaṃ yatra yatra pahmavanaṃ dvijā /
purāṇapaṭhanaṃ yatra yatra saṃnihito hariḥ //
1.6.d:
तुलसीकाननं यत्र यत्र पह्मवनं द्विजा ।
पुराणपठनं यत्र यत्र संनिहितो हरिः ॥
1.6.m: Where there is a grove of tulasī, where there is a lotus garden, O twice-born, / where there is the recitation of a Purāṇa, there Hari is present.

1.6.s:
purāṇasaṃhitāvaktā harirityabhidhīyate /
tadbhaktiṃ kurvatāṃ nṝṇāṃ gaṅgāstrānāṃ dine dine //
1.6.d:
पुराणसंहितावक्ता हरिरित्यभिधीयते ।
तद्भक्तिं कुर्वतां नॄणां गङ्गास्त्रानां दिने दिने ॥
1.6.m: The expounder of a Purāṇa compendium is spoken of as Hari; / for men who show devotion to him, there is bathing in the Gaṅgā day after day.

1.6.s:
purāṇaśravaṇe bhaktirgaṅgāstrānasamā dvija /
tadvaktari ca yā bhaktiḥ sā prayāgopamā smṛtā //
1.6.d:
पुराणश्रवणे भक्तिर्गङ्गास्त्रानसमा द्विज ।
तद्वक्तरि च या भक्तिः सा प्रयागोपमा स्मृता ॥
1.6.m: Devotion in hearing a Purāṇa is equal to bathing in the Gaṅgā, O twice-born; / and the devotion shown toward its speaker is regarded as equal to Prayāga.

1.6.s:
purāṇadharmakathanairyaḥ samuddharate jagat /
saṃsārasāgare magnaṃ sa hariḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
1.6.d:
पुराणधर्मकथनैर्यः समुद्धरते जगत् ।
संसारसागरे मग्नं स हरिः परिकीर्तितः ॥
1.6.m: He who delivers the world sunk in the ocean of transmigratory existence / by recounting the teachings of the Purāṇas is proclaimed to be Hari.

1.6.s:
nāsti gaṅgāsamaṃ tīrthaṃ nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ /
nāsti viṣṇusamaṃ daivaṃ nāsti tattvaṃ guroḥ param //
1.6.d:
नास्ति गङ्गासमं तीर्थं नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः ।
नास्ति विष्णुसमं दैवं नास्ति तत्त्वं गुरोः परम् ॥
1.6.m: There is no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā; there is no elder equal to a mother; / there is no deity equal to Viṣṇu; there is no truth higher than a guru.

1.6.s:
varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śreṣṭhastārakāṇāṃ yathā śaśī /
yathā payodhiḥ sindhūnāṃ tathā gaṅgā parā smṛtā //
1.6.d:
वर्णानां ब्राह्मणः श्रेष्ठस्तारकाणां यथा शशी ।
यथा पयोधिः सिन्धूनां तथा गङ्गा परा स्मृता ॥
1.6.m: Just as the brāhmaṇa is the best of castes, and the moon among the stars, / and the ocean among rivers, so the Gaṅgā is remembered as supreme.

1.6.s:
nāsti śāntisamo bandhurnāsti satyātparaṃ tapaḥ /
nāsti mokṣātparo lābho nāsti gaṅgāsamā nadī //
1.6.d:
नास्ति शान्तिसमो बन्धुर्नास्ति सत्यात्परं तपः ।
नास्ति मोक्षात्परो लाभो नास्ति गङ्गासमा नदी ॥
1.6.m: There is no relative equal to peace; there is no austerity higher than truth; / there is no gain higher than liberation; there is no river equal to the Gaṅgā.

1.6.s:
gaṅgāyāḥ paramaṃ nāma pāpāraṇyadavānalaḥ /
bhavavyādhiharā gaṅgā tasmātsevyā prayantataḥ //
1.6.d:
गङ्गायाः परमं नाम पापारण्यदवानलः ।
भवव्याधिहरा गङ्गा तस्मात्सेव्या प्रयन्ततः ॥
1.6.m: The supreme name of the Gaṅgā is a forest fire to the forest of sins; / the Gaṅgā removes the malady of worldly existence; therefore, she should be served with effort.

1.6.s:
gāyatrī jāhnavī cobhe sarvapāpahare smṛte /
etayorbhaktihīno yastaṃ vidyātpatitaṃ dvija //
1.6.d:
गायत्री जाह्नवी चोभे सर्वपापहरे स्मृते ।
एतयोर्भक्तिहीनो यस्तं विद्यात्पतितं द्विज ॥
1.6.m: Both the Gāyatrī and the Jāhnavī are remembered as removers of all sins; / one who is devoid of devotion to these two should be known as fallen, O twice-born.

1.6.s:
gāyatrī chandasāṃ mātā mātā lokasya jāhnavī /
ubhe te sarvapāpānāṃ nāśakāraṇatāṃ gate //
1.6.d:
गायत्री छन्दसां माता माता लोकस्य जाह्नवी ।
उभे ते सर्वपापानां नाशकारणतां गते ॥
1.6.m: Gāyatrī is the mother of the meters, and Jāhnavī is the mother of the world; / both have become the cause of the destruction of all sins.

1.6.s:
yasya prasannā gāyatrī tasya gaṅgā prasīdati /
viṣṇuśaktiyute te dve samakāmaprasiddhede //
1.6.d:
यस्य प्रसन्ना गायत्री तस्य गङ्गा प्रसीदति ।
विष्णुशक्तियुते ते द्वे समकामप्रसिद्धेदे ॥
1.6.m: To him with whom Gāyatrī is pleased, the Gaṅgā is gracious; / those two, endowed with the power of Viṣṇu, grant the fulfillment of equal desires.

1.6.s:
dharmārthakāmarupāṇāṃ phalarupe nirañjane /
sarvalokānugrahārthaṃ pravartete mahottame //
1.6.d:
धर्मार्थकामरुपाणां फलरुपे निरञ्जने ।
सर्वलोकानुग्रहार्थं प्रवर्तेते महोत्तमे ॥
1.6.m: As the forms of the fruits of duty, wealth, and desire, taintless, / the two most excellent ones proceed for the sake of blessing all the worlds.

1.6.s:
atīva durllabhā nṝṇāṃ gāyatrī jāhnavī tathā /
tathaiva tulasībhaktirharibhaktiśca sāttvikī //
1.6.d:
अतीव दुर्ल्लभा नॄणां गायत्री जाह्नवी तथा ।
तथैव तुलसीभक्तिर्हरिभक्तिश्च सात्त्विकी ॥
1.6.m: Exceedingly difficult to attain for men are Gāyatrī and the Jāhnavī, / and likewise devotion to tulasī and pure devotion to Hari.

1.6.s:
aho gaṅgā mahābhāgā smṛtā pāpapraṇāśinī /
harilokapradā dṛṣṭā pītā sārupyadāyinī /
yatra strātā narā yānti viṣṇoḥ padamanuttamam //
1.6.d:
अहो गङ्गा महाभागा स्मृता पापप्रणाशिनी ।
हरिलोकप्रदा दृष्टा पीता सारुप्यदायिनी ।
यत्र स्त्राता नरा यान्ति विष्णोः पदमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.6.m: Ah, the most fortunate Gaṅgā, when remembered, destroys sins; / when seen, she grants the world of Hari; when drunk, she grants assimilation of form; / bathing in her, men go to the unsurpassed abode of Viṣṇu.

1.6.s:
nārāyaṇo jagaddhātā vāsudevaḥ sanātanaḥ /
gaṅgāstrānaparāṇāṃ tu vāñchitārthaphalapradaḥ //
1.6.d:
नारायणो जगद्धाता वासुदेवः सनातनः ।
गङ्गास्त्रानपराणां तु वाञ्छितार्थफलप्रदः ॥
1.6.m: Nārāyaṇa, the supporter of the world, eternal Vāsudeva, / grants the desired fruit to those devoted to bathing in the Gaṅgā.

1.6.s:
gaṅgājalakaraṇenāpi yaḥ sikto manujottamaḥ /
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prayāti paramaṃ padam //
1.6.d:
गङ्गाजलकरणेनापि यः सिक्तो मनुजोत्तमः ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः प्रयाति परमं पदम् ॥
1.6.m: The best of men who is sprinkled even with a drop of Gaṅgā water, / freed from all sins, departs to the supreme abode.

1.6.s:
yadvindusevanādeva sagarānvayasambhavaḥ /
visṛjyarākṣasaṃ bhāvaṃ saṃprātpaḥ paramaṃ padam //
iti śrīvṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde gaṅgāmāhātmyaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.6.d:
यद्विन्दुसेवनादेव सगरान्वयसम्भवः ।
विसृज्यराक्षसं भावं संप्रात्पः परमं पदम् ॥
इति श्रीवृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे गङ्गामाहात्म्यं नाम षष्टो ऽध्यायः
1.6.m:
By partaking of merely a drop of which, an offspring born in Sagara’s lineage, / casting off his demon nature, reached the supreme abode.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled ‘The Eulogy of the Greatness of the Gaṅgā,’ in the first quarter of the first part in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.7.s:
nārada uvāca
ko 'sau rākṣasabhāvāddhi mocitaḥ sagarāvanvaye /
sagaraḥ ko muniśreṣṭha tanmramākhyātumarhasi //
1.7.d:
नारद उवाच
को ऽसौ राक्षसभावाद्धि मोचितः सगरावन्वये ।
सगरः को मुनिश्रेष्ठ तन्म्रमाख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
1.7.m: Nārada said: / Who is he that was freed from the demon nature in Sagara's lineage? / Who was Sagara, O best of sages? You ought to tell that to me.

1.7.s:
sanaka uvāca
śruṇuṣva muniśārdūla gaṅgāmāhātmyamuttamam /
yajjalasparśamātreṇa pāvitaṃ sāgaraṃ kulam /
gataṃ viṣṇupadaṃ vipra sarvalokottamottamam //
1.7.d:
सनक उवाच
श्रुणुष्व मुनिशार्दूल गङ्गामाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ।
यज्जलस्पर्शमात्रेण पावितं सागरं कुलम् ।
गतं विष्णुपदं विप्र सर्वलोकोत्तमोत्तमम् ॥
1.7.m: Sanaka said: / Listen, O tiger among sages, to the supreme eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā, / by the mere touch of whose water Sagara’s family was purified / and went to the abode of Viṣṇu, best of all best worlds, O learned one.

1.7.s:
āsīdravikule bāhurnāma vṛkātmajaḥ /
bubhuje pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ dharmato dharmatatparaḥ //
1.7.d:
आसीद्रविकुले बाहुर्नाम वृकात्मजः ।
बुभुजे पृथिवीं सर्वां धर्मतो धर्मतत्परः ॥
1.7.m: In the solar dynasty there was a king named Bāhu, son of Vṛka; / devoted to righteousness, he ruled over the entire earth in accordance with duty.

1.7.s:
brahmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścānye ca jantavaḥ /
sthāpitāḥ svasvadharmeṣu tena bāhurviśāṃpatiḥ //
1.7.d:
ब्रह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राश्चान्ये च जन्तवः ।
स्थापिताः स्वस्वधर्मेषु तेन बाहुर्विशांपतिः ॥
1.7.m: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and other beings / were established in their respective duties by that Bāhu, lord of the people.

1.7.s:
aśvamedhairiyājāsau satpadvīpeṣu satpabhiḥ /
atarppayadbhūmidevān gobhūsvarṇāśukādibhiḥ //
1.7.d:
अश्वमेधैरियाजासौ सत्पद्वीपेषु सत्पभिः ।
अतर्प्पयद्भूमिदेवान् गोभूस्वर्णाशुकादिभिः ॥
1.7.m: He sacrificed with seven horse-sacrifices across the seven continents; / he pleased the earthly gods with cattle, lands, gold, garments, and other gifts.

1.7.s:
aśāsannītiśāstreṇa yatheṣṭaṃ paripanthinaḥ /
mene kṛtārthamātmānamanyātapanivāraṇam //
1.7.d:
अशासन्नीतिशास्त्रेण यथेष्टं परिपन्थिनः ।
मेने कृतार्थमात्मानमन्यातपनिवारणम् ॥
1.7.m: He punished his adversaries at will according to the science of statecraft; / he considered himself accomplished in averting the suffering of others.

1.7.s:
candanāni manojñāni baliṃ yatsarvadā janāḥ /
bhūṣitā bhūṣaṇaurdivyaistadrāṣṭre sukhino mune //
1.7.d:
चन्दनानि मनोज्ञानि बलिं यत्सर्वदा जनाः ।
भूषिता भूषणौर्दिव्यैस्तद्राष्ट्रे सुखिनो मुने ॥
1.7.m: Charming sandal pastes and food were ever offered by the people; / adorned with heavenly ornaments, they were happy in his kingdom, O sage.

1.7.s: akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī phalapuṣpasamanvitā //
1.7.d: अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी फलपुष्पसमन्विता ॥
1.7.m: The earth bore crops without plowing, abounding in fruits and flowers.

1.7.s:
vavarṣa bhūmau devendraḥ kāle kāle muniśvaraḥ /
ādharmaniratāpāye prajā dharmeṇa rakṣitāḥ //
1.7.d:
ववर्ष भूमौ देवेन्द्रः काले काले मुनिश्वरः ।
आधर्मनिरतापाये प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षिताः ॥
1.7.m: The lord of the gods rained upon the earth in proper season, O best of sages; / their unrighteous impulses averted, the subjects were protected with righteousness.

1.7.s:
ekadā tasya bhūpasya sarvasaṃpadvināśakṛt /
ahṝṅkāro mahāñjajñe sāsūyo lopahetukaḥ //
1.7.d:
एकदा तस्य भूपस्य सर्वसंपद्विनाशकृत् ।
अहॄङ्कारो महाञ्जज्ञे सासूयो लोपहेतुकः ॥
1.7.m: One day, a great pride that causes destruction of all fortune, / full of envy and the cause of ruin, arose in that king:

1.7.s:
ahaṃ rājā samastānāṃ lokānāṃ pālako balī /
karttā mahākratūnāṃ ca mattaḥ pūjyo 'sti ko 'paraḥ //
1.7.d:
अहं राजा समस्तानां लोकानां पालको बली ।
कर्त्ता महाक्रतूनां च मत्तः पूज्यो ऽस्ति को ऽपरः ॥
1.7.m: ‘I am the king, protector of all worlds, mighty, / and the performer of great sacrifices; who else is more worshipful than me?

1.7.s:
ahaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ śrīmāñjitāḥ sarve mayarayaḥ /
vedavedāṅgatattvajño nītiśāstra viśāradaḥ //
1.7.d:
अहं विचक्षणः श्रीमाञ्जिताः सर्वे मयरयः ।
वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञो नीतिशास्त्र विशारदः ॥
1.7.m: I am wise, prosperous, and all enemies have been conquered by me; / I know the essence of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, and am skilled in the science of statecraft.

1.7.s:
ajeyo 'vyāhataiśvaryo mattaḥ ko 'nyo 'dhiko bhuvi /
ahṝṅkāraparasyaivaṃ jātāsūyā pareṣvapi //
1.7.d:
अजेयो ऽव्याहतैश्वर्यो मत्तः को ऽन्यो ऽधिको भुवि ।
अहॄङ्कारपरस्यैवं जातासूया परेष्वपि ॥
1.7.m: Unconquerable, with unimpeded sovereignty—who else on earth is superior to me?’ / To him who was thus given over to egoism, envy toward others also arose.

1.7.s:
asūyāto 'bhavatkāmastasya rājño munīśvara /
eṣu sthiteṣu tu naro vināṣaṃ yatyasaṃśayam //
1.7.d:
असूयातो ऽभवत्कामस्तस्य राज्ञो मुनीश्वर ।
एषु स्थितेषु तु नरो विनाषं यत्यसंशयम् ॥
1.7.m: From envy, desire was born in that king, O lord of sages; / when these are present, a man goes to destruction without doubt.

1.7.s:
yauvanaṃ dhanasaṃpattiḥ prabhutvamavivekitā /
ekaikamapyanarthāya kimu yatra catuṣṭayam //
1.7.d:
यौवनं धनसंपत्तिः प्रभुत्वमविवेकिता ।
एकैकमप्यनर्थाय किमु यत्र चतुष्टयम् ॥
1.7.m: Youth, abundance of wealth, sovereignty, and lack of discernment— / each one of these leads to ruin; what then where all four exist together?

1.7.s:
tasyāsūyā nu mahatī jātā lokavirodhinī /
svadehanāśinī vigra sarvasaṃpadvināśinī //
1.7.d:
तस्यासूया नु महती जाता लोकविरोधिनी ।
स्वदेहनाशिनी विग्र सर्वसंपद्विनाशिनी ॥
1.7.m: Indeed, a great envy arose in him, opposing the world, / destroying his own person, O wise one, and destroying all fortune.

1.7.s:
asūyāviṣṭamanasi yadi saṃpatpravarttate /
tuṣāgniṃ vāyusaṃyogamiva jānīhi suvrata //
1.7.d:
असूयाविष्टमनसि यदि संपत्प्रवर्त्तते ।
तुषाग्निं वायुसंयोगमिव जानीहि सुव्रत ॥
1.7.m: If fortune appears in a mind overcome with envy, / know it to be like a fire in chaff joined with the wind, O you of noble vows.

1.7.s:
asūyopetamanasāṃ dambhācāravatāṃ tathā /
paruṣoktiratānāṃ ca sukhaṃ neha paratra ca //
1.7.d:
असूयोपेतमनसां दम्भाचारवतां तथा ।
परुषोक्तिरतानां च सुखं नेह परत्र च ॥
1.7.m: For those whose minds are possessed by envy, who practice deceitful conduct, / and who delight in harsh speech, there is no happiness here nor in the hereafter.

1.7.s:
asūyāviṣṭacittā nāṃ sadā niṣṭhurabhāṣiṇām /
priyāvā tanayā vāpi bāndhavā apyarātayaḥ //
1.7.d:
असूयाविष्टचित्ता नां सदा निष्ठुरभाषिणाम् ।
प्रियावा तनया वापि बान्धवा अप्यरातयः ॥
1.7.m: For those whose minds are overcome with envy and who always speak cruel words, / a beloved wife, a son, or even kinsmen become enemies.

1.7.s:
manobhilāṣaṃ kurute yaḥ samīkṣya parastriyam /
sa svasaṃpadvināśāya kuṭhāro nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.7.d:
मनोभिलाषं कुरुते यः समीक्ष्य परस्त्रियम् ।
स स्वसंपद्विनाशाय कुठारो नात्र संशयः ॥
1.7.m: He who conceives a mental desire upon looking at another’s wife / is an axe for the destruction of his own fortune; there is no doubt about this.

1.7.s:
yaḥ svaśreyovināśāya kuryādyatnaṃ naro mune /
sarveṣāṃ śreyasaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa kuryānmatsūraṃ kudhīḥ //
1.7.d:
यः स्वश्रेयोविनाशाय कुर्याद्यत्नं नरो मुने ।
सर्वेषां श्रेयसं दृष्ट्वा स कुर्यान्मत्सूरं कुधीः ॥
1.7.m: That man who strives for the destruction of his own welfare, O sage, / is evil-minded; seeing the welfare of all, he feels envy.

1.7.s:
mitrāpatyagṛhakṣetra dhanadhānyapaṣuṣvapi /
hānimicchannaraḥ kuryādasūyāṃ satataṃ dvija //
1.7.d:
मित्रापत्यगृहक्षेत्र धनधान्यपषुष्वपि ।
हानिमिच्छन्नरः कुर्यादसूयां सततं द्विज ॥
1.7.m: A man wishing ruin upon even his friends, children, home, field, / wealth, grain, and cattle, would constantly harbor envy, O twice-born.

1.7.s:
atha tasyāvinītasya hyasūyāviṣṭacetasaḥ /
haihayāstālalajaṅghāśca balino 'rātayo 'bhavan //
1.7.d:
अथ तस्याविनीतस्य ह्यसूयाविष्टचेतसः ।
हैहयास्ताललजङ्घाश्च बलिनो ऽरातयो ऽभवन् ॥
1.7.m: Now, of that ill-behaved one whose mind was seized by envy, / the Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghas became powerful enemies.

1.7.s:
yasyānukūlo lakṣmīśaḥ saubhāgyaṃ tasya varddhate /
sa eva vimukho yasya saubhāgyaṃ tasya hīyate //
1.7.d:
यस्यानुकूलो लक्ष्मीशः सौभाग्यं तस्य वर्द्धते ।
स एव विमुखो यस्य सौभाग्यं तस्य हीयते ॥
1.7.m:
To whom the Lord of Lakṣmī is favorable, his fortune increases;
he to whom He turns away, his fortune wanes.

1.7.s:
tāvatputrāśca pautrāśca dhanadhānyagṛhādayaḥ /
yāvadīkṣeta lakṣmīśaḥ kṛpāpāṅgena nārada //
1.7.d:
तावत्पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च धनधान्यगृहादयः ।
यावदीक्षेत लक्ष्मीशः कृपापाङ्गेन नारद ॥
1.7.m:
Sons, grandsons, wealth, grain, houses, and the like remain only as long
as the Lord of Lakṣmī gazes with a compassionate glance, O Nārada.

1.7.s:
api mūrkhāndhabadhirajaḍāḥ śūrā vivekinaḥ /
ślādhyā bhavanti viprendra prekṣitā mādhavena ye //
1.7.d:
अपि मूर्खान्धबधिरजडाः शूरा विवेकिनः ।
श्लाध्या भवन्ति विप्रेन्द्र प्रेक्षिता माधवेन ये ॥
1.7.m:
Even the foolish, the blind, the deaf, and the dull become brave, discerning,
and praiseworthy, O best of Brahmins, when looked upon by Mādhava.

1.7.s:
saubhāgyaṃ tasya hīyeta yasyāsūyādilāñchanam /
jāyate nātra saṃdeho jantudveṣo viśeṣataḥ //
1.7.d:
सौभाग्यं तस्य हीयेत यस्यासूयादिलाञ्छनम् ।
जायते नात्र संदेहो जन्तुद्वेषो विशेषतः ॥
1.7.m:
The good fortune of that person wanes who bears the taint of envy and the like;
there is no doubt about this, especially when there is malice toward living beings.

1.7.s:
satataṃ yasya kasyāpi yo dveṣaṃ kurute naraḥ /
tasya sarvāṇi naśyanti śreyāṃsi munisatam //
1.7.d:
सततं यस्य कस्यापि यो द्वेषं कुरुते नरः ।
तस्य सर्वाणि नश्यन्ति श्रेयांसि मुनिसतम् ॥
1.7.m:
Whatever person constantly bears malice toward any being,
all his blessings perish, O best of sages.

1.7.s:
asūyā varddhate yasya tasya viṣṇuḥ parāṅmukhaḥ /
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ mahī saṃpanadviśyati tato dhruvam //
1.7.d:
असूया वर्द्धते यस्य तस्य विष्णुः पराङ्मुखः ।
धनं धान्यं मही संपनद्विश्यति ततो ध्रुवम् ॥
1.7.m:
He whose envy increases has Viṣṇu turn his face away from him;
wealth, grain, land, and prosperity surely perish thereafter.

1.7.s:
vivekaṃ hantyahṝṅkārastvavivekāttu jīvinām /
āpadaḥ saṃbhavantyevetyahṝṅkāraṃ tyajettataḥ //
1.7.d:
विवेकं हन्त्यहॄङ्कारस्त्वविवेकात्तु जीविनाम् ।
आपदः संभवन्त्येवेत्यहॄङ्कारं त्यजेत्ततः ॥
1.7.m:
Egotism destroys discernment, and from a lack of discernment indeed
misfortunes certainly arise for living beings; therefore, one should renounce egotism.

1.7.s:
ahaṃ kāro bhavedyasya tasya nāśo 'tivegataḥ /
asūyāvisṛṣṭamanasastasya rājñaḥ paraiḥ saha //
1.7.d:
अहं कारो भवेद्यस्य तस्य नाशो ऽतिवेगतः ।
असूयाविसृष्टमनसस्तस्य राज्ञः परैः सह ॥
1.7.m:
He who possesses egotism meets destruction very swiftly.
For that king whose mind was given over to envy, with enemies—

1.7.s:
āyodhanamabhīddhoraṃ māsamekaṃ nirantaram /
haihayaistālajaṅghaiśca ripubhiḥ sa parājitaḥ //
1.7.d:
आयोधनमभीद्धोरं मासमेकं निरन्तरम् ।
हैहयैस्तालजङ्घैश्च रिपुभिः स पराजितः ॥
1.7.m:
A fierce battle took place continuously for a single month;
and by his enemies, the Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghas, he was defeated.

1.7.s:
sa tu bāhustato duḥkhī antarvatnyā svabhāryayā /
avāpa paramāṃ tuṣṭiṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā mahatsaraḥ //
1.7.d:
स तु बाहुस्ततो दुःखी अन्तर्वत्न्या स्वभार्यया ।
अवाप परमां तुष्टिं तत्र दृष्ट्वा महत्सरः ॥
1.7.m:
Then, distressed, that Bāhu with his pregnant wife
obtained supreme joy upon seeing a large lake there.

1.7.s:
asūyopetamanasastasya bhāvaṃ nirīkṣya ca /
sarogatavihaṅgāste līnāścitramidaṃ mahat //
1.7.d:
असूयोपेतमनसस्तस्य भावं निरीक्ष्य च ।
सरोगतविहङ्गास्ते लीनाश्चित्रमिदं महत् ॥
1.7.m:
And perceiving the demeanor of him whose mind was possessed of envy,
those birds on the lake hid themselves—this was a great wonder.

1.7.s:
aho kaṣṭamaho rupaṃ ghoramatra samāgatam /
viśantastvarayā vāsamityūcuste vihaṅgamāḥ //
1.7.d:
अहो कष्टमहो रुपं घोरमत्र समागतम् ।
विशन्तस्त्वरया वासमित्यूचुस्ते विहङ्गमाः ॥
1.7.m:
“Oh, the misery! Oh, a dreadful form has arrived here!”
Saying thus, the birds entered their dwellings in haste.

1.7.s:
so 'vagāhyasarobhūpaḥ patnībhyāṃ sahito mutā /
pītvā jalaṃ ca sukhadaṃ vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ //
1.7.d:
सो ऽवगाह्यसरोभूपः पत्नीभ्यां सहितो मुता ।
पीत्वा जलं च सुखदं वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः ॥
1.7.m:
Having plunged into the lake with his two wives, the king, pleased,
drank the comforting water and rested at the root of a tree.

1.7.s:
tasminbāhau vanaṃ yāte tenaiva parirakṣitāḥ /
durguṇānvigaṇayyāsyadhigdhigityabruvanprajāḥ //
1.7.d:
तस्मिन्बाहौ वनं याते तेनैव परिरक्षिताः ।
दुर्गुणान्विगणय्यास्यधिग्धिगित्यब्रुवन्प्रजाः ॥
1.7.m:
When that Bāhu went to the forest, the subjects protected by him,
recounting his vices, cried out: “Shame, shame!”

1.7.s:
yo vā ko vā guṇī martyaḥ sarvaśvādhyatarodvijaḥ /
sarvasaṃpatsamāyukto 'pyaguṇīnindito janaiḥ //
1.7.d:
यो वा को वा गुणी मर्त्यः सर्वश्वाध्यतरोद्विजः ।
सर्वसंपत्समायुक्तो ऽप्यगुणीनिन्दितो जनैः ॥
1.7.m:
Whatever mortal has virtues, or a Brahmin who is most commendable of all,
even endowed with all prosperities, if devoid of virtues, is reviled by people.

1.7.s:
apakīrtisamo mṛtyurlokeṣvanyo na vidyate /
yadā bāhurvanaṃ yātastadā tadrāgagā janāḥ /
saṃtuṣṭiṃ paramāṃ yātā davathau vigate yathā //
1.7.d:
अपकीर्तिसमो मृत्युर्लोकेष्वन्यो न विद्यते ।
यदा बाहुर्वनं यातस्तदा तद्रागगा जनाः ।
संतुष्टिं परमां याता दवथौ विगते यथा ॥
1.7.m:
No other death equal to ill-repute is known in the worlds.
When Bāhu went to the forest, the people attached to him
attained supreme satisfaction, as though a burning fever had passed.

1.7.s:
nindāto bahuśo bāhurmṛtavatkānanesthitaḥ /
nihatya karma ca yaśo loke dvajavarottama //
1.7.d:
निन्दातो बहुशो बाहुर्मृतवत्काननेस्थितः ।
निहत्य कर्म च यशो लोके द्वजवरोत्तम ॥
1.7.m:
Reproached repeatedly, Bāhu stayed in the forest like a dead man,
having destroyed his deeds and renown in the world, O best of Brahmins.

1.7.s:
nāstyakīrtisamo mṛtyurmāsti krodhasamo ripuḥ /
nāsti nindāsamaṃ pāpaṃ nāsti mohasamāsavaḥ //
1.7.d:
नास्त्यकीर्तिसमो मृत्युर्मास्ति क्रोधसमो रिपुः ।
नास्ति निन्दासमं पापं नास्ति मोहसमासवः ॥
1.7.m:
There is no death equal to infamy; there is no enemy equal to anger;
there is no sin equal to censure; there is no intoxicating liquor equal to delusion.

1.7.s:
nāstyasūyāsamā kīrtirnāsti kāmasamo 'nalaḥ /
nāsti rāgasamaḥ pāśo nāsti saṅgasamaṃ viṣam //
1.7.d:
नास्त्यसूयासमा कीर्तिर्नास्ति कामसमो ऽनलः ।
नास्ति रागसमः पाशो नास्ति सङ्गसमं विषम् ॥
1.7.m:
There is no ill-fame equal to envy; there is no fire equal to desire;
there is no snare equal to attachment; there is no poison equal to clinging.

1.7.s:
evaṃ vilapyabahudhā bāhuratyantaduḥkhitaḥ /
jīrṇāṅgomanasastāpād vṛddhabhāvādabhūdasau //
1.7.d:
एवं विलप्यबहुधा बाहुरत्यन्तदुःखितः ।
जीर्णाङ्गोमनसस्तापाद् वृद्धभावादभूदसौ ॥
1.7.m:
Lamenting thus in many ways, Bāhu, exceedingly distressed,
his body withered from mental anguish and old age, declined.

1.7.s:
gate bahutithe kāle aurvāśramasamīpataḥ /
sa bāhurvyādhinā graste mamāra munisattama //
1.7.d:
गते बहुतिथे काले और्वाश्रमसमीपतः ।
स बाहुर्व्याधिना ग्रस्ते ममार मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.7.m:
After much time had passed near the hermitage of Aurva,
that Bāhu, seized by disease, died, O best of sages.

1.7.s:
tasya bhāryā ca duḥkhārtā kaniṣṭhā garbhiṇī tadā /
ciraṃ vilapya bahudhā sahagantuṃ mano dadhe //
1.7.d:
तस्य भार्या च दुःखार्ता कनिष्ठा गर्भिणी तदा ।
चिरं विलप्य बहुधा सहगन्तुं मनो दधे ॥
1.7.m:
Then his younger wife, afflicted with grief and pregnant,
lamenting long in many ways, set her mind on going with him [in death].

1.7.s:
samānīya casaidhāṃsi citāṃ kṛtvātiduḥkhitā /
samāropya tanpūruḍhaṃ svayaṃ samupacakrame //
1.7.d:
समानीय चसैधांसि चितां कृत्वातिदुःखिता ।
समारोप्य तन्पूरुढं स्वयं समुपचक्रमे ॥
1.7.m:
Having gathered firewood and prepared a pyre, exceedingly grieving,
having placed the dead body [upon it], she herself began to mount it.

1.7.s:
etasminnantare dhīmanaurvastejonidhirmuniḥ /
etadvijñātavānsarvaṃ parameṇa samādhinā //
1.7.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे धीमनौर्वस्तेजोनिधिर्मुनिः ।
एतद्विज्ञातवान्सर्वं परमेण समाधिना ॥
1.7.m:
In the meantime, O wise one, the sage Aurva, a treasure of fiery energy,
perceived all this through supreme absorption.

1.7.s:
bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ varttamānaṃ trikālajñāmunīśvarāḥ /
gatāsūyā mahātnānaḥ paśyantijñāna cakṣuṣā //
1.7.d:
भूतं भव्यं वर्त्तमानं त्रिकालज्ञामुनीश्वराः ।
गतासूया महात्नानः पश्यन्तिज्ञान चक्षुषा ॥
1.7.m:
Past, future, and present, knowing the three times, the lords of sages,
freed from envy, great-souled ones, see through the eye of knowledge.

1.7.s:
tapobhistejasāṃ rāśiraurvapuṇyasamo muniḥ /
saṃprātpastatra sādhvī ca yatra bāhupriyā sthitā //
1.7.d:
तपोभिस्तेजसां राशिरौर्वपुण्यसमो मुनिः ।
संप्रात्पस्तत्र साध्वी च यत्र बाहुप्रिया स्थिता ॥
1.7.m:
A mass of splendor through austerities, the sage Aurva, equal to accumulated merit,
arrived there, virtuous, where the beloved wife of Bāhu stood.

1.7.s:
citāmāroḍhumudyuktāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā munisattamaḥ /
provāca dharmamūlāni vākyāni munisattamaḥ //
1.7.d:
चितामारोढुमुद्युक्तां तां दृष्ट्वा मुनिसत्तमः ।
प्रोवाच धर्ममूलानि वाक्यानि मुनिसत्तमः ॥
1.7.m:
Seeing her about to ascend the pyre, that best of sages
spoke words rooted in righteousness, O best of sages:

1.7.s:
aurva uvāca
rājavaryapriye sādhvi mā kuruṣvātisāhasam /
tavodare cakravartī śanuhantā hi tiṣṭati //
bālāpatyāśca garbhiṇyo hyadṛṣṭaṛtavastathā /
1.7.d:
और्व उवाच
राजवर्यप्रिये साध्वि मा कुरुष्वातिसाहसम् ।
तवोदरे चक्रवर्ती शनुहन्ता हि तिष्टति ॥
बालापत्याश्च गर्भिण्यो ह्यदृष्टऋतवस्तथा ।
1.7.m:
Aurva said:
“O virtuous lady, beloved of the best of kings, do not commit such rashness!
For within your womb abides a universal monarch, a slayer of foes.

Women with young children, pregnant women, and those whose courses have not appeared,

1.7.s: rajasvalā rājasutenārohati cintāśubho //
1.7.d: रजस्वला राजसुतेनारोहति चिन्ताशुभो ॥
1.7.m: Or menstruating women, O princess, do not mount the inauspicious pyre.

1.7.s:
brahmahatyādipāpānāṃ proktā niṣkṛtiruttamaiḥ /
dāmbhinonindakasyāpi bhrūṇaghrasya na niṣkṛtiḥ //
1.7.d:
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानां प्रोक्ता निष्कृतिरुत्तमैः ।
दाम्भिनोनिन्दकस्यापि भ्रूणघ्रस्य न निष्कृतिः ॥
1.7.m:
Expiation for sins like the slaughter of a Brahmin has been declared by the noble,
[but] for the deceitful, the censurer, and the slayer of an embryo, there is no expiation.

1.7.s:
nāstikasya kṛtanghasya dharmopekṣākarasya ca /
viśvāsaghātakasyāpi niṣkṛtirnāsti suvrate //
1.7.d:
नास्तिकस्य कृतन्घस्य धर्मोपेक्षाकरस्य च ।
विश्वासघातकस्यापि निष्कृतिर्नास्ति सुव्रते ॥
1.7.m:
For an atheist, an ungrateful person, one who neglects righteousness,
and a betrayer of trust, there is no expiation, O lady of good vows.

1.7.s:
tasmādetanmahatpāpaṃ karttuṃ nārhasi śobhane /
yadetadduḥkhamutpannaṃ tatsarvaṃ śāntimeṣyati //
1.7.d:
तस्मादेतन्महत्पापं कर्त्तुं नार्हसि शोभने ।
यदेतद्दुःखमुत्पन्नं तत्सर्वं शान्तिमेष्यति ॥
1.7.m:
Therefore, O fair one, you ought not to commit this great sin;
all this sorrow that has arisen will come to an end.”

1.7.s:
ityuktā muninā sādhvī viśvasya tadanugraham /
vilalāpātiduḥkhārtā samuhyadhavapatkujau //
1.7.d:
इत्युक्ता मुनिना साध्वी विश्वस्य तदनुग्रहम् ।
विललापातिदुःखार्ता समुह्यधवपत्कुजौ ॥
1.7.m:
Addressed thus by the sage, the virtuous woman, trusting his grace,
lamented, tormented by extreme sorrow, and fainting, fell to the ground.

1.7.s:
aurvo 'pi tāṃ punaḥ prāha sarvaśāstrārthakoviduḥ /
mārodīrāja nanaye śriyamagrye gamiṣyasi //
1.7.d:
